{{Recipe}}

'''Bubur ketan hitam''' is a dish of black glutinous rice pudding with coconut milk.

==Ingredients==
===Porridge===
* 250 [[Cookbook:Gram|grams]] black glutinous [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
* 1 ½ [[Cookbook:Liter|litres]] water
* 2 [[Cookbook:Pandan|pandan]] leaves
* 250 grams coconut sugar or [[Cookbook:Palm Sugar|palm sugar]], microwaved for couple minutes to dissolve easily
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

===Coconut milk sauce=== 
* 350 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] thick [[Cookbook:Coconut Milk|coconut milk]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] salt
* 2 pandan leaves

==Procedure==
===Porridge=== 
# Soak black glutinous rice in water overnight.
# Drain the rice. Cook with water and pandan leaves until soft and thick.
# Add coconut sugar and salt, and continue cooking until the sugar is dissolved and the water is absorbed.

===Coconut milk sauce===
# Cook thick coconut milk with salt and pandan for a few minutes.
# Serve the black rice pudding in a bowl, and pour coconut milk sauce on top.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Additional toppings might be added, such as sliced baked [[Cookbook:Banana|banana]], brown sugar powder, or [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] powder.

This '''ginger banana cake''' is made with [[Cookbook:Buckwheat|buckwheat]] flour, making it [[Cookbook:Gluten-Free|gluten-free]]. [http://www.foodista.com/recipe/C5VCLZHX/ginger-banana-cake-with-chocolate Originally posted to Foodista] by Anne Pedersen. Foodista recipes are released under a [http://www.foodista.com/static/legal CC-BY license].

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (135 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Buckwheat|buckwheat]] flour 
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]]
*¼ cup (60 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]/70 g) [[Cookbook:Maple Syrup|maple syrup]]
*¼ cup (60 ml/65 g) unsweetened [[Cookbook:Applesauce|applesauce]]
*Juice of ½ [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] (8 g) grated fresh [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]] 
*3 very ripe [[Cookbook:Banana|bananas]] (should have dark spots on the peel)
*¼ cup (30 g) roughly-chopped dark [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate]] or chocolate chips

==Preparation==
#Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 170°C (338°F).
#Mix the buckwheat flour, baking powder and baking soda in a bowl, and set aside.
#Mix the maple syrup with the applesauce, the lemon juice, and the grated ginger. Mash the bananas using the back of a fork before mixing them with the other wet ingredients.
#Combine the dry ingredients with the banana mixture. Be careful not to overmix—you don’t want to beat out all of the air.
#Once everything is well-mixed, add the dark chocolate and gently mix again.
#Line a cake pan (20 x 20 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]/ 8 x 8 [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]]) with [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment paper]] and pour the batter into it.
#Place in the oven and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] for about 45 minutes or until a [[Cookbook:Skewer|toothpick]] inserted in the center comes out clean.

{{recipe}}

'''''Bua loi''''' is a traditional Thai rice flour dessert. It is often prepared for religious or ritual ceremonies, but it can also be eaten as an everyday dish. Bua loi are often brightly colored with various ingredients (see notes).

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] sweet glutinous [[Cookbook:Rice Flour|rice flour]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Steaming|steamed]] and mashed [[Cookbook:Taro Root|taro]] root
* ¼ cup water
* [[Cookbook:Coconut Milk|Coconut milk]]

== Procedure ==
# Combine rice flour, mashed taro, and water to make a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# Shape the dough into small balls, using additional rice flour to prevent sticking.
# Bring a large pot of water to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. Add the dough balls to the boiling water. They will initially sink but will gradually float to the surface as they cook.
# Remove the cooked bua loi from the pot, and drain the water.
# Transfer the bua loi to a dish, and serve with coconut milk. This dish is best served hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If you want to make your bua loi more colorful, you can add [[Cookbook:Pumpkin|pumpkin]] (yellow) or [[Cookbook:Pandan|pandan]] (green).

'''Brown butter toffee chocolate chip cookies''' are flavorful [[Cookbook:Cookie|cookies]], and it takes 48 hours for the dough to develop the flavors. This recipe is adapted from the YouTube channel Tasty.<ref>https://google.miraheze.org/wiki/YouTube_Wiki:2-Minute_Vs._2-Hour_Vs._2-Day_Cookie_%E2%80%A2_Tasty</ref>

== Ingredients ==
=== Toffee ===

* ¾ stick (90 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 3 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (140 g / 5 oz) lightly packed light [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] kosher [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* Water, as needed

=== Cookie dough ===

* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (2 sticks / 250 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 9 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) unsalted butter
* 4 ice cubes
* ¾ cup (160 g / 5.5 oz) white [[Cookbook:Granulated Sugar|granulated sugar]]
* 1½ cups (270 g / 9.5 oz) packed light brown sugar
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] [[Cookbook:Coffee|espresso powder]]
* 2 teaspoons kosher salt

(Galette de blé noir) | Category = Pancake recipes | Yield = 12 pancakes | Servings = | Difficulty = 2 | Image = [[File:Galette de sarrasin complète bretonne.jpg|300px]] }} {{recipe}} '''Buckwheat crêpes''' are a type of savory crêpe from Upper Brittany made with [[Cookbook:Buckwheat|buckwheat]] flour. They are locally known as "'''galettes de blé noir'''" or "'''galettes de sarrasin'''" and are traditionally eaten on Fridays. Nowadays, these are cooked at home, served in crêperies, and can be a typical takeaway dish. In all cases, they are served stuffed with fillings like ham, egg, cheese, sausage, etc. == Ingredients == * 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Buckwheat|buckwheat]] flour * 1 [[Cookbook:Liter|L]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]] * 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] * 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]] (optional; see note) * [[Cookbook:Butter|Butter]] for cooking * Fillings as desired == Procedure == === Batter === # [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] together the flour and salt in a [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|mixing bowl]]. # Whisk in the egg and half the water to make a [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]]. # Cover the batter with a cloth, and let it rest for 1 hour at room temperature. # Gradually whisk in the remaining water as needed to get the correct consistency. It needs to be thin enough to flow and coat the pan, but not so watery that the pancake will not bind during cooking. You may not need to add all the water. === Cooking === # Prepare your desired fillings in advance. Anything that requires more than 1 minute to cook (e.g. onions, mushrooms, meat, etc.) should be pre-cooked. # Heat a large flat [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] (about 30 cm in diameter) over medium heat. # When the pan is hot, grease it with a dab of butter (start with about a [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]]), and spread so it melts and coats the pan. The batter may set quickly, so you may need to adjust the volume of butter used for the first few pancakes. # Ladle enough batter into the pan so that you get a large pancake no more than 3 mm thick after spreading it out. # Let the pancake cook until it is dry on the top surface and lightly golden on the bottom. Use a spatula to flip it to the other side. # If you will not be filling the pancake immediately, cook until golden on the other side, then remove and set aside (see notes). If you will be filling the pancake, arrange the ingredients in the center, leaving several centimeters/inches bare all around the filling. Once cooked on the bottom, fold four edges of the pancake into the center to enclose the filling and make a square. Remove and serve hot. # Continue cooking until the rest of the batter is used up. == Notes, tips, and variations == * There is a debate on whether you should include egg in the batter. It seems to act as a stabilizer depending on the quality of the flour used. * If you fully fold the ''galette'' (see image), you can flip it one more time after filling without the risk of the filling escaping. This gives you a little extra time to heat or cook the filling if needed.[[File:Galette_de_Haute_Bretagne.jpg|thumb|Fully folded ''galette'']] * If you choose to pre-cook or buy the pancakes before filling, you should warm them in a pan before filling. To do so, simply butter a skillet over medium heat, place the pancake flat in the pan, and fill/fold as described above. Make sure everything gets well-heated. {{Recipe}}

'''Bunny chow''' is a South African street food consisting of a hollowed-out loaf of [[Cookbook:bread|bread]] filled with [[Cookbook:curry|curry]]. Originating in Durban, it is commonly prepared with mutton, [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], [[Cookbook:beef|beef]], or bean curry. The dish is popular throughout South Africa and is valued for its portability and rich flavor. Served with carrot salad, chutney, or pickled vegetables for additional flavor, the dish is best enjoyed while the bread is fresh and the curry is hot.

==Ingredients==

===Curry===
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]]
* 1 large [[Cookbook:onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 cloves [[Cookbook:garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] grated fresh [[Cookbook:ginger|ginger]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tomatoes with Cheese Stuffing|tomatoes]], chopped
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Curry Powder|curry powder]]
* 1 tsp ground [[Cookbook:turmeric|turmeric]]
* 1 tsp ground [[Cookbook:paprika|paprika]]
* 500 g (1 lb) [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]], [[Cookbook:mutton|mutton]], [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], or mixed [[Cookbook:vegetables|vegetables]], cut in pieces
* 2 medium [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], [[Cookbook:Cube|cubed]]
* 2 cups water or [[Cookbook:Broth and Stock|stock]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
* [[Cookbook:Black pepper|Black pepper]], to taste

===Serving===
* 1 large, unsliced loaf of white [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]]
* [[Cookbook:Cilantro|Fresh coriander]] (optional)

==Procedure==

# Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
# Add the onion and cook until softened.
# Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
# Add the curry powder, turmeric, and paprika. Stir until fragrant.
# Add the meat or vegetables and cook until lightly browned.
# Add the tomatoes and cook until softened.
# Add the potatoes and water, and season with a little salt and pepper.
# [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] for 30–40 minutes, or until the meat and potatoes are tender and the sauce has thickened. Adjust the seasoning as necessary.
# Cut the loaf of bread into halves or quarters, and remove part of the soft interior from each piece to create a cavity.
# Fill the bread cavity generously with hot curry.
# Garnish with coriander if desired and serve immediately.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* The curry may be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Assemble the bunny chow shortly before serving to prevent the bread from becoming soggy.

In some countries, such as the United States, bulk [[Cookbook:sausage|sausage]] is sold in supermarkets. This is sausage with no casing that breaks up during cooking as easily as any other ground meat. But in other countries, bulk sausage is not sold as such, so if you want to follow a recipe that calls for bulk sausage, you need to make it yourself. Here's how to make a sausage that is reminiscent of the bulk sausage sold in the United States, similar to [[w:Jimmy Dean (brand)|Jimmy Dean]] Regular.

==Ingredients==
* 2 [[Cookbook:teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
* 2 tsp dried [[Cookbook:sage|sage]]
* 2 tsp [[Cookbook:salt|salt]]
* 1 tsp ground [[Cookbook:black pepper|black pepper]]
* ½ tsp [[Cookbook:garlic powder|garlic powder]]
* ½ tsp dried [[Cookbook:thyme|thyme]]
* ½ tsp ground [[Cookbook:paprika|paprika]]
* ½ tsp ground [[Cookbook:clove|cloves]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:kilogram|kg]] raw ground [[Cookbook:pork|pork]]

==Procedure==
# Combine all ingredients except the pork together in a large cup or small bowl.
# [[Cookbook:Knead|Knead]] the seasoning mixture into the raw ground pork until it is distributed evenly.
# Use in any recipe calling for bulk sausage.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
The spices and their proportions are not set in stone. Any spice can be increased, decreased, or omitted according to your taste. To make the sausage spicier, add ½ tsp powdered [[Cookbook:cayenne pepper|cayenne pepper]] and/or hot [[Cookbook:chili powder|chili powder]]. The ground pork can be replaced with ground [[Cookbook:turkey|turkey]] if you prefer.

The '''Caesar salad''' is a traditional [[Cookbook:Salad|salad]] served in American restaurants, often prepared table-side. It is referred to by some as the "king" of salads. 

Its origin is largely credited to Italian immigrant Caesar Cardini, a restaurateur and chef in Tijuana, Baja California del Norte, Mexico. Cardini reportedly tossed the first such salad table side at his restaurant on July 4, 1924.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 head Romaine [[Cookbook:Lettuce|lettuce]], roughly [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]<ref group="N">Contrary to popular belief, chopping the lettuce will '''''not''''' cause the edges to brown. If we were using a more delicate leaf, say radicchio, then we would tear it, but we're using Romaine, which isn't that delicate.</ref>
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (about 50 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) extra-virgin [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]], divided
* Heavy [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of sea salt
* Freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]
* Drizzle of red wine [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]
* 3 shots [[Cookbook:Worcestershire Sauce|Worcestershire sauce]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Soft Boiled Eggs|soft-boiled eggs]]
* [[Cookbook:Garlic Croutons|Garlic croûtons]]

== Procedure==
#Drizzle lettuce with 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil. [[Cookbook:Mixing#Tossing|Toss]] to coat.
#Add salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
#Add vinegar and toss to coat.
#Drizzle Worcestershire sauce over lettuce. Toss to coat.
#Crack eggs over salad. Toss to coat.
#Top with garlic croûtons and serve.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Fish|Fish]]

'''Gentgeen's Campfire Trout''' is the recipe [[User:Gentgeen|Gentgeen]] uses to cook trout caught while camping. This method can be used at home with trout purchased at the fish market, but somehow never tastes quite as good.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 whole cleaned [[Cookbook:Trout|trout]], between 10 and 14 [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]]
* 4 strips [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* [[Cookbook:Lemon|Lemon]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]] to taste

== Procedure ==
# Make a pan out of [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|aluminium foil]] slightly larger than your two fish. The pan should have a double layer of foil on the bottom and a lip around the edge of about ¾–1 inch height.
# Place the pan on a [[Cookbook:Grill|grill]] over the campfire. Put the butter into the pan, and allow it to begin melting. Wrap each trout with 2 strips of bacon. Add the trout to the pan and season to taste.
# After the trout has cooked for a few minutes (5–7 depending on the size of the fish), check the inside. If the side close to the fire is white and flakes easily, the fish is ready to turn. Flip the fish, and continue cooking the other side for 3–4 minutes until done.
# Serve with lemon over a bed of white [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]].

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Vietnam|Vietnamese Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Sandwiches|Sandwiches]]

'''''{{lang|vi|Bánh mì}}''''' means 'bread' in [[Vietnamese]], and it often refers to a type of Vietnamese [[Cookbook:Sandwiches|sandwich]]. It may have started as a 'kitchen sink' recipe in [[w:Vietnam|Vietnam]], where various leftovers would be tossed into a [[Cookbook:Sandwiches|sandwich]] to finish them up (like a [[Cookbook:Po' Boy|po' boy]]). {{lang|vi|Bánh mì}} is now sought after by many for its unique and delicious flavours.  There are many different types of ''bánh mì'' sandwiches, ranging from chunked BBQ grilled [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]], sliced pork pâté, and shredded grilled [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], to grilled and smoked [[Cookbook:Seafood|fish]], sardine, meatball, Chinese-style [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausage]], and tripe.

Choices of bread are also quite varied. It is customary to use a toasted French [[Cookbook:Baguette|baguette]] or French bread, because of the textures these breads provide: Bánh mì tastes best when the outer crust of the bread is firm but not overly hard, and the inner part of the bread is fluffy and light like a yeast roll, that is, one which is not overly dense or spongy. The reason for this is that the crust's firmness provides a barrier for the moisture of the sandwich, and the lightness of the inner bread does not overwhelm the flavors of the sandwich, which would otherwise make the sandwich taste overly 'bready'. Still, no sandwich tastes better than the flavor of the bread, so make sure the bread is fresh and flavorful (preferably one from a bakery). Using a store-bought bread yields unpredictable results as they tend to taste overly processed or they taste like the plastic or paper bag in which they are kept. 

== Ingredients ==
Many different ingredients may be used to make bánh mì. Put in as many as you wish in your sandwich—each is different.

=== Core ingredients ===

* 1 loaf baguette-style [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]]
* [[Cookbook:Julienne|Julienned]] [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]]
* Julienned [[Cookbook:Daikon|daikon]] radish
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* Water
* Coconut [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]] or white vinegar
* [[Cookbook:Sugar|Sugar]]

=== Standard bánh mì fillings ===
* [[Cookbook:Cilantro|Cilantro (coriander)]] leaves and stems
* Super-thin [[Cookbook:Jalapeño|jalapeño]] [[Cookbook:Slicing|slices]]
* Fresh sliced [[Cookbook:Cucumber|cucumber]]

=== Protein fillings ===
* BBQ [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]]
* BBQ [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]]
* Sliced pork pâté
* Sliced pork meatloaf
* Sliced [[Cookbook:Ham|ham]]
* BBQ [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]]
* [[Cookbook:Meatballs|Meatballs]]
* Sliced Chinese/Thai/Vietnamese-style [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausage]] (waxy kind)
* [[Cookbook:Sardine|Sardines]]
* [[Cookbook:Tripe|Tripe]]
* [[Cookbook:Smoked Salmon|Smoked salmon]]
* Grilled or [[Cookbook:Frying|fried]] whitefish
* [[cookbook:Textured Vegetable Protein|Textured vegetable protein]] (wheat gluten, [[Cookbook:seitan|seitan]], sueyu, suegai - vegetarian fish fillets)
* Seasoned [[cookbook:tofu|tofu]]

=== Optional additional fillings ===
* Sliced [[Cookbook:Turnip|turnip]]
* Sliced [[Cookbook:Green Onion|green onion]]s
* Sliced, patted dry [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
* Sprigs of [[Cookbook:Mint|mint]]
* Sprigs of [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]]
* Shredded [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]]
* [[Cookbook:Sprout|Sprout]] mix
* [[Cookbook:Lettuce|Lettuce]]

=== Sauces for sandwich ===
* [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Japan|Japanese]] [[Cookbook:Mayonnaise|mayonnaise]] (Kewpie Mayo - squeeze bottle with a baby on front)
* Mayso ([[Cookbook:Mayonnaise|mayo]] and [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]])
* Maysocha (mayo, soy sauce, and [[Cookbook:Sriracha|sriracha]] chili sauce)
* Maycha (mayo and sriracha)
* Hot Mom (mayo, Lao Gan Ma Chinese hot sauce)
* Any of the above with [[Cookbook:Lime|lime]] or [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] juice and [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* [[Cookbook:Barbecue Sauce|BBQ sauce]] and mayo

== Procedure ==

=== Pickling the vegetables ===

# Lightly sprinkle the julienned carrot and radish with salt. Let rest 5 min, then rinse with cold water.
# Mix equal parts of water, vinegar with sugar. Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], cool, and pour over vegetables.
# Store this mixture in a container in the refrigerator for at least a day before using.

=== Sandwich assembly ===

# [[Cookbook:Slicing|Slice]] a length of baguette lengthwise. Form a trench in each half by either removing the excess bread or compressing it. These depressions are where you will put the filling.
# Toast the bread if desired.
# Spread a layer of desired sauce(s) on each half of the bread.
# Fill the sandwich with any of the desired fillings listed above.
# Serve.

| time = 3–6 days
| difficulty = 3
| Image = [[Image:Gimchi.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Korea|Korean Cuisine]]

'''Kimchi''' (김치), also spelled '''kimchee''' or '''gimchi''', is a Korean dish of pickled [[Cookbook:Vegetable|vegetables]], usually [[Cookbook:cabbage|napa cabbage]] or Korean radish and is commonly served as a [[Cookbook:Side dishes|side dish]]. It is usually fermented in a brine of [[Cookbook:Anchovy|anchovy]] sauce, [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]], [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Green onion|green onion]], and [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|chilli pepper]]. There are countless varieties—at least as many as there are households. The following is a standard recipe for ''baechoo kimchi'' (napa-cabbage kimchi), a common variety and often the first kind of kimchi that jumps to mind for non-Koreans. 

==Ingredients==
*1 head [[Cookbook:Cabbage|napa cabbage]] (baechu, Chinese cabbage, wombok)
*½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] sea salt (or any coarse salt)
*1 cup [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Tbsp|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tsp|tsp]] minced [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Gochugaru|gochugaru]] (Korean chile flakes)
*2 tsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*¼ cup [[Cookbook:Fish Sauce|aekjeot]] (Korean fish sauce)
*½ [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], thinly [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
*¼ [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], thinly [[Cookbook:Julienne|julienned]]
*¼ Korean [[Cookbook:Radish|radish]] (muwoo), thinly julienned
*4 [[Cookbook:Green onion|green onions]], cut into 3-cm pieces

==Procedure==
#Quarter the napa cabbage, wash, and drain.
#Combine coarse sea salt and water.
#Put cabbages in salted water and take out one at a time to get salt down.
#Add cabbages to a container. Pour salted water over top, and set aside for at least 6–8 hours (overnight is great). The cabbage should be soft enough to bend.
#Wash cabbages and drain well.
#Combine gochugaru, salt, sugar, jeot gal (Korean fish sauce), minced garlic, and minced ginger.
#Mix the onion, carrot, radish, and green onion into the chilli powder mixture.
#Take one cabbage, and stuff the above mixture between every layer.
#Try to fold the cabbage in half. With 2 outer leaves, wrap the whole thing securely.
#Put cabbages in an airtight container, and let it sit at room temperature overnight.
#Refrigerate for 2–3 days at minimum. After a few days, you will notice some liquid. This is totally normal and a sign that the kimchi is ripening. 
#Enjoy your kimchi!
==Notes, tips, and variations==
*Korean radishes are large (about ½ to 1 kilogram). Japanese (daikon) radishes or a larger quantity of small European radishes could substitute.
*The brine can be varied to include many other ingredients. Be creative.
*The aekjeot can be replaced with moderate amounts of saeujeot (Korean salted tiny shrimp), raw butterfish, or raw oysters. Seafood can also be left out entirely, although an appropriate amount of salt needs to be added in place of missing jeot gal. Alternative flavors can include Asian pears or tangerines.

{{recipe}}

'''Sarmi''' is a [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Bulgaria|Bulgarian]] dish of stuffed [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]] leaves, which shows significant [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Greece|Greek]] influences. For a gathering you may wish to consider presenting these somewhat 'white' rolls side-by-side with a dish of cabbage rolls in tomato sauce (see [[Cookbook:Cabbage Rolls in Tomato Sauce (Holubtsi)|Cabbage Rolls in Tomato Sauce (Holubtsi)]]).

==Ingredients==
*500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (about 1 ⅛ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) minced (ground) [[Cookbook:Veal|veal]] or [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]]
*300 g (about ¾ lb) minced (ground) [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]]
*1 bunch of [[Cookbook:Spring Onion|spring onions]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] uncooked [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
*1 cup [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yogurt]]
*[[Cookbook:Parsley|Parsley]]
*[[Cookbook:Mint|Mint]]
*[[Cookbook:Paprika|Paprika]] (optional)
*[[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
*30–40 [[Cookbook:Grape|grape]] or [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]] leaves (depending on the size, a substantially smaller number of leaves may be needed)
*100 g [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or ½ cup [[Cookbook:Sunflower Oil|sunflower oil]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]

==Procedure==
#[[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] the vine or cabbage leaves in salted water until they look cooked and are just bendable enough to roll. Drain and allow to cool during the following steps.
#Lightly [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] the finely chopped onions in a small amount of oil, and stir in a teaspoon or more of paprika. 
#Add the meat, rice, pepper, mint, and finely chopped parsley, then cook until the meat looks almost done.
#Add ¾ cup of water, bring to a boil, then immediately cover and reduce heat to a bare minimum for 10 minutes, until the water is absorbed by the rice. Uncover and fluff as needed with a small spatula or spoon. Allow to cool to handling temperature.
#Put 1 teaspoon of the meat mixture on each leaf and make into a rolled, fully enclosed, package, similar to a small egg roll. A bit more filling can be used if you are using large cabbage leaves, but try to make all the rolls somewhat uniform in size.
#Arrange the rolls in a saucepan, add 1½ cups of warm water, cover, and simmer gently over low heat.
#In the meantime, mix the yogurt with a bit of paprika for color (or omit if you wish to keep the dish somewhat white in color), and other spices as you desire.
#When rolls are done, allow to cool a bit, gently transfer to a dish, and add the yogurt mixture to coat. 
#Serve with vegetables of your choice. Enjoy!

This dish is an attempt to replicate the flavor of curry chicken dishes that are served at Indian restaurants in California.

==Ingredients==

===Meat and vegetables===
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[cookbook:Oil|cooking oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] yellow [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]] [[cookbook:garlic|garlic]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] boneless [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] meat, cut into cubes
* 6 small [[cookbook:potato|potatoes]], peeled, quartered, and cooked (boiled, baked, or steamed)

===Spices===
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] mild [[Cookbook:Curry Powder|curry powder]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile]] powder
* 1 tbsp [[cookbook:Paprika|paprika]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] ground [[cookbook:Cumin|cumin]]
* 1 tsp [[cookbook:Garlic Powder|garlic powder]]
* 2 tsp [[cookbook:Cardamom|cardamom]] powder
* 1 tsp [[cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]] powder
* 1 tsp [[cookbook:mustard|mustard]] powder
* ¼ tsp ground [[cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaf]]

===Sauce===
*1 ½ cups (12 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Coconut Milk|coconut milk]]
*3 cups [[cookbook:water|water]]
*1 cup [[cookbook:yogurt|yogurt]]
*1 can (12 oz) diced [[cookbook:tomato|tomatoes]], with liquid
*4 tbsp [[cookbook:Butter|butter]]

===Thickener===
*¼–½ cup of instant mashed potato flakes

*[[cookbook:salt|Salt]] to taste
*[[cookbook:pepper|Pepper]] to taste

==Procedure==
#Heat cooking oil in a 4-quart [[cookbook:stockpot|stockpot]].
#Add onions and garlic. [[cookbook:Fry|Fry]] for about 1 minute.
#Add chicken. [[Cookbook:Stir-frying|Stir-fry]] for about 5 minutes.
#Add cooked potatoes.
#Add all the spices, and stir to coat chicken and potatoes. Cook for about 5 minutes more.
#Add sauce ingredients, stir well, bring to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]], and cook for 10 minutes.
#Add ¼ cup of mashed potato flakes, and stir until curry is thickened. If a thicker curry is desired, add additional potato flakes a tablespoon at a time until desired thickness is achieved.
#Add salt and pepper to taste.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*Serve with [[Cookbook:Steaming|steamed]] [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]].

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Southern cuisine|Southern cuisine (USA)]] | [[Cookbook:Fried Chicken|Fried Chicken]] 

'''Fried chicken''' is a Southern main meal in the [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|USA]], served often at "Sunday dinner" ("dinner" being the midday meal for many Southerners) or church "suppers" ("supper" being the term for the evening meal). Recipes are legion; every family has one handed down. 

== Ingredients ==

=== Chicken ===
*1 whole [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Buttermilk|buttermilk]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard powder]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Cayenne pepper|cayenne powder]]
*2 tsp cracked [[Cookbook:Pepper|black peppercorns]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]]
*1 tablespoon [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]]
*[[Cookbook:Flour|Flour]] seasoned with herbs and spices (e.g. pepper, cayenne, salt, ground coriander, cinnamon, thyme, oregano)
*Oil (e.g. peanut or corn oil)

=== Gravy ===
* [[Cookbook:Oil|Oil]]
* 1 small [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]] (or [[Cookbook:Green onion|shallots]]), [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Garlic|clove of garlic]]
* 3–4 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 3 cups [[Cookbook:Stock|chicken stock]] (or 2 cups stock + 1 cup [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]])
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]

== Procedure ==

=== Chicken ===
# Cut the chicken into 8–10 pieces.
# Combine the buttermilk and spices, and [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinate]] the chicken pieces for 4 hours in the mixture.
# Take each chicken piece out of the marinade and allow it to drip dry for a few seconds. Then, dredge it in seasoned flour. An easy way to dredge involves putting flour and seasonings in a small plastic bag, dropping the piece in, and shaking.
# Let the pieces rest (separately; do not stack) for about 10 minutes. Then dredge them again. The first dredging absorbs the buttermilk marinade. The second dredging gives a seasoned flour outer coat.
# Heat the oil in a deep, wide pan. When oil is smoking hot, drop chicken pieces into the pan, and be careful to not overcrowd (pieces should not touch; fry in multiple batches). After 3 or 4 minutes, turn the chicken, and reduce the heat. Let the chicken fry for 20–25 minutes, turning the pieces every few minutes. When the chicken is a deep golden-brown, and the juices run clear, it's done. The chicken will continue to cook after being removed from the pan, so err on the side of "just about done".
# Drain the chicken on [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|absorbent paper]] or cloth. If you are not serving the chicken immediately, place it in a lightly-warmed [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]], uncovered, separately (not stacked).

===Gravy===
# Pour off the accumulated oil from the pan, reserving 3–4 tablespoons and all the flour and chicken residue. Keeping the pan on medium flame, add the chopped onion and garlic. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] for a few minutes. Whisk in 3–4 tablespoons of flour, and keep stirring until the mixture becomes light to medium brown. Do not burn.
# [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] in 3 cups of chicken stock. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] over low heat, covered, for 15 minutes. Salt and pepper to taste.
# Serve chicken with [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] and some green vegetables. Spoon gravy over rice and chicken.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* The spice mix isn't fixed. You can use more or less as desired.

ingredients.sourceText: Flour seasoned with herbs and spices (e.g. pepper, cayenne, salt, ground coriander, cinnamon, thyme, oregano)
ingredients.amountText: Flour seasoned with herbs and spices (e.g. pepper, cayenne, salt, ground coriander, cinnamon, thyme, oregano)

ingredients.name: 3 cups chicken stock (or 2 cups stock + 1 cup cream)
ingredients.sourceText: 3 cups chicken stock (or 2 cups stock + 1 cup cream)
ingredients.amountText: 3 cups chicken stock (or 2 cups stock + 1 cup cream)

steps.text: Cut the chicken into 8–10 pieces.
steps.sourceText: Cut the chicken into 8–10 pieces.

steps.text: Combine the buttermilk and spices, and marinate the chicken pieces for 4 hours in the mixture.
steps.sourceText: Combine the buttermilk and spices, and marinate the chicken pieces for 4 hours in the mixture.

steps.text: Take each chicken piece out of the marinade and allow it to drip dry for a few seconds. Then, dredge it in seasoned flour. An easy way to dredge involves putting flour and seasonings in a small plastic bag, dropping the piece in, and shaking.
steps.sourceText: Take each chicken piece out of the marinade and allow it to drip dry for a few seconds. Then, dredge it in seasoned flour. An easy way to dredge involves putting flour and seasonings in a small plastic bag, dropping the piece in, and shaking.

steps.text: Let the pieces rest (separately; do not stack) for about 10 minutes. Then dredge them again. The first dredging absorbs the buttermilk marinade. The second dredging gives a seasoned flour outer coat.
steps.sourceText: Let the pieces rest (separately; do not stack) for about 10 minutes. Then dredge them again. The first dredging absorbs the buttermilk marinade. The second dredging gives a seasoned flour outer coat.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a deep, wide pan. When oil is smoking hot, drop chicken pieces into the pan, and be careful to not overcrowd (pieces should not touch; fry in multiple batches). After 3 or 4 minutes, turn the chicken, and reduce the heat. Let the chicken fry for 20–25 minutes, turning the pieces every few minutes. When the chicken is a deep golden-brown, and the juices run clear, it's done. The chicken will continue to cook after being removed from the pan, so err on the side of "just about done".
steps.sourceText: Heat the oil in a deep, wide pan. When oil is smoking hot, drop chicken pieces into the pan, and be careful to not overcrowd (pieces should not touch; fry in multiple batches). After 3 or 4 minutes, turn the chicken, and reduce the heat. Let the chicken fry for 20–25 minutes, turning the pieces every few minutes. When the chicken is a deep golden-brown, and the juices run clear, it's done. The chicken will continue to cook after being removed from the pan, so err on the side of "just about done".

steps.text: Drain the chicken on absorbent paper or cloth. If you are not serving the chicken immediately, place it in a lightly-warmed oven, uncovered, separately (not stacked).
steps.sourceText: Drain the chicken on absorbent paper or cloth. If you are not serving the chicken immediately, place it in a lightly-warmed oven, uncovered, separately (not stacked).

steps.text: Pour off the accumulated oil from the pan, reserving 3–4 tablespoons and all the flour and chicken residue. Keeping the pan on medium flame, add the chopped onion and garlic. Sauté for a few minutes. Whisk in 3–4 tablespoons of flour, and keep stirring until the mixture becomes light to medium brown. Do not burn.
steps.sourceText: Pour off the accumulated oil from the pan, reserving 3–4 tablespoons and all the flour and chicken residue. Keeping the pan on medium flame, add the chopped onion and garlic. Sauté for a few minutes. Whisk in 3–4 tablespoons of flour, and keep stirring until the mixture becomes light to medium brown. Do not burn.

steps.text: Whisk in 3 cups of chicken stock. Simmer over low heat, covered, for 15 minutes. Salt and pepper to taste.
steps.sourceText: Whisk in 3 cups of chicken stock. Simmer over low heat, covered, for 15 minutes. Salt and pepper to taste.

steps.text: Serve chicken with rice and some green vegetables. Spoon gravy over rice and chicken.

These '''cake brownies''' are somewhat less dense and almost [[Cookbook:Cake|cake]]-like compared to ready-made mixtures one would buy from a store.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (6 ¾ [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] / 2.4 [[Cookbook:Deciliter|dl]]) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* ½ cup (4 ¼ oz / 120 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) melted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Cocoa|cocoa]]
* ¾ cup (6 ¼oz / 180 g / 1.8 dl) [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ½ tsp [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]]
* ½ cup (4 ¼ oz / 120 g / 1.2 dl) [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Walnut|walnuts]] or other nuts (optional)

== Procedure ==
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9 x 9 [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] (23 x 23 cm) square [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|cake pan]].
# [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] eggs until light in a medium-sized bowl.
# Add sugar, melted butter, and cocoa. Mix well.
# Add flour, salt, baking powder, vanilla, and nuts. Mix well with a rubber spatula.
# Pour into prepared pan. Bake for 20 minutes at 350 °F/175 °C (Gas Mark 4).
# Cool.

Serve as a soup or accompanied with rice and boiled ground provisions.

==Ingredients==
*12 [[Cookbook:Taro Root|taro]] (dasheen or callaloo) leaves 
*¼ [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] [[cookbook:Beef|salted beef]] or [[cookbook:Pork|salted pork]] (optional)

{{recipe}}| [[Cookbook:Desserts|Desserts]]

'''Bête Noire''' is a rich flourless chocolate cake. 

Similar recipes include [[Cookbook:Chocolate Orbit Cake|Chocolate Orbit Cake]] and [[Cookbook:Flourless Chocolate Cake|Flourless Chocolate Cake]]. 

==Ingredients==
*½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[cookbook:water|water]]
*1 ⅓ cup white granulated [[cookbook:sugar|sugar]]
*4 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (120 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[cookbook:Bittersweet chocolate|bittersweet chocolate]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*8 oz (230 g) [[cookbook:Unsweetened chocolate|unsweetened chocolate]], finely chopped
*½ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (225 g) [[cookbook:butter|butter]]
*5 beaten [[cookbook:egg|egg]]s

==Procedure==
# Heat the water and sugar together until fully dissolved.
# Melt butter in a large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] over a low heat.
# Add the chopped chocolate to the melted butter, and [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] until smooth.
# Whisk in the sugar syrup and allow to cool slightly.
# Add the eggs and whisk until well blended.
# Pour the mixture into a greased and [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment]]-lined 9-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] (23 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]])[[Cookbook:Springform Pan| springform pan]].  
# Wrap the bottom and sides of the springform in aluminum foil so that no water can seep to the cake while it is cooking in the water bath.
# Cook in a [[Cookbook:Bain-marie|bain-marie]] at 350°F (180°C) in an [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] for 25–30 minutes.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Venezuela|Cuisine of Venezuela]]

'''Cachapas''' are traditionally made with fresh corn, and are a summer favorite, but this easy recipe uses canned cream corn, pancake mix, and whatever cheese you have on hand. Try this simple appetizer for a taste of Venezuela whenever you like. 

== Ingredients ==
* 1 can (14 fl [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] / 398 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) creamed corn 
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Pancake Mix|pancake mix]]
* ¼ cup [[cookbook:flour|flour]]
* 1 [[cookbook:egg|egg]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] melted [[cookbook:butter|butter]] or [[cookbook:margarine|margarine]]
* 2 tablespoons [[cookbook:sugar|sugar]], or to taste
* [[cookbook:cheese|Cheese]] of your choice

== Procedure ==
# Blend all the ingredients together in a [[cookbook:blender|blender]]. The mix should become thick and heavy. If not, add more corn. 
# Shape the mix into small pancakes approximately ½ [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] (1.5 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]) thick and about 5 inches (13 cm) in diameter. Let them cook on medium heat for about 1 minute on each side, or until small bubbles form on the top.
# Cachapas should be served hot and may be accompanied with cheese (feta cheese is one option, Mexican white cheese "Cotija", Venezuelan or Colombian "Queso Blanco" ,"Queso de Mano" or "Queso Guayanes" where available).

This recipe was inspired by the Wikipedia article on Alfredo.

==Ingredients==
* Dry linguine or [[Cookbook:Spaghetti|Spaghetti]] (enough for 2 people)
* 1 vegetarian [[Cookbook:Bouillon Cube|bouillon cube]]
* 1–2 pat(s) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]

# Fill pot with enough water for 2 servings of linguine.

{{recipe}}

==Ingredients==
* 12 [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]] leaves
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] chopped [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (about 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) ground [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]]
* ¾ cup cooked [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]

=== Sauce ===
* 1 can [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* 1 can chopped [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
* ½ cup water
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]
* 3 Tbsp [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 2 Tbsp [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|cornstarch]] mixed with ½ cup cold water

==Procedure==
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 350°F (175°C).
# Put cabbage into pot of boiling water, cover, let sit for three minutes, then drain.
# Combine ground beef, milk, egg, rice, onion, pepper, and salt. Divide into twelve portions.
# Place 1 meat portion on each cabbage leaf.
# Roll leaf around filling and fasten with [[Cookbook:Toothpick|toothpick]].
# Place the rolls in a [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|baking dish]].
# Combine tomato paste, tomatoes, sugar, water, and vinegar, then pour over cabbage rolls.
# Cover baking dish, and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] at 350°F (175C) for 40 minutes.
# Remove cabbage rolls from pan, and take out toothpicks. Place on the serving dish
# Add cornstarch and water to sauce mixture and stir together. Warm, if needed, to allow the cornstarch mixture to thicken the sauce.
# Pour the completed sauce over the rolls on the serving dish.
# Garnish as desired and serve.

Literally "coffee with milk", '''café au lait''' is a drink made of coffee and scalded milk in a ratio of 1:1. It is the staple coffee drink of French Louisiana and is often served in bowls in [[Cookbook:Cajun cuisine|Acadiana]]. 

==Ingredients==
* 4 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] brewed [[Cookbook:Coffee|coffee]] or 1.5–2 cups (350–475 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) cold [[cookbook:Coffee concentrate|coffee concentrate]]
* 4 cups (950 ml) [[cookbook:milk|milk]]
==Procedure==
# If you are using coffee concentrate, add enough hot water to make 4 cups of coffee.
# At the same time, heat the milk over a low to medium heat until scalded. 
# Pour equal amounts of coffee and scalded milk into bowls or cups. 

==Notes, tips, and variations== 
* Steamed milk can be substituted for scalded milk. 
* The milk can be heated in the cups by half filling each cup with milk and [[Cookbook:Microwaving|microwaving]] briefly. A 1,000W microwave oven will heat one half-cup of milk in 50 seconds, two in 60 seconds.

{{recipesummary
| category = Chickpea recipes
| servings = 2–3
| time = 3–10 hours
| difficulty = 2
}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Gibraltar|Cuisine of Gibraltar]]

'''Calentita''' is the quintessential 'Yanito' dish. Every Gibraltarian knows how to cook calentita! Or so they should, as it is a matter of national pride.

It is believed this dish is based on the Genoese '[[Cookbook:Socca|farinata]]' which is cooked thinner and often with toppings whereas calentita is cooked in a deeper pan and is never topped with anything but black pepper.

The name 'calentita' has a most interesting history. When Gibraltarian evacuees returned to Gibraltar after World War II many were forced to live in cramped and often inadequate housing. Not all homes had workable ovens and people cooked mainly Spanish-style stews (potajes) and similar dishes. However, the local bakeries took advantage of this and would use their ovens in slack periods to make calentita which was sold by street vendors (this had been the fashion before the war when almost no-one had an oven at home). The calentita would be baked in a large low pan (similar to a frying pan of diameter about 90 cm with two small grab handles) with a metal hinged lid. The vendor would then walk along the streets on the Rock shouting out his wares. His shout would be similar to this: 'La llevo caliente, calentita! Calentita, caliente!' A simple translation would be: 'Hot! Come and get it! I still have it hot!'. Caliente means hot and calentita is an endearing version of hot! Everyone would rush to him and buy a portion which was invariably about 8cm by 5cm and cost 6d (about 2 1/2p  of today's money) and was served on a piece of greaseproof paper. The vendor would sprinkle ground pepper on it and off you went!

# Remove a significant fraction of liquid from pan, add drained beans, and add back just enough liquid to cover beans. Simmer beans until they just begin to break up and the liquid starts to become creamy, about 45 minutes. Stir frequently. Add back liquid as needed to keep beans covered. If beans begin to scorch, do not stir; transfer mixture to another pan without scraping scorched beans into new pot.
# Add ham hocks and cook 45 minutes more, and serve immediately.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Vietnam|Cuisine of Vietnam]]

'''''Canh chua''''' is the Vietnamese "Hot & Sour" soup. It is closest to the Thai and the Cambodian tom yum soup, although it is more sweet and sour than its spicier counterparts. Each family has its own ''canh chua'' recipe and sometimes, members from the same family have their own. 
==Ingredients==

=== Marinade ===
* 1 whole [[Cookbook:Catfish|catfish]] or other firm white [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Scallion|scallions]], green part reserved for garnish and white part crushed
* 4 teaspoons nước mắm
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook: Salt|salt]]
* Freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]

===Soup===
* 1 [[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] (950 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) water
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Fish Sauce|nước mắm]]
* ½ cup (120g) sour bamboo
* ¼ fresh [[Cookbook:Pineapple|pineapple]], core removed, cut lengthwise and sliced

===Garnish===
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Cilantro|fresh coriander]]
* Green part of scallions, chopped

==Procedure==

# Marinate the fish for 15 minutes with the crushed scallions, black pepper, salt, and nước mắm.
# Bring water to the boil. Add the sour bamboo and pineapple slices. Boil for 5 minutes.
# Add marinated fish and continue to boil for a total of 10 minutes. While the fish is boiling, add Nước mắm, and salt.
# For serving, the soup can be garnished with coriander and the green part of scallions.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Traditionally, the fish head is not removed, but you can if you prefer.

{{recipesummary|category=Pizza recipes|servings=4 or 5|time=45 minutes|difficulty=2|Image=[[Image:20000227--calzone.jpg|300px]]}}
'''Calzone''' is a popular Italian form of pizza. The word means ''sock'' because the resulting pizza looks similar to a sock.

==Ingredients==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Ricotta|ricotta cheese]]
* 1 cup (240 ml) shredded [[Cookbook:Mozzarella Cheese|mozzarella cheese]]
* 4 ounces (115 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) any topping (such as [[Cookbook:Ham|ham]], [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]], [[Cookbook:Salami|salami]], [[Cookbook:Pepperoni|pepperoni]], and/or [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausage]]) (optional)
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] (10 ml) [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]]
* 1 package store-bought pizza dough

==Procedure==

# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|400°F]] (200°C).
# Combine ricotta, mozzarella, toppings, and oregano.
# Roll the pizza dough between 2 pieces of waxed paper.
# Spoon the cheese mixture into the center of the dough.
# Moisten edges of dough slightly. Fold the dough over, and seal edges by pressing with a fork.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] until golden brown, about 10 or 12 minutes.
# Serve with [[Cookbook:Marinara Sauce|marinara sauce]].

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Turkey|Cuisine of Turkey]]

'''Börek''' is a general term in Turkish cuisine that applies to a family of [[Cookbook:Pastry|pastries]] with about fifty different members.  They have in common the fact that they are all pastry layers of some type enclosing a filling. There are two basic methods; one consists of rolling out very thin sheets of dough, called [[w:en:yufka|yufka]] in Turkish and [[w:en:phyllo|phyllo]] in Greek. The other main type of börek, called ''[[w:en:nemse börek|nemse börek]]'' in Turkish, uses a dough very similar to ''[[Cookbook:Puff pastry|pâte feuilletée]]'', in which the dough is layered with butter, folded, and rolled out several times.<ref>Algar, Ayla Esen (1985) ''The Complete Book of Turkish Cooking'' {{#isbn:0-710-30334-3}}</ref>

The following recipe describes the procedure required to prepare triangle-shaped börek from commercially produced phyllo. Links to recipes for fillings are listed at the end of the recipe.

==Ingredients==

=== Fillings ===
*[[Cookbook:Cheese Filling for Peynirli Börek|Peynirli börek]] (white cheese filling)
*Kıymalı börek (minced meat filling)
*Tavuklu börek (chicken filling)
*Ispanaklı börek (spinach filling)

=== Assembly ===
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] prepared filling (see above)
* 1 box yufka/[[Cookbook:Phyllo Dough|phyllo]] pastry sheets<ref>Available from Turkish, Greek, Armenian and Middle-Eastern grocers, among others, as well as some supermarkets.</ref>
* Melted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or high-quality [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]<ref>e.g. peanut, hazelnut, walnut, almond, grapeseed. Avoid anything with a greasy taste such as corn oil.</ref>
[[Image:Wrapping börek.jpg|thumbnail|right|250px|Assembling börek triangles]]
==Procedure==
#Remove the phyllo sheets from the container. Unfold carefully so as not to break them. Lay them flat and cover with a clean, damp tea towel to prevent them from drying out—this is important.
# Working quickly, cut the phyllo into lengthwise thirds (step 1 in the diagram). Lay one of these out and cover the other two with the damp tea towel.
# Brush the strip of phyllo with the melted butter. Place a heaped [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoonful]] of filling on one end of the strip (step 2 in the diagram).
#Fold the right lower corner upward over the filling to form a triangle (step 3 in the diagram).
#Now fold the right upper corner over to the left (step 4 in the diagram).
#Continue folding in this manner until you reach the end of the strip.
#Trim of any excess dough and seal the edges by rubbing a damp finger over the dough and pressing the edge of the triangle where the strip ends.
#[[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] in oil at 340°F until golden brown or [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] at 350°F for 15 minutes.<ref>Prewrapped, uncooked börek freezes well. To cook, bake at 325ºF for 30 minutes.  Do not deep-fry frozen foods.  Splattering oil can cause burns and fires.  You may sautée them in a covered pan 2 or 3 at a time.  Hold the cover in front of your face as you place each börek in the pan.</ref>

==Notes==

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Sauces|Sauces]]

'''Béarnaise sauce''' is an egg-yolk and butter emulsion in the [[Cookbook:Hollandaise|Hollandaise]] family of sauces. 

== Ingredients ==
* 30 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]]) tarragon [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]
* 30 ml (2 tablespoons) [[Cookbook:Sherry|sherry]] [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]] or dry white [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallot]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Egg yolk|egg yolks]]
* 75–100 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (⅓–½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] / 3–4 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) melted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] (warm but not hot)
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Cayenne pepper|Cayenne pepper]] to taste
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] freshly-chopped [[Cookbook:Tarragon|tarragon]]
* 1 tablespoon freshly-chopped [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]

== Procedure ==

# Put the vinegars, shallot, and herbs in a small [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]; [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] until reduced to 1 tablespoon. This is the flavorful glaze. Strain and set aside to cool.
# Add the egg yolks and [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] until the ribbon stage with a balloon whisk.
# Place the bowl over a pan of hot water (a [[Cookbook:Double Boiler|double boiler]]) and continue whisking. Gradually add the melted butter, whisking until the sauce thickens and all the butter has been added.
# Season and serve.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Do not use dried tarragon; if you cannot find fresh tarragon, use a sprig from the vinegar bottle.
* To find the right temperature to [[Cookbook:Emulsification|emulsify]] the egg mixture and the butter, the bowl should be just hot enough so that you can still touch it. If you cannot hold the bowl it is too hot. Be forewarned that this trick may not always work depending on a multitude of conditions.

==References==
* Julia Child (1961), ''Mastering the Art of French Cooking'', Alfred A. Knopf

'''Buñuelos''' are a type of Latin-American fried [[Cookbook:Pastry|pastry]].

==Ingredients==
*5 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
*¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:White Sugar|white sugar]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
*2 cups [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
*1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
*1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*1 cup white sugar 
*1 teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
*1 cup vegetable oil for frying

==Procedure==
#In a large bowl combine eggs with ¼ cup sugar, and [[Cookbook:Beating|beat]] until thick and lemon-colored. Add the oil. 
#Combine 1 ½ cups of the flour, the baking powder, and the salt. Gradually add this to the egg mixture and beat well.
#Turn dough out onto a floured board (use remaining ½ cup flour) and [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] thoroughly until dough is smooth. 
#Shape dough into 16 balls. [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll]] each one into a circle about 5 [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]] (13 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]) in diameter. Let stand uncovered on waxed paper for about 10 minutes. 
#Heat oil in a deep [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] to 350°F (175°C). [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] dough circles until golden brown, turning once. Drain on [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towels]]. 
#Combine the cinnamon and 1 cup sugar. Sprinkle fried dough with sugar/cinnamon mixture. Store in an airtight container.

{{Warning|'''''Warning: Cannabis possession is prohibited in some regions. Be aware of local regulations.'''''}}'''Cannabutter''' is a preparation where butter is infused with cannabis. This transfers the psychoactive compounds in cannabis to the fat, and the resulting product can then be used to make various cannabis edibles.

==Ingredients==
*Water
*200 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (7 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*2 g [[Cookbook:Cannabis|cannabis]] (or more, depending on desired potency)

==Procedure==
#Bring a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] with a small amount of water to a boil.
#Add the butter and cannabis.
#[[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] this for a few hours on a low heat, adding water if too much evaporates. Do not let the temperature rise above about 190°F.
#Cool down. The oils and the extracts in the cannabis are now dissolved in the fat.
#Strain the mixture to remove the cannabis solids. Chill the mixture in the refrigerator to solidify the butter and separate out the water. The finished cannabutter should have a slight green color with a slightly off taste from the cannabis.
#Store the butter for up to 2 weeks in the fridge or 6 months in the freezer.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* The active ingredients in cannabis are readily absorbed by fats. Therefore any fats can be used, including lard, shortening, margarine, oils, etc. The unwanted portions of the cannabis, such as the color and flavor, are more readily absorbed into the water.
* The purpose of including water is to help prevent the temperature from rising too high, which would cause the psychoactive compounds to vaporize out of the mixture.

==Uses==

* This is a very good ingredient to make your favorite dishes. The cannabutter simply replaces the butter or other fat in the recipe.

'''Camotes enmielados''', also known as '''camotes con pilocilo''', or '''camotes enmielados al horno''', '''camotes con piloncilo al horno''', is a baked, or stovetop, dessert-style Mexican yam/sweet potato dish. It is traditionally a home-cooked food, not typical restaurant fare. The finished product should have a strong caramel flavor, with a typical hint of bitterness from the molasses component of the sugar used. The sauce should be syrupy and very dark in color. The cinnamon flavor should be an accent, and not dominating.

==Ingredients==
*1 large [[Cookbook:Yam|yam]] or [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potato]], optionally peeled
*1 large piloncilo cone (unrefined Mexican [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]])
*4 sticks [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
*½ water

== Procedure ==

# Place whole or thickly-sliced yams in a large [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|baking dish]].
# Place piloncilo cone atop the yams, then add water and cinnamon.
# Cover dish, and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] for about 60 minutes, [[Cookbook:Basting|basting]] the yams with the now sweetened cooking liquid as needed.

== Notes, tips, and variation ==

* Any dark, unrefined sugar may be reasonably substituted for the piloncilo, including [[Cookbook:Turbinado Sugar|turbinado sugar]], [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]], brown sugar with added molasses, muscovado, and even [[Cookbook:Jaggery|jaggery]].

[[File:Vendedor de camotes - Ciudad de México..jpg|thumb|Street vendor applying sweetened condensed milk to Camotes, Mexico City]]

==Further reading==
*''Latin American Street Food: The Best Flavors of Markets, Beaches, and Roadside Stands from Mexico to Argentina'', Sandra A. Gutierrez. The University of North Carolina Press (2013), ISBN: 978-1469608709

This is a very easy recipe made with only a few ingredients. The apricots can be served with chicken, pork or [[Cookbook:Turkish dolma pilav|Turkish dolma pilav]]. This should be enough for two people but it can easily be scaled up.

== Ingredients ==
*6–10+ dried [[Cookbook:Apricot|apricots]]
*About 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] water
*A generous handful of [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*[[Cookbook:Walnut|Walnuts]] (optional)

== Procedure ==
#Soak dried apricots in a large volume of water for around 10 minutes.
#Combine the 1 cup water and the sugar, and taste to adjust sweetness.
#Bring sugar mixture to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] and add apricots.
#[[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] until the liquid is reduced. The traditional consistency is close to a light syrup.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
*If reduced until it is a dark syrup it will be very hot and harden quickly, so plan accordingly.
*If serving as a dessert you can reduce to a light syrup and stuff or garnish with walnuts.
*This is good served with [[Cookbook:Turkish dolma pilav|Turkish dolma pilav]], or with a chicken or pork dish. It can also be served on its own with nuts as a dessert.

'''Béchamel''' or '''French white sauce''' (French: ''Sauce Béchamel'') is a white rich [[Cookbook:Sauces|sauce]], used as a basic sauce for many dishes.<ref>{{cite book|title=Mrs. Beeton's Book of Household Management|last=Beeton|first=Isabella|author-link=|isbn=|publisher=|date=1907|location=|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Mrs._Beeton%27s_Book_of_Household_Management/Chapter_X|page=220}}</ref>

== Ingredients ==

* 40 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (1½ [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) of [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|plain flour]]
* 40 g (2 oz) of [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 700 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (1¼ pints) of [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] (or white [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]])
* 1 small [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]] or [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallot]]
* 1 small [[Cookbook:Bouquet Garni|bouquet-garni]] ([[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]], [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]], [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaf]])
* 10 [[Cookbook:Pepper|peppercorns]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaf]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|cayenne]]
* ½ tsp [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]]
* ½ tsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

== Procedure ==

# Put the milk into a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] and place on the [[Cookbook:Cooktop|hob]]. Add the onion or shallot, the bouquet garni, peppercorns, mace, and bay leaf, and bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
# In another saucepan, melt the butter, stir in the flour, and cook a little without browning to make a [[Cookbook:Roux|roux]].
# Stir in your hot milk mixture and whisk over the heat until it boils, then bring down the temperature and let it [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 15 to 20 minutes.
# Strain and pass through a [[Cookbook:Sieve|sieve]] or muslin, return to the saucepan, and season lightly with ½ tsp nutmeg, ½ tsp cayenne, and ½ tsp salt.
# Serve.

==References==

'''Béchamel''' is one of the five "mother [[Cookbook:Sauces|sauces]]" in [[Cookbook:Cuisine of France|French cuisine]]. As a basic white sauce, it can be used as the base of many other sauces.

==Ingredients==
* 50 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 50 g (¼ cup) white wheat [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] (type 405)
* 1000 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (4½ cups) whole [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] (>3% milk fat)
* 1 small [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
*1 fresh [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaf]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]

==Procedure==

#In a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], melt the butter over medium-low heat. Whisk in the flour to make a [[Cookbook:Roux|roux]].
#Cook the roux over gentle heat for 3–5 minutes, but do not brown. This cooking is necessary to remove the floury taste.
#In a separate pot, begin heating the milk. Peel the onion, but do not cut it.
#Add the onion and bay leaf into the pot with the milk. Keep stirring until milk is heated to 80°C. Do not let the milk adhere and cook to pot bottom.
#Remove onion and bay leaf.
#Gradually whisk the heated milk into cooked roux. Add salt and pepper to taste.
#Stir and cook for 15 minutes until thickened. No lumps should be present.

{{Recipe summary
| Servings = 1
| Time = 40 minutes
| Difficulty = 2
}}{{Recipe}}

'''Koki corn''' is a classic Cameroonian dish known for its vibrant yellow color derived from red palm oil, as well as its delightful sweet taste originating from fresh corn. Corn holds a significant position as a staple food in the West African region, and steamed corn recipes are widely enjoyed. This traditional meal is often prepared during the rainy season when fresh corn is abundant. Like Cameroon, Nigeria also boasts dishes such as corn moimoi, ekoki, and okpo oka. However, what sets koki corn apart from these Nigerian counterparts is its simplicity and minimal use of ingredients.

== Ingredients ==

* ⅓–¼ cup [[Cookbook:Palm Oil|palm oil]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] fresh [[Cookbook:Corn|corn]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
* 1 cup yellow [[Cookbook:Cornmeal|corn meal]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Dehydrated Broth|stock cube]]
* 5 [[Cookbook:Banana|banana]] leaves

== Procedure ==

# Warm the palm oil in a skillet for 2–3 minutes without bleaching it.
# Place the corn, onion, and hot pepper in a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]] or [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]]. Add ¼ cup water, then blend until you achieve a coarsely ground paste. Avoid blending it into a fine paste; small bits and pieces of corn should still be visible.
# Transfer the blended mixture to a bowl and add the cornmeal. Pour in the heated oil and mix thoroughly. Add salt and stock cube, then continue mixing.
# Incorporate the chopped leaves into the mixture and mix until well combined.
# Prepare a pot by lining the bottom with stripped corn cobs. This creates an elevated base that prevents water from seeping into the koki corn. Pour approximately ½ cup  water into the pot and bring it to a gentle [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] while you proceed with wrapping the koki corn.
# Wrap the corn mixture in banana leaves to make little bundles. Place them in the pot, then cover them with torn or unused banana leaves (or aluminum foil). This helps retain the steam during cooking. 
# Place the lid on the pot and [[Cookbook:Steaming|steam]] for about 30 minutes. Every 5–10 minutes, open the pot and add ½ cup water to prevent it from drying out.
# After cooking, allow it to rest for approximately 10 minutes. Unwrap the bundles and serve the koki corn warm.
# Enjoy your delicious koki corn!

{{Recipe}}

'''Cachupa''' is a popular dish eaten throughout West Africa. It requires a lot of time to prepare.

== Ingredients ==

* 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] [[Cookbook:Corned Beef|corned beef]] brisket, cut into cubes
* 1½ pound [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] pork, cut into big chunks
* 3 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] apple cider or white [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]
* 2 fresh [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaves]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] powdered smoked paprika
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] or to taste
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]] or to taste
* 3 tablespoons crushed [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] feijao Pedro beans (rock [[Cookbook:Beans|beans]])
* 3 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 2 medium-size [[Cookbook:Onions|onions]], neatly [[Cookbook:Chop|chopped]]
* 2 large beef bouillon cubes
* 3 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* About 18 cups [[Cookbook:Water|water]]<nowiki/>y
* 2 cups dry yellow [[Cookbook:Hominy|hominy]], well-rinsed
*1 cup cranberry [[Cookbook:Beans|beans]]
* 1¼ cup large white [[Cookbook:Fava Bean|fava beans]]
* 1 medium size [[Cookbook:Cassava|madioca or yuca]]
* 4 cups [[Cookbook:Collard Greens|collard greens]] or [[Cookbook:Kale|kale]], rinsed and chopped
* 2 pounds [[Cookbook:Chorizo|chourico]] or linguica [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausage]], rinsed and [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] into rounds

== Procedure ==

# Season the corned beef and salt pork the night before with vinegar, bay leaves, smoked paprika, salt, black pepper, and 2 tablespoons crushed garlic. Let the meat [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinate]] in the refrigerator overnight.
# [[Cookbook:Soaking Beans|Soak]] the beans overnight as well.
# In a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], heat the olive oil over medium heat and add the neatly chopped onions and the remaining tablespoon of garlic. Transfer the bay leaves from the seasoned meat to the saucepan. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] the onions until fragrant.
# Add the marinated meat to the saucepan and let brown for about 10 minutes (5 minutes for each side). Remove the meat from the saucepan and set aside.
#Add the tomato paste and some of the crushed bouillon cubes to the saucepan. [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] until smooth. 
#Add the meat back to the saucepan, then cover with water. Cover the pot and bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
#Stir in the hominy, bring to a boil, and reduce the heat to low. Cover and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for about 1 hour. Make sure there is enough water in the saucepan, and check on the hominy about every 20 minutes to give it a stir.
#Remove the meat from the saucepan and shred it by lightly dragging a fork against it. This step is optional but can help break up some of the pieces of meat to make more space in the saucepan for the remaining ingredients.
#Add the meat back to the saucepan, stir it again and add the cranberry beans, fava beans, yuca, and greens. If the ingredients seem too bulky, add about half of the greens at first and let it cook for about 5 minutes, then add the remaining ones. Let everything cook for about 50 minutes.
#Add the chourico, and let cook for about 20 minutes.
#Stir and taste the cachupa, then adjust the seasoning as desired. Leave it to simmer for another 10–15 minutes.
#Remove from the heat, and let the cachupa rest, covered, for 20 minutes.
#Enjoy with any complimentary or favourite side dish of your choice.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* When preparing this meal, it is advisable to have a kettle of boiling water at hand throughout the cooking process so more water can be added at any stage when needed—do not use cold water.
* You can also use white hominy instead of yellow; it all depends on your preference, although most people prefer to use the yellow hominy.

| difficulty = 2
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Canjeero''' is a popular Somali [[Cookbook:Pancake|pancake]] that is enjoyed as a staple breakfast dish. Made with simple ingredients, these spongy and slightly tangy pancakes are perfect for soaking up stews and sauces or simply enjoyed on their own.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Self-rising Flour|self-rising flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Yeast|active dry yeast]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 3 cups lukewarm [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste

== Equipment ==
* Large [[Cookbook: Mixing Bowl|bowl]]
* [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] or spoon
* [[Cookbook:Griddle|Griddle]] or [[Cookbook:Non-stick|non-stick]] [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]]
* [[Cookbook: Towel|Towel]] or [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|plastic wrap]]

== Procedure ==
# In a large bowl, combine the all-purpose flour and self-rising flour.
# In a separate small bowl, mix the active dry yeast and sugar with 1 cup of lukewarm water. Let it sit for a few minutes to activate the yeast; it should become frothy.
# Pour the yeast mixture into the large bowl with the flours.
# Gradually add the remaining 2 cups of lukewarm water to the bowl while whisking or stirring continuously to form a smooth [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]]. The consistency should be similar to pancake batter.
# Cover the bowl with a clean kitchen towel or plastic wrap and let the batter [[Cookbook:Fermentation|ferment]] for at least 2 hours, or until it doubles in size and becomes slightly bubbly.
# After the fermentation process, add a [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of salt to the batter and stir well.
# Preheat a griddle or non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
# Pour a ladleful of the batter onto the hot griddle to form a round pancake. You can make the pancakes as small or as large as you like.
# Cook the pancake on one side until bubbles start to form on the surface and the edges look set. Then, flip it over and cook the other side until it turns golden brown.
# Repeat the process with the remaining batter, adding more oil to the griddle or pan as needed to prevent sticking.
# Serve warm with your favorite toppings, such as [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]], [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], or Somali tea.
== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Canjeero is traditionally cooked on a large, flat griddle called a ''taawa''. However, a non-stick frying pan works well too.
* The fermentation step is crucial to achieve the signature spongy texture and tangy flavor of canjeero. Make sure to allow enough time for the batter to ferment properly.
* You can customize the size of the pancakes to your preference. In Somali culture, smaller canjeero pancakes are often served for breakfast with a variety of accompaniments.

{{Recipe}}

'''Cake mix cookies''' is a delightful, quick recipe. It only takes three ingredients.<ref name="iheartnaptime">{{Cite web |last=Nye |first=Jamielyn |date=2022-12-17 |title=Cake Mix Cookies (3 Ingredients) |url=https://www.iheartnaptime.net/cake-mix-cookies/ |access-date=2024-12-07 |website=I Heart Naptime |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Ingredients ==
* 1 package (15 [[Cookbook:oz|oz]] / 425 [[Cookbook:g|g]]) [[Cookbook:Cake Mix|cake mix]] (any flavor)
* 2 [[Cookbook:egg|egg]]s
* 6–7 [[Cookbook:tablespoon|tablespoon]]s melted [[Cookbook:butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
* Add-ins, such as [[Cookbook:chocolate|chocolate]] chips (optional)

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|Baking sheet]]
* [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|Baking paper]]
* [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|Mixing bowl]]
* [[Cookbook:Spatula|Spatula]], wooden spoon, or electric [[Cookbook:Mixer|mixer]]
* Ice cream scoop or [[Cookbook: Tablespoon|tablespoon]]
* [[Cookbook:Oven|Oven]]
* [[Cookbook:Cooling Rack|Wire rack]]

== Procedure ==
# Preheat the oven to 180 °C (356 °F). Line a baking sheet with baking paper.
# Combine the cake mix, eggs and butter in a large bowl, mixing to form a soft dough. If using, fold in the add-ins.
# Scoop tablespoonfuls of dough onto the pan. The dough may be sticky, but chilling the dough for 30 minutes makes them firmer and easier to work.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 9–11 minutes until set. Transfer to a wire rack and leave them to cool.

== Notes, tips and variations ==
* For red velvet cake mix cookies, use red velvet cake mix and mix 1 cup (125 g) white chocolate chip into dough.<ref name="iheartnaptime" />
* For M&Ms cake mix cookies, use white or yellow cake mix and mix 1 cup (125 g) M&Ms into dough.<ref name="iheartnaptime" />
* For lemon cake mix cookies, use lemon cake mix and mix 1 tablespoon [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] [[Cookbook:Zest|zest]] and 1 tablespoon lemon juice into dough. Roll dough into balls and roll in [[Cookbook:Powdered sugar|powdered sugar]]. Bake as usual.<ref name="lemon">{{Cite web |last=Nye |first=Jamielyn |date=2020-04-06 |title=Lemon Cake Mix Cookies |url=https://www.iheartnaptime.net/lemon-cake-mix-cookies/ |access-date=2024-12-07 |website=I Heart Naptime |language=en-US}}</ref> You may need less butter to compensate the extra moisture and make it easier to roll.
* For snickerdoodle cake mix cookies, use white cake mix, and mix 1 tablespoon ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] into dough. Roll dough into balls and roll in cinnamon sugar (½ cup granulated sugar mixed with 1 tablespoon ground cinnamon).<ref name="cinnamonsugar">{{Cite web |title=Make Your Own Cinnamon Sugar at Home! And Save Money! |url=https://www.thespruceeats.com/how-to-make-cinnamon-sugar-3060767 |access-date=2024-12-07 |website=The Spruce Eats |language=en}}</ref> Bake as usual.<ref name="snickerdoodle">{{Cite web |last=Nye |first=Jamielyn |date=2021-04-19 |title=Easy Snickerdoodle Cake Mix Cookies |url=https://www.iheartnaptime.net/snickerdoodle-cake-mix-cookies/ |access-date=2024-12-07 |website=I Heart Naptime |language=en-US}}</ref>

{{recipesummary
|Category   = Vietnamese recipes
|Servings   = 10–15
|Time       = 18 hours
|Difficulty = 3
|Image      = [[Image:Nguyen lieu banh chung.jpg|300px]]
}}{{recipe}}

'''Bánh chưng''' (literally "steamed cake") is a traditional Vietnamese dish made from glutinous rice, mung beans and pork,<ref>{{Cite web |last=pasgo.vn |title=Sự tích bánh chưng bánh dày:Nguồn gốc ý nghĩa sâu xa của bánh truyền thống |trans-title=The story of Chung cake and Day cake: The origin and profound meaning of traditional cakes |url=https://pasgo.vn/blog/su-tich-banh-trung-banh-day-nguon-goc-y-nghia-sau-xa-cua-banh-truyen-thong-hoamkt-124-5655 |access-date=2026-02-03 |website=pasgo.vn |language=Vietnamese}}</ref> all wrapped in ''lá dong'' (''Stachyphrynium placentarium'') and tied tightly with strings. It is traditionally eaten during Lunar New Year ({{w|Tết|''Tết''}}).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bánh Chưng biểu tượng văn hoá trong ngày Tết cổ truyền Việt |trans-title=Bánh Chưng – A Cultural Symbol of Vietnam’s Traditional Lunar New Year (Tết) |url=https://banhbaominh.com/banh-chung-bieu-tuong-van-hoa-trong-ngay-tet/#:~:text=%C4%91%E1%BB%83%20g%C3%B3i%20b%C3%A1nh.-,Chu%E1%BA%A9n%20b%E1%BB%8B%20nguy%C3%AAn%20li%E1%BB%87u,ti%E1%BA%BFng%20ho%E1%BA%B7c%20%C4%91%E1%BB%83%20qua%20%C4%91%C3%AAm. |access-date=3 February 2026 |website=banhbaominh |language=vi}}</ref>

Bánh chưng is often eaten with pickled onions (dưa hành), pickled vegetables in fish sauce (dưa món), or dipped in sugar for a sweet treat. It can also be sliced, pan fried until golden, and served with sugar or sweet chili sauce.

== Ingredients ==
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Mung Bean|mung beans]], washed and soaked in water for 4 hours, or better overnight
* 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] belly (both lean pork and pork fat), cut in large cubes
* 2½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2½ tsp freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Black pepper|black pepper]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] fried [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallot]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]]
* 3 shallots, [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Fish Sauce|fish sauce]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] banana leaves (fresh or thawed)
* 5½ cups sticky [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]], washed and soaked in water overnight

== Procedure ==
# Place the mung beans in a pot, cover with water, and bring to a boil.
# Reduce to a simmer, and cook for about 20 minutes until the beans are soft and easily mashable.
# Mash the beans into a paste. Season to taste with 1 tsp salt, fried shallots, 1 tsp pepper and vegetable oil.
# Season the meat with ½ tsp salt and 1½ tsp pepper, and combine with the shallots and fish sauce. Mix well and let it marinate for a few hours.
# Spread about 1 cup of mashed mung bean onto plastic wrap, add a few pieces of lean pork and pork fat, and shape it into a round or squared piece.
# Tear the banana leaves into very large pieces(around 18–20 inches).
# Season the soaked rice with a pinch of salt.
# Lay out two sheets of partially overlapping banana leaves on a flat surface. Place 1 cup of sticky rice at the center of the leaves. Place the fillings on top of the rice and then cover it up with another cup of sticky rice. Fold the leaves and wrap it up tightly like a present.
# To prevent water penetrating into the cake during the boiling process, it is important to wrap up the cake a second time. For the inner layer, make sure that the darker side of the banana leaf faces the rice so that it can tint the cake with a nice subtle green color later on. However, for the outer layer, the darker side of the banana leaf should face outside to give it a beautiful green package.
# After wrapping, tie the cake tightly with twines.
# Arrange the cakes tightly in a large stockpot and fill with water. Bring the stockpot to a boil and let it simmer for about 6 to 8 hours until the cakes feel plump and the rice is congealed.
# To serve, untie and unwrap the cakes, and cut into pieces with a thread or dental floss.
