|Image      = [[Image:Bo Bia Jicama Rolls.jpg|300px]]
}}{{recipe}}

'''Bò bía''' is the southern Vietnamese variant of popiah, a Fujianese/Teochew-style fresh spring roll filled with an assortment of fresh, dried, and cooked ingredients, eaten during the Qingming Festival and other celebratory occasions.

== Ingredients ==
* 9 [[Cookbook:Rice Paper|rice paper]] rounds
* 3 [[Cookbook:Each|ea.]] Chinese sweet sausages (''lạp xưởng'')
* 2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsps]] dried small shrimps
* 400 g [[Cookbook:Jicama|jicama]], peeled and cut into [[Cookbook:Julienne|matchsticks]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], minced
* [[Cookbook:Lettuce|Lettuce]], Thai basil, fresh [[Cookbook:Chili|chili]]
* Crushed [[Cookbook:Peanut|peanuts]], fried shallot
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]], [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]]

For the dipping sauce:
* 1 tbsp vegetable oil
* 1 tbsp minced garlic
* 5 tbsps [[Cookbook:Hoisin Sauce|hoisin sauce]]
* 5 tbsps pork broth or water
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Peanut Butter|peanut butter]]
* 1 tbsp sugar
* Pickled [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]] and [[Cookbook:White Radish|daikon]]

== Procedure ==

=== Filling ===
# Roast the small dried shrimps without any oil in a pan by stirring constantly on medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant.
# Clean the pan, fill about half full with water and bring to a boil. Cook 2 Chinese sausages for about 10 minutes to soften and remove some of the fat. Rinse the sausages well, let them cool and slide them thinly on a diagonal.
# Crack 2 eggs in a small bowl and beat them until fluffy. Season lightly with a pinch of salt and a pinch of sugar.
# In a non-stick pan, add 1 tsp of vegetable oil. When it's hot enough, pour in half of the egg mixture and quickly tilt the pan in a circular motion to spread the egg thinly and evenly. When one side is golden, flip it over and fry the other side for 5 more seconds. Repeat until the egg mixture has been used up.
# Let the omelettes cool completely. Roll them up and cut into half-inch strips.
# In a saucepan, heat up some cooking oil and sauté 1 tbsp of garlic until fragrant.
# Add in the jicama strips and stir-fry with some salt for about 10 to 15 minutes until it turns quite translucent and tastes naturally sweet.

=== Dipping sauce ===
# Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a small sauce pan on medium-high heat, then fry 1 tbsp minced garlic till golden brown.
# Then add hoisin sauce, pork broth, peanut butter and sugar. Stir well and simmer on low heat for 1-2 minutes until thickened. 
# Transfer to condiment bowls and top up with minced fresh chili, pickled carrots and daikon and crushed peanuts.

=== Assembly ===
# Set up a rolling station with the prepared Chinese sausages, stir-fried jicama, omelette strips, fresh greens (e.g. lettuce and Thai basil), roasted small dried shrimps, some crushed peanuts and fried shallots ready on the plates. 
# Prepare a small bowl with pickled carrots and daikon.
# Also prepare a large bowl of lukewarm water to soften rice paper, and a flat work surface (like a cutting board or a large plate) for the rolling job.
# To soften the rice paper, quickly dip it into a bowl of warm water (the dipping motion should take no more than 2 seconds). Gently shake off excess water and lay it on the flat surface.
# Place a piece of lettuce and a few basil leaves at one end of the paper, then continue to add some of the stir-fried jicama, few slices of the Chinese sausages, few omelette strips, some roasted small dried shrimps, some fried shallots and crushed peanuts.
# Starting from the end with vegetables, roll 1-2 rounds first until you reach the center of the rice paper, then fold both sides inwards. Then continue rolling until reaching the other end of the paper.
# Roll gently and tight enough, so that the ingredients do not fall out after one's first bite. A nice roll should show up all the colors of the ingredients inside.

=== Serving ===
# To serve, dip the salad roll in the dipping sauce or spoon some of the sauce onto the roll and have a bite.

{{Recipe}}

'''Cake goop''', also called '''pan release''', is an alternative to greasing and flouring cake pans, or buying commercial sprays. It is particularly useful for [[Cookbook:Bundt Cake Pan|Bundt pans]] and other complex shapes.

== Ingredients ==
{| class="wikitable"
!Ingredient
!Volume
!Weight
|-
|[[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|Vegetable oil]] or another neutral-flavored oil
|½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]]
|100 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]
|-
|[[Cookbook:Shortening|Vegetable shortening]]
|½ cup
|90 g
|-
|[[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|All-purpose flour]]
|½ cup
|60 g
|}

== Procedure ==

# Stir together the oil and shortening. This can be done with a spoon, a whisk, or an electric mixer.
# Add the flour and stir until mostly smooth. Don't worry about trying to get every little lump out.
# When a recipe says to prepare the cake pan by greasing and flouring it, or by spraying it with a cooking spray containing flour, instead use a [[Cookbook:Brush|brush]] to spread a thin layer of cake goop on the bottom and sides of the pan. If the pan has intricate details, be sure that the goop has gotten into the crevices. Then, pour in the cake batter, and bake as usual.
[[File:Zwei Backpinsel.jpg|alt=Hand holding a natural-bristle brush and a silicone rubber brush|thumb|Use a pastry brush to spread it on the pan]]
== Notes, tips, and variations ==

=== Storage ===
* Cake goop can be stored in an airtight jar or container at room temperature for months, and in the refrigerator for at least six months. It can even be frozen, which is convenient if you want to make one batch, divide it up (e.g., in an [[Cookbook:Ice Cube Tray|ice cube tray]]), and then thaw smaller amounts as needed. It's easier to use if it's not cold.
* If it separates while it sits, just stir it again.

=== Limitations ===

*If you use too much, it can actually make the cake stick. For a small pan, you will use about 1 tablespoon (15 ml) each time.
*Very large cakes and cakes with very high amounts of sugar usually do better with [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment baking paper]] than with any kind of grease-and-flour approach, including this one. For example, for a 12-inch (30 cm) round cake, the best approach is to line the bottom of the pan with parchment and then use cake goop on the sides. A bit of cake goop can be used under the parchment to stick it in place.

=== Ingredients and variations ===

*[[Cookbook:Gluten-Free Flour|Gluten-free flour]] substitutes can be used in this recipe. However, you may want to make and test a small amount with your preferred flour substitute, to see whether that particular blend of flours is compatible.
* [[Cookbook:Butter|Butter]] can be used instead of the shortening. However, it must be stored in the refrigerator, and the shelf life is reduced to the shelf life of your butter (usually three months or less).
* [[Cookbook:Cocoa|Unsweetened cocoa powder]] can be substituted for up to half of the flour. Sift (or at least stir) the cocoa and flour together before adding. This is handy if you are baking a chocolate cake and don't want to risk having any flour-colored streaks on the edges.

'''Carpetbag steak''' is a uniquely Australian dish that was first popularised in Sydney around 1950. 

==Ingredients ==
* 1 Scotch [[Cookbook:Steak|fillet steak]] (thickly-cut)
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] (optional)
* Ground [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|black pepper]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|Cayenne pepper]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|Lemon juice]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]] (optional)
* 3–4 [[cookbook:Oyster|oyster]]s
* [[Cookbook:Worcestershire Sauce|Worcestershire sauce]]
* [[Cookbook:Lime|Limes]] (optional)
* Shredded [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]] (optional)

==Procedure==
#Cut a small pocket, approximately 6 cm (2.5 inches) in length and about the same depth, in the edge of the thick steak.
#If desired, season the inside of the pocket with some of salt, pepper, cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and olive oil.
#Dip the oysters into the Worcestershire sauce, and then insert them in the pocket in the steak.
#If desired, add lime pulp or some shredded cheese into the pocket.
#Seal the pocket with a moistened [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewer]].
#[[Cookbook:Barbecuing|Barbecue]], [[Cookbook:Grilling|grill]], or [[Cookbook:Broiling|broil]] the steak to your desired level of [[Cookbook:Meat and Poultry#Doneness|doneness]]. Alternatively, cook over a moderate heat in a heavy-based [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]].

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Substitutes for Worcestershire sauce include [[Cookbook:Teriyaki Sauce|teriyaki sauce]], [[Cookbook:Oyster sauce|oyster sauce]] or red wine vinegar marinades, or the steak has the marinade or sauce.
*Substitutes for oysters include [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]], [[Cookbook:Crawfish|yabbies]], and [[Cookbook:Shrimp|prawns]].
*Some recipes [[Cookbook:Poaching|poach]] or [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] the oysters first a little, if the diners prefer rare steak but not raw oysters.
*Some recipes wrap the steak in [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]] or [[Cookbook:Pancetta|pancetta]].
*If applicable and desired, you can [[Cookbook:Deglazing|deglaze]] the cooking pan with [[Cookbook:Sherry|sherry]] or [[Cookbook:Brandy|brandy]], or make a reduction of oyster liquid and [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]] with chopped [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]].

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] | [[Cookbook:Rice Recipes|Rice]]

'''Chakarai pongal''' is a sweet and buttery porridge-like dish that is traditionally prepared in South [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|India]] for the Makar Sankranti festival that heralds the arrival of summer. The [[Cookbook:Khara pongal|khara pongal]] variety differs only in the spices added, and the two are often cooked together from the same batch of rice and dhal.

==Ingredients==
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] white [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Mung Bean|moong]] [[Cookbook:Dal|dhal]]
* 4 cups [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Cashew|cashew]] nuts
* ¼ cup white [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Cardamom|cardamom]] powder
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Ghee|ghee]] (or [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]])
* ¾ cup [[Cookbook:Jaggery|jaggery]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]

==Procedure==
# Cook the rice and dhal together with cups of water in a pot or [[Cookbook:Pressure Cooker|pressure cooker]] until mushy.
# Meanwhile, melt the jaggery with 1 cup of water in a pan.
# Add the cardamom to the jaggery as it melts.
# Mush the rice and paruppu (dal) mixture well and add to the pan of jaggery.
# Stir well and cook on low heat till the mixture comes together well.
# Heat 4 tablespoons of the ghee in a separate pan and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] cashews to golden brown. 
# Add raisins and fry for a few more seconds or until they swell up. 
# Add the nuts and raisins to into the pongal.
# Serve hot with an additional dollop of neyyi or ghee.

==Procedure==
# In a large [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|mixing bowl]], mix flour, salt and orange peel; [[cookbook:whisk|whisk]] gently to distribute the ingredients.
# Split green cardamom pods and remove the seeds inside. With a [[Cookbook:Mortar and Pestle|mortar and pestle]], grind the seeds into a powder and add this to the other dry ingredients.
# In a small bowl, combine yeast, warm water and sugar. Stir gently for a few seconds, then let stand until the yeast is frothy.
# In a small [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] on low-to-medium heat, combine butter and milk and bring the mixture to at least {{convert|180|F|C}} while stirring, then turn off heat to let it cool.
# In a separate bowl, [[Cookbook:Beating|beat]] the eggs and set aside.
# Check that the milk and butter mixture is not hot, then add the it into the dry ingredients and mix.
# Mix in the beaten eggs.
# [[cookbook:Knead|Knead]] the dough until it is smooth and elastic. 
# Place the kneaded dough in a greased bowl and let rise in a warm place (in the oven, for example) until it doubles in size, about one hour.
# Knock back the dough, and cut in two parts (one for each loaf).

=== Braiding ===
# For one of the halves, split the dough into three equal sized portions.
# Roll these into "ropes" about 18 inches (45 cm) long.
# Pinch one end of each rope together.
# Braid the ropes together:
## Take the left rope and cross it over the middle one.
## Take the right rope and cross it over the middle one.
## Repeat this procedure until the ropes are fully braided.
## Pinch the other end of the ropes together.
## Tuck each pinched end underneath the main loaf.
# Repeat the rope-making and braiding for the second half of the dough.
# Put finished braids on a greased [[Cookbook:cookie sheet|cookie sheet]].
# Let rise again until doubled in size, about 45 minutes.
# Prepare the egg wash by beating the 1 egg with a dash of water to thin it.
# [[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] the top of each braid with the egg wash.
# Sprinkle each braid with pearl sugar and sliced almonds.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at 180 °C (350 °Fahrenheit) for 25 minutes.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Store-bought ground cardamom can be used in this recipe, but has a less intense flavor than freshly-ground cardamom.
* Orange peel is not traditional in cardamom bread.
* For a [[Cookbook:Vegan cuisine|vegan]] version, substitute [[Cookbook:Soy Milk|soy milk]] for milk, egg replacer for eggs, and a vegan [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]] for butter.

'''Kinpira''' is a [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Japan|Japanese]] cooking term that roughly translates to ''[[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]]''. The aim is to cook root vegetables such as carrots and burdock root in a minimum amount of water so that they end up tenderly cooked and with none of their flavour or nutritional value lost into discarded cooking water.

==Ingredients==
*250 g (½ lb) [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]]s, [[Cookbook:Julienne|julienned]]
*1 Tbsp [[cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]], preferably [[Cookbook:Sesame Oil|sesame oil]]
*[[Cookbook:Water|Water]]
*Tamari or shoyu [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]], to taste

==Procedure==
# Cut the carrots into thin matchstick pieces (sen-giri, or [[Cookbook:Julienne|julienned]])
# Pour a small amount of oil into a [[cookbook:saucepan|saucepan]] and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] the carrot pieces briefly
# Add just enough water to half-cover the carrot pieces
# Place the lid on the pot and let the carrots [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] briefly on medium-low heat
# Add a little tamari or shoyu to enhance flavour. Serve.

The '''century egg''' (a.k.a. preserved egg, thousand-year egg, hundred-year egg, hundred-year-old egg, thousand-year-old egg; Chinese: 皮蛋; pinyin: pídàn or Chinese: 松花蛋; pinyin: sōnghūadàn) is a Chinese delicacy made by preserving duck (or less commonly chicken) eggs in a mixture of charcoal and lime for (despite the name) around 100 days. It is greenish in color, has a creamy cheese-like flavor, and a strong aroma.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Peru|Cuisine of Peru]]

==Ingredients==
* 10 medium [[cookbook:potato|potatoes]] (yellow, new, or red are a good choice)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] of shredded boiled [[cookbook:chicken|chicken]] meat
* 100 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[cookbook:mayonnaise|mayonnaise]]
* 25 g [[cookbook:butter|butter]]
* 2 cloves [[cookbook:garlic|garlic]]
* [[cookbook:salt|Salt]]
* [[cookbook:pepper|Pepper]]
* [[cookbook:lettuce|Lettuce]]
* 3 [[cookbook:Hard Boiled Eggs|hard boiled eggs]]
* [[cookbook:Olive|Black olives]]

==Procedure==
# Cook and peel potatoes. Allow to cool, then mash.
# In a bowl combine the chicken, mayonnaise, onion, salt, and pepper.
# Line a deep dish with plastic wrap, or place a molding cylinder on a plate.
# Add the mashed potatoes to form a bed about 1 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] tall at the bottom.
# Add a second layer of 1 cm of the chicken mixture evenly over the potato.
# Top the chicken mixture with a final layer of potato, forming a sandwich of chicken inside two layers of potato.
# Unmold or remove the cylinder.
# [[cookbook:Garnish|Garnish]] with lettuce and mayonnaise.
# Cut the hard boiled eggs in discs and place on top. Add black olives, if desired.
# This dish can be served slightly cold.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Mashed potatoes can be prepared with a mix of olive oil and butter and adding one tablespoon of lemon juice. You can compensate lemon with salt. Don't add milk.
* You can replace the chicken with a can of tuna mixed with mayonnaise and fine chopped onion. Serve this variation fresh only.

}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of China|Cuisine of China]]

This is a recipe for '''Cantonese roast duck or goose''' (燒鴨\燒鵝).

== Ingredients ==
__NOTOC__
=== Marinade ===
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]] light [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
* 2 Tbsp dark soy sauce (optional, can use light soy sauce instead)
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (450 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) of white [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]], [[Cookbook:Sherry|sherry]], or Chinese cooking wine
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Five Spice Powder|Chinese five spice powder]]

=== Glaze ===
* 2 Tbsp [[Cookbook:Hoisin Sauce|Hoisin sauce]]
* 2 Tbsp dark soy sauce

=== Duck ===

* 3–6 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (1.3–2.6 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]]) whole [[Cookbook:Duck|duck]] or [[Cookbook:Goose|goose]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Green Onion|green onions]] or 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]

== Procedure ==

=== Preparation ===
# Mix all marinade ingredients together.
# Mix all glaze ingredients together.
# [[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] the marinade mixture all over the duck, inside and outside.
# Brush some glaze mixture inside the duck cavity.
# Sit duck breast-up on a rack in an open container.
# Put in the refrigerator to chill overnight.

=== Cooking ===
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 450°F (220°C)
# Put ½–1 [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] (2.5 cm) of water in a roasting pan—this catches the grease that comes out from the duck while roasting and prevents it from smoking.
# Place green onions inside the duck cavity.
# Place the duck on a roasting rack in the roasting pan. [[Cookbook:Roasting|Roast]] the duck for 15 minutes.
# Turn the duck breast-up, and roast for another 15 minutes.
# Turn oven heat to 375°F (190°C), and roast the duck until the internal temperature reaches a minimum of 180°F (test between the thigh, the thickest part of the duck/goose, being careful not to touch the bone)
# Brush the duck with glaze, turn oven up to 450°F (200°C), and roast again for about 10 minutes.
# Carve and serve!

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Mexico|Mexican cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Tex-Mex cuisine|Tex-Mex cuisine]]

A '''chalupa''' is a kind of tostada platter in [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Mexico|Mexican cuisine]]. It is a specialty of South-central regions of Mexico, such as the states of Guerrero and Oaxaca. It is made by pressing a thin layer of masa dough around the outside of a small mold and then deep frying it to produce a crisp shallow corn cup. It is typically filled with shredded pork meat, a slice of onion, and a piece of chipotle pepper. In the Americanized form, described below, the tortilla is typically left flat.

== Ingredients ==
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]]
* 12 corn [[Cookbook:Tortilla|tortillas]]
* 6 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] refried beans ([[Cookbook:Pinto Beans Recipe from South Texas|pinto beans]] or [[Cookbook:Black Bean|black beans]] may be substituted)
* ½ [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] grated [[Cookbook:Queso Fresco|queso fresco]] [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]]
* Chopped [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
* 1 large [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 3 cups shredded [[Cookbook:Lettuce|lettuce]]

== Procedure ==
# In a small skillet, heat about ½ [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] of vegetable oil. Test the oil for the correct temperature by putting in a small piece of tortilla. If the oil immediately bubbles frantically and the bread quickly becomes crisp then the oil is at the right temperature. This is important because a low temperature will produce an unpleasantly oily and soggy chalupa shell.
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] the tortilla completely flat in the oil, on both sides, until very crisp. Drain and keep the fried tortilla warm on a newspaper or [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towel]]-covered [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|cookie sheet]] in a warm [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]]. Spread a layer of refried beans on each fried tortilla, about ¼ inch thick. Top with a generous amount of grated cheddar cheese and about 1 tablespoon of chopped onion.
# Place the assembled chalupas on a cookie sheet and brown under [[Cookbook:Broiler|broiler]] until the cheese melts and begins to bubble. Watch them carefully at this stage, as they can burn quite quickly.
# Top with shredded lettuce and tomato, and serve immediately.

== External links ==
* [http://authentic-mexican-recipes.blogspot.com/2006/05/chalupas.html Chalupa recipe - Authentic Mexican Recipes]

==Ingredients==
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive]] or [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]]
* 4 large yellow or white [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] into thin strips
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Vinegar|balsamic vinegar]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ⅛ teaspoon coarse ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]

==Procedure==
# Heat oil in a large [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] over medium heat. Add onions, and [[Cookbook:Sauté|sauté]], stirring, for about 15 minutes, or until they begin to brown. Do not cook over high heat, as the outside of the onions will char too quickly before the insides have softened and sweetened.
# When onions have softened and turned a light golden brown, add sugar. Continue stirring until sugar melts and begins to bubble.
# As the onions turn a richer brown, clear a space in the center of the pan. Pour balsamic vinegar directly onto the hot pan, then stir it into onions.
# When vinegar has reduced, leaving a syrupy coating on the onions, turn off the heat.
# Stir in salt and pepper, and allow onions to cool.

==Uses==

'''Caramel squares''' (alternatively: '''caramel slices''', '''caramel shortbread''', or '''millionaire's shortbread''') are a wonderfully rich and classic treat, very popular all over [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|Britain]] and [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Ireland|Ireland]]. They can often be found in cafes, served with morning coffee or afternoon tea. They're perfect for [[cookbook:picnic|picnic]]s, lunches and your guests will love them! They have a crunchy base with a creamy caramel filling, topped off with chocolate.

== Ingredients ==

=== Base ===
*350 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Self-rising Flour|self-raising flour]]
*225 g unsalted [[cookbook:butter|butter]]
*110 g [[cookbook:caster sugar|caster sugar]]

=== Filling ===
*225 g [[cookbook:Caster sugar|caster sugar]]
*225 g unsalted [[cookbook:butter|butter]]
*5 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tablespoons]] [[cookbook:Golden Syrup|golden syrup]]
*400 [[Cookbook:ML|ml]] full-fat [[cookbook:condensed milk|condensed milk]]

=== Topping ===
*340 g good-quality [[cookbook:chocolate|chocolate]] (milk or dark), melted

==Procedure==

=== Base ===
#Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 180°C (gas mark 4; 350°F). Rub flour, butter, and caster sugar together until it resembles breadcrumbs.
#Press into a 25 x 38 x 4 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] Swiss roll pan.
#[[cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 20 minutes or till golden.
#Cool.

=== Filling ===
#Melt butter in a heavy-based [[cookbook:saucepan|saucepan]] over a low heat; add sugar, golden syrup, and condensed milk.
#Stir continuously for 40–50 minutes. It should be golden brown in colour when ready to eat. To test, drop a little blob into a bowl of cold water; it should firm up.
#Pour this caramel mixture over the base, and let it cool.

=== Topping ===
#Pour melted chocolate over the top.
#Spread the chocolate evenly, and let set.

This is a wonderful dish that is very easy to do. It uses raw eggs, which are not to everyone's taste and should be avoided by pregnant women.

==Ingredients==
* 4 free-range [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]] with large yolks
* 3 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (65 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) fresh Italian [[Cookbook:Pancetta|pancetta]], [[Cookbook:Cube|cubed]] into ¼–⅜-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] (0.64–0.95 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]) pieces
* 1 sprig of fresh [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* ¼ small [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely chopped
* The minced [[Cookbook:Zest|zest]] of ½ a [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]] to taste
* Grated [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|parmigiano]] and/or [[Cookbook:Pecorino Romano Cheese|pecorino romano]] cheese
* 12 oz (340 g) uncooked [[Cookbook:Pasta|pasta]] (e.g. spaghetti or penne)

==Procedure==

# Put on the desired quantity of pasta to cook.
# Crack the eggs carefully, and separate the yolks from the whites—a good way of doing this is to run the egg through the almost closed fingers of your upturned palm, so as the white runs away through the fingers, and the yolk remains in your hand. Keep the yolks in a large bowl, and use the whites for another purpose. Remember to pick out the pesky little white bit that always remains behind on the yolk.
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] the pancetta on a lowish heat in a dry [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] until it is crispy. 
# When the pancetta is cooked, drain and allow it to cool for a few minutes before combining it with the yolks in a large bowl. Allowing it to cool prevents cooking of the eggs.
# Add a [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of rock-salt and a very generous amount of ground pepper to the yolk mixture.
# Add the lemon zest, chopped thyme, and a small amount of the Parmigiano cheese.
# Drain the pasta through a [[Cookbook:Colander|colander]], count to 10 to let the pasta cool slightly, and add it to the bowl with the yolk mixture.
# Mix it through with a wooden spoon and serve immediately, sprinkling the remaining Parmigiano cheese over the top.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* For the pancetta, don't buy the ready cubed stuff, but the fresh, Italian version with a little cracked pepper on the rind. If you really can't find it, smoked [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]] will do.
* Use yolks as fresh and yellow as possible!
* If you want to add a little chopped flat-leaf [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]] (not the curly stuff) to add colour, go ahead.
* Served with a simple green salad, it's delicious.

{{recipe}}

'''''Cappeletti in Brodo''''' is a very simple and very delicious Italian pasta soup, made with Cappeletti (small meat or vegetable filled) ravioli. It's delicious on a cold day, getting in from a long day at work, and without much time to devote to preparing a tasty meal. Best served with some home made garlic bread and a healthy salad.

==Ingredients==
*250 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] packet of Cappelletti [[Cookbook:Pasta|pasta]] pillows
*½ [[Cookbook:Liter|litre]] of water plus more to thin out the soup if required
*2 good quality [[Cookbook:Bouillon Cube|chicken stock cubes]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] of single [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]
*1 dash of [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
*1 handful of [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]
*1 dash of sweet [[Cookbook:Sherry|sherry]]
*Freshly-grated [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|Parmesan]] to serve

==Procedure==
#Bring the water to a rolling [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], add the stock cubes, and let them dissolve.
#Add the Cappelletti pasta, and cook according to the instructions on the packet.
#Add the cream and the parsley about 2 minutes before the end of the cooking. Turn down the heat.
#Add the slug of sherry just before serving. If serving to children, the sherry can be added to the grown-up's plate after serving!
#Let stand for a few minutes.
#Serve sprinkled with grated Parmesan cheese. Further serving suggestion might include a green salad, or a cold bean salad.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Colombia|Cuisine of Colombia]]

'''Cazuela Gallega''' is a delicious egg, ham and cheese casserole, good for breakfast or dinner.

==Ingredients==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 2 slices of [[Cookbook:ham|ham]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:tablespoon|tablespoons]] of petit pois (canned [[Cookbook:pea|peas]])
* 2 [[Cookbook:tablespoon|tablespoons]] of [[Cookbook:Ketchup|ketchup]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:tablespoon|tablespoon]] of [[Cookbook:butter|butter]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:cup|cup]] of ground [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|Parmesan cheese]] 
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]

==Procedure==
# Place 3 sheets of [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|aluminum foil]] (approx 15 x 15 inches or 35 x 35 cm) into a bowl with a 5-inch (12 cm) diameter and 2-inch depth. Press gently the foil downwards in order to give it the shape of the bowl. 
# Spread the [[Cookbook:butter|butter]] all over inside walls of the aluminum-shaped bowl.
# Place one slice of [[Cookbook:ham|ham]] in the bottom of the bowl. Cut the additional slice in three strips. With each strip, cover inside walls of aluminum bowl.
# Add both [[Cookbook:egg|eggs]] to the bowl.
# Add the [[Cookbook:pea|peas]], spreading them all over the eggs. Be careful with the yolks—don't break them. Add 1 teaspoon of the liquid from the can.
# Add a [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]], and the [[Cookbook:Ketchup|ketchup]], trying to cover all the area.
# Carefully remove foil with the casserole from the bowl. Top with the [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|cheese]] and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] 30 minutes in a preheated 400°F (205C) [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]].

This is a traditional Jewish dish.

==Ingredients==
* 4 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], separated
* 75 [[Cookbook:Gram|grams]] white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 25 grams [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*1 small cooking [[Cookbook:Apple|apple]]
* Grated [[Cookbook:Zest|zest]] of 1 [[Cookbook:Orange|orange]]
* 225 grams [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]]
* Juice of 1 [[Cookbook:Orange|orange]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] juice
* 50 grams [[Cookbook:Potato Flour|potato flour]]

==Procedure==
# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 190°C (375°F). 
# Grease a 1-litre [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|casserole dish]].
# [[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] the egg yolks and sugar in a bowl until light and fluffy and pale in color.
# Very finely [[Cookbook:Grating|grate]] the carrot and apple, then squeeze out and discard all the liquid.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian Cuisine]]  

'''Caponata''' is a Sicilian eggplant dish consisting of cooked vegetables with chopped up fried eggplant, celery, sweetened vinegar, and capers with sweet sauce.  
==Ingredients==

* 2 ¼ [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] (1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]]) [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplant]] (aubergine) 
* ½ pound (225 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) green [[Cookbook:Olive|olives]] packed in brine, pitted 
* 6 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] (170 g) salted [[Cookbook:Caper|capers]], rinsed 
* 1 ¼ (570 g) pounds [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]] ribs 
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Tomato Sauce|tomato sauce]] (optional) 
* ⅔ pound (300 g) [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]]
* ⅔ pound (300 g) [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
* ⅓ cup [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar ]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* [[Cookbook:Basil|Basil]]
* ⅜ cup [[Cookbook:Pine Nut|pine nuts]]
* [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]

==Procedure==
# Strip the filaments from the celery sticks and [[Cookbook:Blanching|blanch]] in lightly salted water for five minutes. Drain and cut the celery into bite-size pieces, [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] them in a little oil, and set aside. 
# Wash and [[Cookbook:Dice|dice]] the eggplant, strain, and sprinkle liberally with salt, and let sit for several hours to draw out the bitterness. In the meantime, blanch, peel, seed and [[Cookbook:Chopping|chop]] the tomatoes. 
# Once the eggplant has sat, rinse away the salt and pat the pieces dry. Finely [[Cookbook:Slicing|slice]] the onion and sauté them in olive oil; once they have turned translucent, add the capers, pine nuts, olives, and tomatoes. Continue cooking, stirring with a wooden spoon, until the tomatoes are done, about 15 minutes, and then remove the pot from the heat. 
# While the tomatoes are cooking, heat another pan of oil and fry the eggplant, in batches, to prevent lowering of the frying temperature. When the last batch is done, return the tomato pot to the heat and stir in the eggplant together with the previously sautéed celery. Cook for several minutes over low flame, stirring gently, then stir in the vinegar and the sugar; when the vinegar has almost completely evaporated, remove the pot from the fire and let it cool.
# Serve the caponata cold with a garnish of fresh basil. Caponata keeps for several days in the refrigerator.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* You can serve this on toast as an appetizer, as a side dish, or as a main dish for a light meal.

#[[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] the dough with the beaten egg. 
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in the oven at moderate heat (180°C) for 25 minutes.

==Procedure==

[[File:Cookbookchallah1.jpg|right|200px]]
=== Dough ===
# Put bread flour in a bowl. Mix in the ½ cup of sugar and the salt.
# In a small bowl or large measuring cup, add the 1 ½ cups of warm water. Mix in the 1 tablespoon of sugar. Sprinkle the yeast on top and wait 8 minutes. The yeast mixture should be foamy.
# Briefly mix the yeast mixture, then mix it into the flour mixture.
# Mix in the eggs and oil.
# Add the remaining 1 cup warm water, and [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] the [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] for about 10 minutes.
# Let the dough rise, covered, for two-four hours.
===Braiding===
# Divide the dough into four parts. These will make 4 challahs.
# Take one part. Separate it into four pieces. Take each piece and roll it between your hands until it is a long strand. Attach the four strands together at one end by squeezing the ends together (see picture).
# Place on a piece of [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|foil]] or a pan.
# Take the strand at the far left and braid by putting it over two strands to the right and then put it back under one strand to the left.
# Take the strand at the far right and  put it over two strands to the left and then put it back under one strand to the right.
# Repeat the last two steps until you reach the end of the strands.
# Do the same thing with the other three parts.
===Finish===
# [[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] each loaf with egg wash and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
# Allow to rise for two hours.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in preheated [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] at 400°F (200°C) for 25 minutes.

{{recipe}}

'''Carrot and coriander soup''' is a classic combination made with both fresh and ground coriander. The fresh coriander added near the end of cooking really adds the bright flavour of coriander to match with the carrot.

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 1 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] 
* 500 g (1.1 lb) [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] 
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Coriander|ground coriander]]
* 1.2 L (41 oz) [[Cookbook:Vegetable Stock|vegetable stock]]
* 1 large bunch [[Cookbook:Cilantro|fresh coriander]] (cilantro), roughly [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|Black pepper]]

==Procedure==
# Heat the olive oil in a non-stick pan, to a medium heat.
# Add the onions and carrots. Cook for approximately 5 minutes until they start to soften.
# Add the ground coriander, salt, and pepper. Cook for another minute.
# Add the vegetable stock, and bring the mixture to the [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] for 10–15 minutes until the carrots are very soft.
# [[Cookbook:Puréeing|Purée]] until smooth.
# Add the fresh coriander, and serve.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Sauces]]

This [[Cookbook:Gravy|gravy]] is a thick cashew-based sauce that tastes great on vegetables. '''Cashew gravy''' is traditionally one way of making a creamy vegan sauce—use unsweetened soy milk instead of milk if a vegan recipe is desired.

==Ingredients==
*½ thinly-[[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
*½ thinly-sliced [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Peanut Oil|peanut oil]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
*[[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]] to taste
*2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:White Wine|white wine]]
*1½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] or unsweetened [[Cookbook:Soy Milk|soy milk]]
*½ cup [[Cookbook:Cashew Butter|cashew butter]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Cayenne pepper|cayenne pepper]]

==Procedure==

# Allow the cashew butter to come to room temperature, if refrigerated.
# Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the peanut oil over low to medium heat with salt and pepper, until the onion begins to turn translucent and the bell pepper is soft.
# Add the wine and deglaze the pan.
# Add cayenne pepper and milk, and heat through.
# Add the cashew butter by the spoonful and stir until incorporated and smooth. Gravy will appear lumpy at first, but will become smooth after a few minutes of stirring and simmering. Adjust the quantity of milk or cashew butter as necessary for desired consistency.
# Taste and add salt if necessary.
# Serve gravy on [[Cookbook:Green Beans|green beans]] or other vegetables, or brown rice.

{{Recipe}}

'''Cassoulet''' (Pays D'OC ''caçolet'') is a speciality of the region of Languedoc and named after the clay stew-pot in which it is made. It is possibly related to cocido in Spain. Cocido is said to have originated from the Jewish and Muslim tradition  of preparing food the a day or two previously in order to rest on the Sabbath. The pork was reputedly substituted as demonstration of Christian fidelity after the "reconquest".

== Ingredients ==
* 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (about 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) dried white haricot/navy [[Cookbook:Beans|beans]]
* [[Cookbook:Cumin|Cumin]]
* 1 pig ear or [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] rind (optional)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] (about 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) mixture of [[Cookbook:Duck|duck]] or [[Cookbook:Goose|goose]] meat, Toulouse [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausages]] (strong garlic sausage), [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]], and/or [[Cookbook:Mutton|mutton]]
* Duck [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|fat]], goose fat, or [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* [[Cookbook:Stock|Stock]] or white [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]
* [[Cookbook:Bouquet Garni|Bouquet garni]]
* 1 head of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], peeled
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
* [[Cookbook:Clove|Cloves]]
* [[Cookbook:Juniper Berry|Juniper berries]]
* Water or [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]]

== Procedure ==
#[[Cookbook:Blanching|Blanch]] the beans for a few minutes by immersing them in plenty of [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]] water for a few minutes and then into cold water seasoned with cumin. 
#Drain the beans and reserve.
# [[Cookbook:Searing|Sear]] the meat in a [[Cookbook:Skillet|pan]] with duck or goose fat—brown only the outside. Remove the meat and reserve.
# [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] or [[Cookbook:Stir-frying|stir-fry]] the onion in the same pan until golden or dark brown, then set aside.
# Drain and discard any residual fat from the pan. [[Cookbook:Deglazing|Deglaze]] the dark residue in the pan using stock or white wine. Reserve the deglazing liquid.
# In a [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|casserole dish]], pan, or pot, layer beans, meat, cooked onion, garlic cloves, bouquet garni, and juniper berries. Add the deglazing liquid then enough boiling salted water to cover the beans by about an inch.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at 90 °C (195°F) for about 4½ hours. If necessary, add additional boiling water during the baking. When a light crust has formed and the beans have absorbed all the water and become tender, the preparation is done.
# Let stand for about 1 hour before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* If kept cool, cassoulet may be reheated next day, but thereafter is likely to go sour.
* The meats used can also include confits of pork, cheap canned pork, pig's trotters, cured sausages, and/or green bacon.

{{Recipe}}

This recipe originates from Ida Geller Weiner (1912–2008), of New Haven CT, who made it Thanksgiving and other family gatherings.

==Ingredients==

*1.5 [[Cookbook:Pound|lbs]] (1.25 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] / about 4–5 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]].) [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]]
* 1¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*½ tsp [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
*½ tsp [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]]
*1 cup [[Cookbook:Shortening|shortening]], [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], or [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Egg Yolk|egg yolks]]
*⅓ cup [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
*1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] juice
*½ tsp [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Egg White|egg whites]]

==Procedure==

#Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 325 °F (150 °C).
#Cook carrots until soft, then drain and [[Cookbook:Mashing|mash]] them. Set aside.
#[[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] together flour, salt, baking powder, and baking soda.
#[[Cookbook:Creaming|Cream]] together shortening and egg yolks.
#[[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] in brown sugar, cold water, lemon juice, and vanilla until well-mixed. Stir in mashed carrots, then dry ingredients.
#[[Cookbook:Whipping|Whip]] the egg whites until stiff, then [[Cookbook:Folding|fold]] into carrot batter.
#Transfer batter to a well-greased ring mold (with a bottom).
#Place a large shallow pan with about an [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] of water in the preheated oven, and place the pudding in the pan.  
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 1 hour. Unmold onto a serving plate while still somewhat warm.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If needed, you can substitute baby carrots for the regular carrots.
* If desired, you can add other chopped vegetable (peas, chopped string beans, etc).
* If you can't make a water bath, just bake without it.

{{recipe}} 
[[Category:Recipes using chicken]]
[[Category:Chinese recipes]]
'''Crispy fried chicken''' is a Hong Kong/Cantonese specialty.

== Ingredients ==

=== Pepper salt ===
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tbsp|Tbsp]] salt
* 3 Tbsp [[Cookbook:Szechuan Pepper|Sichuan peppercorns]] (花椒)
* 1 Tbsp [[Cookbook:Ajinomoto|ajinomoto]] seasoning (味の素)

=== Chicken ===
* 1 whole [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] (small)
* 2 Tbsp Chinese [[Cookbook:Five Spice Powder|five-spice powder]] (五香粉)
* 3 slices of [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]], crushed
* 2 [[Cookbook:Green Onion|scallions]]
* Water to poach chicken in

=== Glaze ===
* 3 Tbsp [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]

=== For Frying ===
* 4 cups [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|oil]] (or enough for deep fryer)
* Prawn crackers/shrimp chips (not the ready made ones)

== Procedure ==

=== Pepper salt ===
#Put salt and peppercorns in a small [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|pan]]. Heat on medium to low heat until it barely smokes. 
#Remove from heat.
#Grind well in [[Cookbook:Mortar and Pestle|mortar and pestle]], or with a [[Cookbook:Rolling Pin|rolling pin]].
#Add ajinomoto and mix well.
===Poaching===
These steps can be done in advance, and the chicken can be kept in the refrigerator.
#Clean and rinse off chicken, discarding the giblets.
#Heat enough water to cover the chicken in a pot until [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]].
#Put five-spice powder, ginger, and scallions in a cloth and tie it. Add to water, and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 15 minutes.
#Add chicken, reduce heat, and gently [[cookbook:poaching|poach]] for 20 minutes.
#When chicken is done, remove from heat, then pat dry with [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towels]] and air dry for a little bit.
#Put vinegar and sugar in [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], and heat until dissolved to make a [[Cookbook:Syrup|syrup]]. 
#Coat the entire chicken on the inside and outside with the syrup.
#Let chicken dry in a breeze until very dry.

===Frying===
#Fill deep fryer with oil, and heat oil to 350°F (175°C).
#[[Cookbook:Deep Fat Frying|Deep fry]] chicken about 10 minutes per side until brown and done. 
#Remove from oil, and chop with a meat cleaver into 1 x 2-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] pieces.
#When chicken is done, fry the shrimp chips in deep fryer.
#Sprinkle shrimp chips with a little salt.
#Serve chicken adorned with shrimp chips, with pepper salt in a small dish on the side.
== Notes, tips, and variations ==
#[[Cookbook:Poaching|Poaching]] is not the same as boiling, since the temperature is lower, about {{convert|160|-|180|F|C}} instead of at {{convert|212|F|C}}, and is even lower than simmering. If boiled, the meat will come out tough and dry. Also the lower the poaching temperature, the longer it will take to poach.
#Drying the skin is important, since it helps the syrup to stick. The second drying also is important, since that is what helps to make skin crispy. It can be done the day before, and the chicken kept in the fridge.
#The caramelized sugar gives the nice brown color. Vinegar lowers the pH, and helps the caramelization.
#Oil temperature is important, since it imparts the brown color to the skin. If the oil temperature is too low, the sugar will not caramelize, and the chicken will not be brown. If it is too high, the sugar will burn. If you don't have a temperature controlled fryer, use a frying (or candy) thermometer.
#A deep fryer can hold 2 or 3 liters of oil. Use as much as your deep fryer manual dictates.
#If you don't have a deep fryer, it can be fried on the stove in a pot or wok with a fry thermometer, but be very careful. '''WARNING:''' A wok can easily tip, spilling oil and giving severe burns. If the oil overflows, one can easily have a very dangerous oil fire. Please read warnings in the article on [[Cookbook:Deep Fat Frying]]

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (450 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) dry [[Cookbook:Pinto Bean|pinto beans]]
*8 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] ground black [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*1 ham bone or a rough equivalent of salt bacon
*1–2 [[Cookbook:Bay leaf|bay leaves]]
*5 cups [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
*A very small amount (3 oz / ~90 g) of that day's brewed [[Cookbook:Coffee|coffee]] (optional)

==Procedure==
#Wash beans carefully and [[Cookbook:Soaking Beans|soak]] overnight in 8 cups of water.  
#Drain and refill with 5 cups of water.  
#Add all the other ingredients. 
#Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] at least 1 hour, or until tender.  
#Remove bay leaves.  
#Do not drain prior to serving, the liquid is an important aspect of the dish.
#Can be served using slotted spoon, to allow draining, or with a ladle into small side-dish bowls   

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* The beans and the liquid can be ladled on to dry, stored cornbread (which, otherwise, can be exceptionally dry for eating purposes). The combination is very traditional.

'''Butter chicken''' is a Cape Malay dish.

==Ingredients==
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Yoghurt|yoghurt]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Ginger Garlic Paste|ginger/garlic paste]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]]
* 1 tablespoon crushed [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|black pepper]]
* 1 tablespoon [[Cookbook:White Pepper|white pepper]]
* ¼ tablespoon powdered tuj ([[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]])
* ¼ tablespoon powdered elachi ([[Cookbook:Cardamom|cardamom]])
* ¼ tablespoon powdered [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]]
* 1 ½ tablespoon freshly pounded red [[Cookbook:Chiles|chillies]]
* 1 tablespoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Chicken|chickens]] (split in halves)
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 1 can (1 cup) tomato purée
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]]
* Fresh [[Cookbook:Mint|mint]] sprigs

==Procedure==

# Mix yoghurt, oil, ginger/garlic paste, half the lemon juice, and spices together. Smear this mixture over the chicken halves and allow to marinate for a few hours.
# [[Cookbook:Grilling|Grill]] chicken over live coals or rotisserie until browned. Alternatively, lightly [[Cookbook:Pan frying|pan-fry]] and cook them.
# Combine butter, tomato purée, and the remaining lemon juice. Mix in the leftover marinade from the chicken. Bring this mixture to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for a few minutes. Remove from the heat, and stir in the cream.
# Place the chicken on a platter, and spread the sauce over top. [[Cookbook:Garnish|Garnish]] with mint sprigs, and serve hot.

'''Caprese salad''' is a delicious Italian dish made with [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]] and [[Cookbook:Mozzarella Cheese|mozzarella]] cheese. It is quite simple but tastes great and looks attractive.

# Cut a horizontal slit halfway through each slice.
# Put a basil leaf on top of each one.
# Sprinkle herbs over each slice.

# Eat fresh.

{{Recipe}}

'''Cauliflower rice''' is a rice alternative that contains fewer calories and fewer carbohydrates. Riced cauliflower can be prepared the same way as regular brown and white rice: stir-fried, steamed, boiled, or otherwise cooked.

== Ingredients ==

* White [[Cookbook:Cauliflower|cauliflower]]
* [[Cookbook:Vinegar|Vinegar]]
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* White [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]

== Procedure ==

# Use a knife to remove the cauliflower's green leaves.
# Submerge the cauliflower head in water with vinegar. Soak for 5 minutes to 1 hour. Drain the cauliflower and dry well.
# Use a [[Cookbook:Grater|grater]] with medium-sized holes to grate the cauliflower into rice-like bits. 
# Heat 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] vegetable oil in a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]]. Add the riced cauliflower, and stir continuously for 3 minutes over low heat. This gives the cauliflower rice a texture similar to regular rice and helps to lessen the amount of water in it.
# Add a dash of salt and some white pepper, then cover and cook for 1 minute.
# Remove from the heat, season, and use as desired.

| Yield = 6 cups
| Time = 30–60 minutes
| Difficulty = 3

{{Recipe}}

To create the texture of '''caramel sauce''', you need a 1:1 ratio of fat and liquid. In this recipe, heavy cream (40% fat) is used along with butter to create this ratio. If you want to substitute milk you will need to use less milk and more butter to keep the ratio. You can also substitute soy-milk and margarine to make a vegan caramel sauce, but make sure to keep the fat:liquid ratio.

You can easily halve this recipe if you wish. If it is sealed in clean canning jars, the sauce can be stored for 3 months without refrigeration. Or, store refrigerated for up to 6 months.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] water
* 4 cups white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Corn Syrup|corn syrup]] (optional)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2 cups heavy [[Cookbook:Cream|whipping cream]]
* ½ cup (1 stick) unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], chopped into 1-inch cubes

== Procedure ==

# Dissolve the water, sugar and corn syrup in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] over medium-high heat until fully dissolved.
# <u>Stop stirring</u> and let the solution [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] over medium heat. Check on the solution every 5 minutes. You will see the bubbles slow down and get larger. When the bubbles begin to reach ½–¾ inch in size, start monitoring the solution carefully.
# When the solution begins to turn amber, get your cream and butter and watch it constantly.
# When the solution has turned a shade of [[Cookbook:Caramel|caramel]] that you like (darker is deeper and will start to take on a little bitterness), step back and add the cream at arms length, stirring constantly and scraping the sides of the pan.
# Add the butter and stir until incorporated. Pour the sauce into a serving dish for immediate serving with bread, drizzled on [[Cookbook:Ice Cream|ice cream]], as a garnish or for use in other desserts.
# If you desire, follow standard canning procedures and distribute into canning jars. Allow to cool until the buttons are depressed. Any jars with buttons that are not depressed should be refrigerated and consumed first. To reheat the caramel sauce, [[Cookbook:Microwave|microwave]] the jars (without covers) for 10–30 seconds depending how soft and hot you want it.

File:Caramel added cream th.jpg|Stirring in the cream

File:Caramel filled jars th.jpg|Caramel stored in jars
</gallery>

== Variations ==
The following are all variations that can be made at different stages of the recipe above.

* '''Caramel chews:''' Replace the cream with ¾ cup [[Cookbook:Half and Half|half-and-half]]. Pour the finished hot caramel mixture onto a silicone mat or [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment paper]] to cool. When it is cool enough to handle, fold and [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] the caramel a few times, then break into bite size pieces. Allow to cool completely before wrapping individually.
* '''Turtles''': Replace the cream with ¾ cup [[Cookbook:Half and Half|half-and-half]]. Pour the finished hot caramel mixture over 4 cups of your favorite nut on a silicone mat or [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment paper]] to cool. When it is cool enough to handle, fold and [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] the caramel until the nuts are fully distributed, then break into bite size pieces. Melt chocolate over a [[Cookbook:Double Boiler|double boiler]] or in the [[Cookbook:Microwave|microwave]] and dip the turtles or simply drizzle chocolate on top.
* '''Toffee''': Instead of cream, use 7 sticks of butter (a total of 8 sticks or 4 cups, so you have equal parts butter and sugar). Mix in chopped nuts if desired, and pour the finished hot caramel mixture onto a silicone mat, [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment paper]], or molds. Once cool, drizzle or dip with chocolate and chopped nuts.
* '''Nut brittle''': Do not use any cream or butter. Stir ½ tsp baking soda into the caramel mixture, then pour the molten caramel over 4 cups of your favorite nuts on a silicone mat or parchment paper and let it cool. When it has reached room temperature, break it up with a mallet or by dropping the sheet on the counter. Wrap and store in an air-tight container.
* '''Sugar art''': You can do this at any point during the hard crack or caramel stages. Remove the sugar from the heat and allow to cool for one minute. Using a spoon, let the syrup drip off. If it drips in globs, let it cool longer. If it drips in a continuous stream, you can start making art. Drizzle the syrup in patterns over a silicone mat or parchment paper and allow to cool, then carefully peel off. Or, spray bowls and other (clean) objects with cooking spray and drizzle the syrup to create domes and other shapes. Allow to cool to room temperature, then serve soon or store in an air tight container. These will eventually soften and droop from [[wikipedia:humidity|humidity]] in the air.

== Safety ==
* Adding liquid to sugar that is over 300°F is dangerous! Some of the liquid will immediately flash to super-hot steam. To avoid steam burns, stay back from the pot and pour liquids at arms length. Use an oven mitt for your hand.
* When you add your liquid to the hot sugar it will boil violently. To avoid messy and dangerous boil-overs, a 2.5 quart heavy bottomed sauce pan or pot is the minimum, but 3-4 quarts is recommended
* Use a heat proof [[wikipedia:spatula|spatula]] or spoon such as wood or [[wikipedia:silicone|silicone]].

{{Recipe}}

'''Chadian grilled fish''' is a popular dish in Chad known for its simplicity and flavorful taste. Fresh fish is marinated with local spices, then grilled to perfection, resulting in a delicious and aromatic meal. It is often served with a side of rice or millet for a complete and satisfying experience.

== Ingredients ==

* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] ground [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]]
* 1 teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
* 1 teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* 1 teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]]
* 1 teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* Freshly ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]], to taste
* 2 whole fresh [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]] (such as [[Cookbook:Tilapia|tilapia]] or [[Cookbook:Catfish|catfish]]), cleaned and scaled
* [[Cookbook:Lemon|Lemon]] wedges, for serving

== Equipment ==

* [[Cookbook:Grill|Grill]]
* [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|Mixing bowl]]
* Basting [[Cookbook:Brush|brush]]
* [[Cookbook:Tongs|Tongs]] or [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]]
* [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|Aluminum foil]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|Paper towels]]

== Procedure ==

# Preheat your grill or barbecue to medium-high heat.
# In a mixing bowl, combine the vegetable oil, paprika, ginger, garlic, cumin, coriander, salt, and black pepper. Mix well to form a smooth [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinade]].
# Pat dry the fish with paper towels and place them on a plate or tray. Using a basting brush, generously coat both sides of the fish with the marinade. Make sure to cover the fish thoroughly for maximum flavor.
# If desired, you can let the fish marinate in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes to allow the flavors to penetrate. However, this step is optional, and you can proceed directly to grilling if you're short on time.
# Once the grill is heated, lightly oil the grates to prevent sticking. You use a folded paper towel soaked in vegetable oil and held with tongs to do so.
# Carefully place the marinated fish on the grill and close the lid. Cook for about 4–5 minutes per side, depending on the thickness of the fish, or until the flesh is opaque and easily flakes with a fork. While grilling, you can [[Cookbook:Basting|baste]] the fish with any remaining marinade using a basting brush for added flavor and moisture.
# Once the fish is cooked through and nicely charred, remove from the grill using tongs or a spatula. Be careful not to break the delicate flesh.
# Serve hot with lemon wedges on the side for squeezing over the fish. It pairs well with a side of rice or millet and can be accompanied by a fresh salad or steamed vegetables.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Cooking times may vary depending on the size and thickness of the fish, as well as the heat of your grill. Adjust accordingly to ensure the fish is cooked to your desired doneness.
* If desired, you can place the fish on a sheet of aluminum foil on the grill to prevent direct contact with the grates and facilitate easier flipping.

{{Recipe}}

'''Chadian salad''' is a colorful and flavorful [[Cookbook:Salad|salad]] that combines fresh vegetables with a zesty dressing. It is a healthy and refreshing dish, perfect for hot summer days or as a side dish to accompany grilled meats or fish.

== Ingredients ==

* 2 [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cucumber|cucumber]], diced
* 1 red [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], thinly [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]] (any color), diced
* 1 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]], juiced
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]] to taste
* Fresh [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]] or [[Cookbook:Mint|mint]] leaves, chopped (optional, for garnish)

== Equipment ==

* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* Mixing bowl
* [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] or fork
* [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|Plastic wrap]]

== Procedure ==

# Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, red onion, and carrot in a mixing bowl.
# In a separate small bowl, whisk together the lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper to make a dressing. Adjust the seasoning according to your taste.
# Pour the dressing over the vegetables in the mixing bowl. Gently [[Cookbook:Mixing#Tossing|toss]] the salad to ensure all the vegetables are coated with the dressing.
# Cover the mixing bowl with plastic wrap or a lid and let the salad marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. This allows the flavors to blend together and enhances the taste.
# Remove the salad from the refrigerator. Give it a final toss to mix the flavors, and transfer it to a serving dish. If desired, sprinkle chopped parsley or mint leaves on top as a [[Cookbook:Garnish|garnish]].
# Enjoy as a standalone dish or as a side salad alongside grilled meats, fish, or other main courses.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Feel free to customize the salad by adding or substituting vegetables according to your preference and availability. You can also add a touch of heat by including chopped chili peppers or a sprinkle of paprika.

It is easy to make once the carrot is blended smoothly.

== Ingredients ==
*4 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Psyllium|psyllium]] husk powder or [[Cookbook:Xanthan Gum|xanthan gum]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]

== Special equipment ==
*[[Cookbook:Blender|Blender]]
*[[Cookbook:Cheesecloth|Cheesecloth]]

== Procedure ==
#Blend the chopped carrot until smooth.
#Transfer the carrot to the cheesecloth, and squeeze out all the water from the carrot paste.
#Cook the carrot paste in a pot over medium heat for 5 minutes.
#Stir in the psyllium husk to thicken and bind the fufu.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
*The function of the psyllium husk is to make the carrot fufu moldable, and this give it the texture of [[Cookbook:Eba|eba]].
*Cut or scrape off any dark marks on the carrot.

{{Recipe}}

'''Chakalaka''' is a spicy South African vegetable relish made from beans, peppers, carrots, and tomatoes. It is often served as a side dish with bread, pap (maize porridge), or meat. Chakalaka is versatile and can be customized with various vegetables and spices depending on regional or personal preference.
== Ingredients ==

*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|oil]], or as needed
*3 medium [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Curry Powder|curry powder,]] or to taste
*1 teaspoon [[Cookbook: Chile Powder|chile powder]]
*2 small Thai green [[Cookbook:Chiles|chiles]], chopped
*3 medium [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]], diced
*3 medium [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], diced
*2 medium green [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell peppers]], diced
*¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
*1 cube vegetable [[Cookbook:Dehydrated Broth|bouillon]], crumbled
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] and ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]] to taste

== Equipment ==

* Large [[Cookbook: Saucepan|saucepan]] or [[Cookbook: Dutch Oven|Dutch oven]]
* [[Cookbook: Cooking Spoon|Cooking Spoon]]
* [[Cookbook:Cooktop|Stove]] or Cooking gas

==Procedure==

# Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
# Add the chopped onions and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] for 2–3 minutes until softened.
# Stir in the curry powder, chile powder, and chopped chile peppers. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
# Add the chopped tomatoes, grated carrots, and diced bell peppers. Stir well.
# Add the crumbled bouillon cube and water. Cover and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 10–15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
# Stir in the baked beans and cook for an additional 3–5 minutes, uncovered, until the mixture thickens.
# Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Chakalaka can be made ahead of time and tastes even better the next day.
* Grated [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]] or [[Cookbook:Green Bean|green beans]] can be added for extra variety.
* It can be served hot or cold, depending on preference.

'''Carrot cookies''' are soft cookies with an orange-flavored icing.  They get their golden color from pureed carrots, but they taste like oranges instead of carrots.  

This recipe is adapted from the "Golden Carrot Cookies" recipe in Betty Crocker's ''Cooky Book''.

== Ingredients ==

== Equipment ==

* [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|Mixing bowl]]
* [[Cookbook:Mixer#Stand mixer|Stand mixer]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|Baking sheet]]

== Procedure ==

=== Make the cookies ===
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven Temperatures|400 °F (205°C, gas mark 6—moderately hot)]]. Line baking sheets with parchment baking paper, or lightly grease the pans with shortening.
# Put the butter in a large mixing bowl, and [[Cookbook:Beat|beat]] it with an electric mixer for about 30 seconds. Alternatively, beat it with a wooden spoon until soft.
# Beat in the sugar, scraping the bowl as needed.
# Beat in the eggs, vanilla extract, and orange extract.
# Stir in the carrots, then the flour, salt, and baking powder.
# Stir in the coconut.
# Drop the cookie dough by rounded teaspoonfuls on the prepared baking sheets. Space them out, as they will spread somewhat while baking.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in the preheated oven for 8–10 minutes, until they are golden in color and no imprint remains when you gently touch them.
# Cool slightly on the pan, then remove from the pan and cool completely.

=== Make the icing ===

# Using an electric mixer or a wooden spoon, beat together the butter and powdered sugar.
# Stir in the orange juice, zest, and extract to make a smooth, soft buttercream icing.
# Spread gently on the tops of cooled cookies. If the icing is too stiff, the cookies will break when you try to frost them—thin it by adding a small spoonful of water, or warm it slightly to make it softer.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If you want a solid, uniform color for the cookies, then the carrots should be pureed (smooth like baby food). If you want visible streaks of orange, then shred the carrots on a grater.
* You can use [[Cookbook:Gluten-Free Flour|gluten-free flour substitutes]]. Avoid high-gluten bread flours.
* You can replace up to half the sugar with a sugar substitute.
* This recipe can be halved or doubled easily.
* The dough is soft enough to pipe through a large pastry bag, which may be faster than scooping when making larger batches.
* Store at room temperature or in the refrigerator for a few days.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Pakistan|Pakistani Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Flatbread|Flatbread]] | [[Cookbook:African cuisines|African cuisines]] | [[Cookbook:Vegan_cuisine|Vegan Cuisine]]

The '''chapati''', also known as a '''roti''', is the staple flat bread of Northern [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|India]] and [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Pakistan|Pakistan]]. It can be made from many types of grain, but is most commonly made with finely-ground [[Cookbook:Whole Wheat|whole wheat flour]]. Sometimes it is cooked in a little oil.

==Ingredients==
* 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Whole Wheat|whole wheat flour]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste (about 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]])
* Warm water as required (about 1 ½ cups)
* [[Cookbook:Clarified Butter|Ghee]] (clarified butter; optional)

==Procedure==
# [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] together the flour and water, starting with only a slight dribble of water and adding more as you go until the [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] becomes smooth but not too sticky.
# Cover dough, and let rest for at least 5 minutes.
# Divide dough into balls and [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|roll out]] into disks, slightly thicker than denim material; sprinkle with flour as you roll.
# Place a non-oiled [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|pan]] over moderately high heat and test its surface temperature by holding your hand over it.
# When very hot, put a chapati on the pan and press it flat with a [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]] or dry cloth to make it rise up.
# Flip and repeat so it becomes lightly browned on both sides.
# If desired, [[Cookbook:Brush|brush]] with ghee.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* Regional variations abound in the detail of preparing and cooking roti. In most Indian cooking, for example, the roti is finished by toasting it in the open flame of the cooker. The aim of this process is to encourage the roti to puff up. The hot air which builds inside because the water inside the roti begins to turn into steam and cooks the roti inside out. This may also be achieved under a grill, or by using a microwave (try 30 seconds on high power). Universally, however, the aim in rolling is to get the roti to a perfectly round shape (for aesthetics) and to create uniform thickness, which is vital for successful cooking.
* There are Caribbean-specific variations of roti, one of which uses boiled and ground yellow split peas in its preparation.
* Chapatis are usually eaten with cooked dal (lentil soup) or vegetable dishes like Indian curry. Pieces of the chapati are used to wrap and lift bites of the other dishes.

These little confections are great one-per-afternoon snacks. They are dense and will give you a euphoric high on sweets but make you want to go work out after.

==Ingredients==

*1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (450 g) [[Cookbook:Cream Cheese|cream cheese]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Eggs|eggs]]
*¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (180 g) granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*Semi-sweet [[cookbook:chocolate chips|chocolate chips]]

==Equipment==
*[[Cookbook:Cupcake Liner|Cupcake papers]]
*[[Cookbook:Cupcake Pan|Cupcake pan]]
*[[cookbook:Microwave Oven|Microwave oven]]
*[[Cookbook:Oven|Oven]]
*[[cookbook:Mixing bowl|Mixing bowl]]
*[[cookbook:Double boiler|Double boiler]] (optional)

==Procedure==

#Preheat your [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven Temperatures|350°F]] (180°C).
#Soften the cream cheese in the [[Cookbook:Microwave Oven|microwave]] in a bowl. Thirty seconds on a medium setting should be sufficient.

'''Cherry brownies''' are a rich [[Cookbook:Brownies|brownie]] with no frosting, a fudge-like base, and a [[Cookbook:Cheesecake|cheesecake]]-like top, filled with maraschino cherries and chocolate chips.

== Ingredients ==

=== Base ===
* 2 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (100 g) [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (2.4 [[Cookbook:Deciliter|dl]]) white granulated [[Cookbook:sugar|sugar]]
* 6 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (0.6 dl) [[Cookbook:Cocoa|cocoa]]
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (1.8 dl) [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

=== Topping ===
* 4 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] (110 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) softened [[cookbook:Cream Cheese|cream cheese]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (0.6 dl) [[Cookbook:Maraschino Cherry|maraschino cherry]] syrup
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (0.6 dl) [[cookbook:icing sugar|icing sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (1.2 dl) semi-sweet [[cookbook:Chocolate chip|chocolate chips]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (1.2 dl) [[cookbook:Cherry|maraschino cherries]]

== Procedure ==

=== Base ===
# Melt margarine in a [[cookbook:saucepan|saucepan]] over medium-low heat, then mix in the cocoa.
# Add the sugar, salt, and eggs. Mix well and then [[cookbook:fold|fold]] in the flour.
# Spread in a greased 9 x 9-inch (22 x 22 cm) [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|cake pan]] and set aside.

=== Topping ===
# [[cookbook:Beat|Beat]] the cream cheese, cherry syrup and icing sugar together in a bowl until creamy.
# Add the egg to the mixture and blend well.
# Mix in the chocolate chips and cherries.
# Pour the second mixture over top the base.

=== Baking ===
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at 350 °F/175 °C for 30–40 minutes, until a [[Cookbook:Toothpick|toothpick]] poked through the centre comes out moist (but not wet with batter).
#  Let cool and cut into 36 squares.

== Notes, tips and variations ==

* Cool for at least 10 minutes before cutting and eating or you will have hot broken brownies.

'''Pães de queijo''' are Brazilian cheese puffs made of tapioca. They are similar to gougères and are typically served at breakfast or as a snack.

==Ingredients==

* ⅔ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (160 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* ⅓ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (80 ml) neutral [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]] (e.g. [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]])
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (450 g) fine [[Cookbook:Manioc Flour|cassava flour]] or [[Cookbook:Tapioca Starch|tapioca flour]]
* 6 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] (170 g) [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]] hard [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]] (a mix of [[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|cheddar]] and [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|parmesan]] is good)
* 2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]] to taste

==Procedure==
#Mix the milk and oil together in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], and [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] until a white foam appears.
#Gradually add flour to this hot mixture; mix well to form a firm [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] with no lumps.
#Let the dough rest for 15 minutes.
#Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 375°F (190°C).
#Mix the eggs, cheese, salt, and pepper into the dough. The dough will become sticky and wet. If the dough is too wet, add more flour and cheese in order to make firmer balls (instead of cookies).
#Grease your hands, and form small balls 1–2 inches in diameter.
#Place the balls on a greased [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking tray]]. [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 15–20 minutes, until the top begins to brown.
#Cool slightly.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Ensure you use a fine flour, and not the coarser grain type of flour used to make ''farofa''. This recipe should produce small cheesy bread rolls, so a finer flour consistency is required.
* An egg substitute like Egg Beaters is fine.

'''Cheese sauce''' is a variation of [[Cookbook:Béchamel Sauce|Béchamel Sauce]].

== Ingredients ==
* 2½ [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 1½ tablespoons [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Heavy Cream|heavy whipping cream]] or ½ cup whole [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]], hot
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Cream Cheese|cream cheese]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]] [[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|cheddar cheese]]
* ⅓ cup grated [[Cookbook:Mozzarella Cheese|mozzarella cheese]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]] (optional)
* 1½–2 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinches]] of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

== Procedure ==
# Melt the butter in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]. Add the flour and [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] together over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, to make a white [[Cookbook:Roux|roux]]. Do not allow to brown. Remove from heat and allow to cool nearly to room temperature.
# Gradually add hot heavy whipping cream to the roux, whisking to combine. This will also work with a hot roux and room temperature heavy cream or milk.
# Add the salt, cheese, and mustard, then heat till just [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmering]] and cheese has melted.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* If desired, you may bring the sauce to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]; once the cheese sauce has come to a boil, lower the heat to low and very slowly simmer for about 45 minutes. Stir it every so often to avoid sticking to the bottom (a whisk is appropriate here). 
* Do not allow the sauce to brown. 
* The longer the sauce is simmered, the smoother it becomes due to the cooking and swelling of the starch grains.

Cooking: 20 minutes|difficulty=3 }} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Meat Recipes|Meat Recipes]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of China|China]] '''Cha shao''' is a kind of spiced Cantonese honey roast [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]]. It is often also called by the Cantonese '''char siu''' or '''char siew'''. Sometimes (usually in America) it is called '''Chinese BBQ pork'''. It is very popular, and can be eaten by itself (usually cold), or used as an ingredient for other dishes such as cha shao bao (pork buns), or in [[Cookbook:Noodle|noodles]] or [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]. The pork used should be quite fatty in order to keep the meat moist during cooking. Pork shoulder is a good choice. The meat is traditionally hung to cook, as this allows it to cook from all sides in the very hot oven. It can be laid on a rack, but if possible hang from metal S-hooks on a high rack, which are easily and cheaply available from hardware stores. [[Cookbook:Sherry|Sherry]] can be used instead of Shaoxing wine (also called Shao Hsing wine), but it does not provide quite the same flavour. Since this dish requires a reasonably large amount of time and preparation, even while cooking (frequent basting is needed), it is easiest to make it in large batches. The recipe here makes 1 kg, which is enough for several different dishes. It can be kept in the fridge for several days or frozen until required. ==Ingredients== * 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] (2.25 [[Cookbook:Pound|lbs]]) [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] shoulder * 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] dark [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]] * 2 tbsp light soy sauce * 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Oyster sauce|oyster sauce]] * 2 tbsp Shaoxing rice [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]] * 2 tbsp clear [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]] * 4 tbsp [[Cookbook:Hoisin Sauce|hoisin sauce]] * ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Five Spice Powder|five spice]] ==Procedure== #[[Cookbook:Slicing|Slice]] the meat into strips about 1 [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] (2.5 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]) wide by 6 inches (15 cm) long. A long thin strip like this will keep its shape better when hanging. #Pierce the pork all over thoroughly with a fork. This makes the pork more tender and allows the marinade to penetrate the meat to give flavour all the way through. #Mix all other ingredients together to make a marinade. #Place pork strips in a tray and cover with marinade. Ensure strips are covered completely in marinade. #Cover tightly with [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|cling film]] and place in the refrigerator for several hours (8–24 hours is preferable). #Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 230°C or 420°F and place a pan in the bottom to catch drippings. Line this pan with [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|aluminium foil]] to make cleaning easier. #Hang the meat on hooks in the oven or lay them on a rack. Depending on the method and the size of your oven, it may be easiest to do this in two or three batches, rather than all at once. #[[Cookbook:Roasting|Roast]] for 20 minutes, until pork is cooked all the way through. [[Cookbook:Basting|Baste]] at least twice to build up a good layer of marinade on the outside of the meat. The pork should turn a golden-red colour as it cooks. #Allow to cool while still hanging, or lay on wire rack to cool.
