{{recipe}}
[[Category:Recipes using chicken]]
A '''locrio''' is a common Dominican dish similar to [[Cookbook:Paella|paella]]. Like paella, there are many variations. The main point is to have a little tomato sauce/paste for coloring, and some caramelized sugar. In that way it is similar to the Trinidadian pilau. Like paella, the rice at the bottom should be toasted or browned, but not burnt. This browned rice is called "concon". You're not considered a good cook until you can do this.

== Ingredients ==
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|oil]] for frying 
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*4 [[Cookbook:Pound|lbs]] (1.8 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]]) [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], cut in pieces
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Olive|olives]] (pitted) or [[Cookbook:Caper|capers]]
* 2 tbsp oil, for when rice is almost done
* ½ cup finely [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]]
* ½ cup finely diced [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 4 cups [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
* 5¼ cups chicken [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]] or water
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] or to taste
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]]
* ½ tsp [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]] (optional)
* 1 tsp ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]

== Procedure ==

=== Stovetop method ===
#Heat the ¼ cup oil in a pot over high heat.
#Add the sugar to the pot. Let it melt and [[Cookbook:Caramelization|caramelize]], turning light brown. Pay close attention and don't let the sugar burn. Do not use plastic utensils to stir the sugar, since it will be at around 350°F (175°C).
#Add the meat to the caramel and let it brown on all sides. Remove and reserve the meat.
#Add the garlic, onions, and celery to the pot. [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]].
#Add rice and cooked meat to pot with the vegetables. [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] together chicken stock and tomato paste until smooth, then stir it into the rice mixture. Stir in the salt, pepper, thyme, and olives.
#Check the seasoning. If the salt level is good, add an extra ½ tsp of salt. This is because the rice will absorb some of the salt, and it will come out a bit flat in the end unless you add extra salt.
#Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] over high heat. Let it boil, stirring occasionally, until the water is absorbed. The high heat is needed to bring the rice temperature up so that it cooks. If you lower the flame at this point, the rice might not cook all the way.
#Cover, lower the heat, and let it cook for 15 minutes.
#Uncover, sprinkle 2 Tbsp oil on top, and stir so that the uncooked rice on top goes to the bottom. Cook for another 5 minutes.
#If rice still not cooked, give it another stir and cook for another 5 minutes. Sometimes you may need more time; see notes below.
#Turn heat on high for a couple of minutes to brown and toast the rice on bottom. Sometimes it does this by itself during the main cooking so you don't have to do this. Experience will tell.
#Serve.

=== Oven method ===
#Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 350°F (125°C).
#Proceed with the recipe as above, using an oven-proof pot, until the rice absorbs all the liquid. Once this happens, cover the pot, put it in the oven, and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] for 30 minutes. 
#Add 2 tbsp oil, and stir so the uncooked rice is on the bottom and the bottom rice is on the top. Bake for another 20 minutes.
#Stir. If it is still not fully cooked, bake another 20 minutes.
#Serve.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
*If the rice doesn't cook but all the water was absorbed, you can separate the rice from the meat, put it in a bowl, and give it 5 minutes on high in the [[Cookbook:Microwave|microwave]]. Often there wasn't enough heat to cook the rice. On some stoves, once covered (as mentioned above), you may have to cook 20 minutes, add oil, stir, and cook another 20–40 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes.
*It is also helpful to put a sheet or two of [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|aluminium foil]] over the pot before putting the lid on. That helps seal the lid and keep the heat/steam from escaping, and the rice often comes out better. 
*Dominicans tend to cook the rice on the dry side—the rice will be cooked through, but not too watery. The ratio should be 4 cups rice to 5½ cups liquid (some locrio recipes ask for 7–8 cups of liquid, which makes things mushy). If you have tomato sauce instead of tomato paste, you can use that also, as long as the ratios are the same (e.g. 1 cup tomato sauce to 4½ cups water/stock; which makes a total of 5½ cups liquid). If you halve the recipe, the ratio rice to liquid will be 2 cups rice to 2¾ cups liquid.
*Some people deep fry the meat separately, remove the excess oil, and then caramelize the sugar.
*The ingredients of the sofrito vary, and can be made in advance. Some add [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]], [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell peppers]], [[Cookbook:Culantro|culantro]], and other aromatics to it.
*Other vegetables such as 1 cup of cubed auyama squash are sometimes added with the rice.
*You can also substitute guineafowl, [[Cookbook:Rabbit|rabbit]], Dominican [[Cookbook:Salami|salami]], [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] chops, or other meat for the chicken. Almost any meat can be used, including cubed [[Cookbook:Ham|ham]] or spam, arrenque (smoked dried herring, pre-soaked in warm water to remove some salt, but cut the amount of salt you use), canned sardines, Vienna sausages, shellfish (mariscos) and if in desperation, ground beef, meatballs, hot dogs, etc. can also be used. You can use 2 lbs of chicken gizzards also, but gizzards need to be boiled (or pressure cooked) until tender first. 
*Some people use Sazón Completo for the seasoning. Although it is not authentic, you can also add 1 tsp ajinomoto (味の素), which is similar.
*You can take the skin off the chicken before frying it.
*Instead of chicken stock, some people throw in a stock cube.

*1½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] dried [[Cookbook:Lentil|lentils]], picked through
*3–4 cups water or [[Cookbook:Stock|vegetable stock]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Garlic Salt|garlic salt]]
*1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
*1 medium to large [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], finely [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
*1 stalk [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]], finely diced
*2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]] [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
*4 tbsp dried [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]
*1–2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Worcestershire Sauce|Worcestershire sauce]]
*2 whole [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
*¼–1 cup plain or Italian [[Cookbook:Bread Crumb|bread crumbs]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
*[[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]] to taste

==Preparation==
#Place the lentils in a large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], and add water or stock so that it covers the lentils by at least 2 [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]] (check the cooking instructions for the type of lentil you are using, as some may require soaking before cooking).
#Cook for the approximate time as suggested by the lentil package (usually 30–45 minutes at a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]).
#Place the cooked lentils into a fine [[Cookbook:Sieve|sieve]] and allow to drain and cool.
#Sauté the carrot and celery in the butter and oil over medium heat until softened (about 10 minutes).
#Just before the carrot and celery are done, add the dried onion and parsley.
#Place the drained and cooled lentils in a large bowl, add the carrot mixture, and mash everything with a potato masher. Don't over-mash; it is fine to leave some of the lentils whole.
#Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
#Add the eggs and about ¼ cup bread crumbs, and stir to combine all the ingredients. Continue to add bread crumbs until you have a slightly moist but not wet mixture.
#Form mixture into patties. Place the formed patties onto a plate and layer with waxed paper in between. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
#To cook, it is best to use either a large [[Cookbook:Sauté Pan|sauté pan]] or a griddle on the [[Cookbook:Grilling|grill]]—these burgers don't do well on grill grates. Cook over medium to medium-high heat until warmed through and a nice crust has formed on the outside. Depending on the thickness of the burgers, this will take anywhere from 3–7 minutes per side.
#To serve, you can place on a bun with the usual accoutrements or go crazy with whatever you think will go (garlic aioli, roasted peppers, etc). You could also serve without the bun with grilled [[Cookbook:Pineapple|pineapple]], barbecue sauce, etc—the choices are endless.

{{Recipe}}| [[Cookbook:tea|Tea]] 

A '''Long Island iced tea''' is a mixed cocktail originating in the [[Wikipedia:Prohibition|prohibition era]] and made popular in New York speakeasies. Despite its name, the drink does not contain any tea whatsoever.

== Ingredients ==
* ¼ part [[Cookbook:Vodka|vodka]]
* ¼ part white [[Cookbook:Rum|rum]]
* ¼ part [[Cookbook:Gin|gin]]
* ¼ part [[Cookbook:Tequila|tequila]] or [[Cookbook:Triple Sec|triple sec]]
* 1 part sweet and sour mix OR [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]/[[Cookbook:Lime|lime]] juice to taste
* 1 splash [[Cookbook:Cola|cola]] or [[Cookbook:Coffee Liqueur|coffee liqueur]]
* Lemon, [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] for garnish

== Procedure ==

=== Shaken method ===
# Shake all the ingredients except the cola with ice in a cocktail shaker.
# [[Cookbook:Straining|Strain]] into a highball glass.
# Float the cola on the top and serve with a lemon slice.

=== Stirred method ===
# Fill a highball glass until it's almost full with ice.
# Add vodka, gin, rum, and tequila.
# Add sweet and sour mix, leaving some room on top.
# Splash in the cola and enjoy.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Don't forget—it has to look like an iced tea, so don't add too much cola.
* To make a '''Long Beach Tea''', use [[Cookbook:Cranberry|cranberry]] juice instead of cola.

== Ingredients ==
* about 6 medium [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemons]], juiced to yield 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (250 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]/8.5 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) juice
* 3¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (850 ml/29 oz) [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* ¾ cup superfine [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] (160 g/5.6 oz)

== Procedure ==
# Juice the lemons on a citrus reamer. Rolling the lemons on the counter with moderate pressure prior to juicing will result in more juice from each lemon. Try to keep out the seeds. If you prefer lemonade with no pulp, strain the juice to remove it.
# Dissolve the sugar in the water. Heat may be helpful if using a large amount of sugar.
# Combine the juice and sugar water in a pitcher. Stir well.
# Chill or serve over ice cubes.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* The sugar can be adjusted by ± ¼ cup (55 g/1.9 oz).

{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian chicken gravy''' is a delicious African [[Cookbook:Stew|stew]]. A lot of oil is required to cook most African stews, but when it comes to this dish, you don't need so much.

== Ingredients ==

* 3 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], cut into medium pieces
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* Ground red or black [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]] to taste
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] chicken [[Cookbook:Dehydrated Broth|bouillon cube]]
* 2 medium-size [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], neatly [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 4 fresh [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
* 4 medium-size red [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]]
* 5 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]] and [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* 2 lb any type of dried [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]] steak of your choice, cleaned
* Smoked [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]] (optional)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]] powder
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|cayenne pepper]]
* 2 medium-size habanero [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]], neatly chopped
*1 pound large [[Cookbook:Shrimp|shrimp]], cleaned 

== Procedure ==

# In a medium-size [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] the chicken with salt, pepper, some chopped onions, and 1 tablespoon of the chicken bouillon. Let them cook until tender—the cooking time varies according to the chicken.
# Remove the chicken to a bowl, reserving the stock.
# In a blender, purée the tomatoes, red bell pepper, onions, garlic, basil, and parsley.
# Add ½ cup oil to a pot, then add the blended mixture followed by the tomato paste. Allow it to cook for about 15 minutes, stirring the pot frequently as the sauce simmers.f
# Add the reserved chicken broth, then the chicken, dried fish, smoked paprika, ginger powder, cayenne pepper, and habanero pepper. Let simmer for about 10 minutes.
# Add the shrimp and cook for about 5 minutes.
# Adjust the stew with water, broth, and/or bouillon cubes if needed.
# Enjoy with any complimentary dish of your choice.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* It is not compulsory to use fish when preparing this stew.
* You can use any variety of tomatoes such as canned tomatoes, fresh tomatoes, or Roma tomatoes.
* Use any range of vegetables such as [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], green [[Cookbook:Beans|beans]].
* You can also make use of extra spices such as [[Cookbook:Curry Powder|curry powder]], [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]], and [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaves]] as desired.

{{recipe}}

This dish is popularly eaten in Liberia.

== Ingredients ==

* 48 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] dried [[Cookbook:Beans|beans]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] vegetable [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]]
* 2 medium size [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], neatly [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 22 oz [[Cookbook:Seitan|seitan]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Habanero|habanero pepper]], neatly chopped
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Palm Oil|palm oil]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Potash|country soda]] or 2 pinches of [[Cookbook:Baking soda|baking soda]], dissolved in warm water
* 1 teaspoon of [[Cookbook:salt|salt]] or to taste

== Procedure ==

# Pick over the beans and remove any unwanted ones. You may [[Cookbook:Soaking Beans|soak]] them overnight to reduce the cooking period. Place beans in a pot and cover with water. [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] until tender, adding water if needed.
# Drain and mash the beans to your preferred consistency.
# Bring the vegetable broth to a boil in a separate pot. Stir in the mashed beans along with the onions, 1 cup water, seitan, and habanero pepper. Boil for about 20–25 minutes.
# Stir in the palm oil. Reduce to low heat and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for about 5 minutes, stirring to prevent burning.
# Stir in the potash and salt to taste.
# Remove from the heat and let rest for about 5 minutes.
# Enjoy with any complimentary dish of your choice such as bread, rice, or garri.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If you are using baking soda, the stew will foam.
* You can prepare the torborgee with any type of beans, including kidney beans, pinto beans and cranberry beans.

{{Recipe}}

== Ingredients ==

* 2 large [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] breasts, cut into cubes
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Chiles|Chile]] powder to taste
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
* 1 large sweet [[Cookbook:Onions|onions]], neatly [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiled]] [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] or [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]], cut into cubes
* 2 bags of frozen mixed [[Cookbook:Vegetable|vegetables]] (such as sweet [[Cookbook:Corn|corn]], string beans, etc), thawed and drained
* 2 medium-size cans of [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* 4 chicken [[Cookbook:Dehydrated Broth|bouillon cubes]], crushed
* 3 pounds steamed [[Cookbook:Shrimp|shrimp]] (optional)
* 2 cups [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]]
* 5 cups [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]], rinsed

== Procedure ==

# Season the chicken with salt and red pepper. Leave it to stand for about 5 minutes.
# In a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]], brown the chicken in hot vegetable oil. Then transfer the chicken to a large pot.
# In the same frying pan, add the onions and beef or pork. Fry lightly and add to the pot with the chicken.
# Combine the mixed vegetables, tomato paste, bouillon cubes, salt to taste, shrimp, and bell pepper. Leave to simmer for about 10 minutes.
# Add the rice, stir well, and cook over low heat for about 40–45 minutes.
# Serve hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Ingredients for this recipe vary between people. Some people might use shrimp, [[Cookbook:Curry Powder|curry powder]], or even [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]] to prepare it—it just depends on what you like and what you want to see in your food.
* For the [[Cookbook:Vegetable|vegetables]] you can make use of any okay by you (e.g. spring onions, red beans, etc)

{{Recipe}}

This is an easy and delicious dish popularly cooked in West Africa.

== Ingredients ==

*3 large bunches of sweet potato greens (see notes)
*[[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]]
*2 big [[Cookbook:Onions|onions]], neatly [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lbs]] meat, cut into medium cubes
*Seasoned [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] to taste
*[[Cookbook:Onion Powder|Onion powder]] to taste
*Chicken [[Cookbook:Dehydrated Broth|bouillon cubes]], crushed
*Ground red or black [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]] to taste

== Procedure ==

# Wash the potato greens very well, and remove the leaves from the stems. [[Cookbook:Chopping|Chop]] the leaves into small pieces and set aside.
# Heat a few tablespoons of oil in a large pot. Add the onions and meat, and cook until almost done. Remove from the pot and set aside.
# Add the potato greens, and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] for about 15 minutes or until tender. Stir frequently to prevent burning.
# Add enough water to cover the greens, and season to taste with salt, onion powder, bouillon cubes, and ground pepper.
# Cook over medium heat until all the water is gone, stirring frequently.
# Remove from the heat and serve.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Do not eat '''white potato''' greens—they are toxic. Sweet potato greens, however, are safe. You can get potato greens from the market or from local farmers.
* If desired, add a pinch of baking soda to the greens when cooking to keep their green color.

{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian palm oil stew''' is a delicious and hearty dish from Liberia. Made with a rich combination of palm oil, vegetables, and protein, this stew is a staple in Liberian cuisine and is often served with rice or fufu.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Palm Oil|palm oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook: Pepper|green bell pepper]], [[Cookbook:Knife Skills|diced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook: Pepper|red bell pepper]], diced
* 1 Scotch bonnet [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile pepper]], finely chopped (optional, for spiciness)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], cut into pieces
* 2 cups [[Cookbook:Broth|chicken broth]]
* 1 pound [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]], cut into steaks or fillets
* ½ pound [[Cookbook:Okra|okra]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplant]], diced
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Ground black pepper]], to taste

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]
* Large [[Cookbook: Stock Pot|pot]]
* [[Cookbook: Wooden Spoon|Wooden spoon]]

== Procedure ==
# In a large pot, heat the palm oil over medium heat.
# Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot. [[Cookbook:Sauté|Sauté]] until the onion becomes translucent and fragrant.
# Stir in the diced green and red bell peppers and chopped Scotch bonnet pepper (if using). Cook for a few minutes until the peppers start to soften.
# Add the chicken pieces to the pot and cook until they are lightly browned on all sides.
# Pour in the chicken broth and bring the mixture to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]]. Cover the pot and let the chicken cook for about 20–25 minutes, or until it is fully cooked and tender.
# Once the chicken is cooked, add the fish steaks or fillets to the pot and let them simmer in the stew for an additional 5–10 minutes, or until they are cooked through.
# Stir in the sliced okra and diced eggplant. Let the stew simmer for another 5–7 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender.
# Season the stew with salt and ground black pepper to taste. Adjust the seasoning according to your preference.
# Remove the pot from the heat and let the stew rest for a few minutes before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Palm oil gives the stew its distinctive flavor and vibrant red color. It is a traditional ingredient in Liberian cuisine and can be found in specialty African grocery stores.
* For a spicier version, you can add more Scotch bonnet pepper or a pinch of [[Cookbook:Cayenne pepper|cayenne pepper]] to the stew.
* This stew is traditionally served with rice or [[Cookbook:Fufu|fufu]], a starchy side dish made from cassava or other root vegetables.

{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian pepper soup''' is a flavorful and spicy soup from Liberia. It is a popular dish that is often enjoyed as a warming and comforting meal, especially during cold weather or when feeling under the weather.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Palm Oil|palm oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]], grated
* 2 Scotch bonnet [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile peppers]], finely chopped
* 1 [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaf]]
* 1 pound [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], cut into pieces
* 4–5 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] chicken [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]]
* 1 pound [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]], cut into steaks or fillets
* 1 [[Cookbook:Plantain|plantain]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], sliced
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Ground black pepper]], to taste

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]
* Large pot
* Wooden spoon

== Procedure ==
# In a large pot, heat the palm oil over medium heat.
# Add the chopped onion, minced garlic, and grated ginger to the pot. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] until the onion becomes translucent and fragrant.
# Stir in the chopped Scotch bonnet peppers and bay leaf. Cook for a few minutes to release the flavors.
# Add the chicken pieces to the pot and cook until they are lightly browned on all sides.
# Pour in the chicken broth and bring the mixture to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]]. Cover the pot and let the chicken cook for about 20–25 minutes, or until it is fully cooked and tender.
# Once the chicken is cooked, add the fish steaks or fillets to the pot and let them simmer in the soup for an additional 5–10 minutes, or until they are cooked through.
# Stir in the sliced plantain and carrot. Let the soup simmer for another 5–7 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender.
# Season the soup with salt and ground black pepper to taste. Adjust the seasoning according to your preference and desired level of spiciness.
# Remove the pot from the heat and let the soup rest for a few minutes before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Liberian pepper soup is traditionally served with rice, [[Cookbook:Swallow|fufu]], or other starchy side dishes.
* For a milder version, you can reduce the amount of Scotch bonnet peppers used or remove the seeds before chopping them.
* You can also add other vegetables such as bell peppers, spinach, or cabbage to the soup for added flavor and nutrition.

== Nutrition ==
* This soup is a good source of protein from the chicken and fish, as well as vitamins and minerals from the vegetables and spices.

{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian cassava leaf soup''' is a delicious and hearty dish that is widely enjoyed in Liberia. Made with cassava leaves, meat, and an assortment of vegetables, this soup is a flavorful and nutritious meal that is perfect for gatherings and special occasions.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] [[Cookbook:Cassava|cassava leaves]], fresh or frozen
* 1 pound [[Cookbook:Meat|meat]] ([[Cookbook:Beef|beef]], [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], or [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]]), cut into bite-sized pieces
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2–3 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 piece of [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]], [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]]
* 2–3 Scotch bonnet [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile peppers]], finely chopped
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Palm Oil|palm oil]]
* 4–5 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Chicken Broth|chicken broth]] or water
* 1 [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potato]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Plantain|plantain]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
* [[Cookbook:Black pepper|Ground black pepper]], to taste

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]
* Large pot
* Wooden spoon

== Procedure ==
# If using fresh cassava leaves, wash them thoroughly and remove any tough stems. If using frozen cassava leaves, thaw them according to the package instructions.
# In a large pot, heat the palm oil over medium heat.
# Add the chopped onion, minced garlic, and grated ginger to the pot. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] until the onion becomes translucent and fragrant.
# Stir in the chopped Scotch bonnet peppers and cook for a few minutes to release the flavors.
# Add the meat to the pot and cook until it is browned on all sides.
# Pour in the chicken broth or water and bring the mixture to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]]. Cover the pot and let the meat cook for about 20–25 minutes, or until it is tender.
# Add the diced sweet potato and sliced plantain to the pot. Let the soup simmer for another 10–15 minutes, or until the vegetables are cooked through.
# Stir in the cassava leaves and let the soup simmer for an additional 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
# Season the soup with salt and ground black pepper to taste. Adjust the seasoning according to your preference.
# Remove the pot from the heat and let the soup rest for a few minutes before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Cassava leaves can be found in African or international grocery stores. If unavailable, you can substitute with spinach or other leafy greens, but the taste will be different.
* The longer the cassava leaf soup cooks, the more flavorful it becomes. It is traditionally simmered for several hours to develop its rich taste.
* This soup is often served with rice or [[Cookbook:Fufu|fufu]], a starchy side dish made from cassava, plantains, or other ingredients.
* Cassava leaves are a good source of vitamins A and C, as well as calcium and iron.
* The meat and vegetables in the soup provide protein, vitamins, and minerals.

{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian fried fish''' is a popular and delicious dish in Liberia. Made with fresh fish and a flavorful spice blend, this dish is crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, making it a delightful meal for seafood lovers.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] fresh [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]] ([[Cookbook:Tilapia|tilapia]], snapper, or any firm white fish)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|ground black pepper]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Garlic powder|garlic powder]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Onion powder|onion powder]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cayenne pepper|cayenne pepper]] (optional)
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Buttermilk|buttermilk]]
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]], for frying

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]
* Large bowl
* Deep [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] or pot
* [[Cookbook:Tongs|Tongs]] or slotted spoon
* [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|Paper towels]]

== Procedure ==
# Clean and gut the fish, removing any scales and innards. Rinse the fish thoroughly under cold running water and pat them dry with paper towels.
# In a large bowl, mix the all-purpose flour, salt, ground black pepper, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and cayenne pepper (if using).
# Pour the buttermilk into another bowl.
# Dip each fish into the buttermilk, allowing any excess to drip off, and then coat the fish with the seasoned flour mixture, pressing the flour onto the fish to adhere.
# Heat about 1 inch of vegetable oil in a deep frying pan or pot over medium-high heat. To test if the oil is hot enough, drop a small piece of bread into the oil; it should sizzle and turn golden brown.
# Carefully place the coated fish in the hot oil, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding the pan.
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] the fish for about 3–4 minutes per side, or until they are golden brown and cooked through. Use tongs or a slotted spoon to flip the fish during frying.
# Remove the fried fish from the oil and place them on a plate lined with paper towels to drain any excess oil.
# Serve the fish hot, with your favorite side dishes like plantains, rice, or salad.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* You can adjust the level of spiciness by increasing or decreasing the amount of cayenne pepper in the seasoning mixture.

* Leftover fried fish can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. To reheat, place the fish in the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] at 350°F (175°C) for a few minutes until warmed through.
* Fish is a rich source of protein and essential omega-3 fatty acids.

{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian fufu''' is a staple food in Liberia and many other West African countries. It is made from starchy vegetables like cassava, yams, or plantains, which are boiled, pounded, and formed into a smooth, dough-like consistency. Fufu is typically served with various soups and stews, making it a versatile and satisfying dish.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] [[Cookbook:Cassava|cassava]], [[Cookbook:Yam|yams]], or [[Cookbook:Plantain|plantains]]
* Water

== Equipment ==
* Large pot
* Potato [[Cookbook:Masher|masher]] or [[Cookbook:Mortar and Pestle|pestle and mortar]]

== Procedure ==
# Peel and cut the cassava, yams, or plantains into chunks, and place them in a large pot.
# Add enough water to cover the vegetables, and bring the pot to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] over high heat.
# Reduce the heat to medium and let the vegetables [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] until they are tender and easily pierced with a fork.
# Drain the water from the cooked vegetables, and transfer them to a large bowl.
# Use a potato masher, or mortar and pestle to pound the vegetables into a smooth, thick paste. You can also use a stand [[Cookbook:Mixer|mixer]] or [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]] for this step.
# Continue pounding and kneading the mixture until it forms a smooth and stretchy dough-like consistency. This process may take some time and effort, but it is essential for achieving the right texture.
# Once the fufu has reached the desired consistency, shape it into small balls or serve it as a large mound on a serving platter.
# Serve with various soups and stews. It can be used as a utensil to scoop up the soup or stew.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* To enhance the flavor, you can add a pinch of salt or other seasonings to the cooked vegetables before pounding.
* Some people prefer their fufu to be softer, while others prefer it to be firmer. Adjust the amount of pounding and kneading to achieve your desired texture.
* Leftover fufu can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. To reheat, steam it or place it in a [[Cookbook:Microwave|microwave]] for a few minutes until warmed through.
* Fufu is naturally gluten-free and can be enjoyed by those with gluten sensitivities.

{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian fried plantains with beans''' is a popular and delicious dish in Liberia. It combines the sweet and savory flavors of [[Cookbook:Plantain|ripe plantains]] with the heartiness of cooked [[Cookbook:Beans|beans]]. This dish can be served as a main course or as a side dish, and it's perfect for any occasion.

== Ingredients ==
* 3 [[Cookbook:Plantain|ripe plantains]]
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]], for frying
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] cooked [[Cookbook:Beans|beans]] (black-eyed peas or kidney beans)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] ground [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]]
* ½ teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Black pepper|black pepper]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
== Equipment ==
* Large [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]]
* Slotted spoon

== Procedure ==
# Peel the ripe plantains and cut them into diagonal slices, about ½ inch thick.
# In a large frying pan, heat vegetable oil over medium-high heat.
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] the plantain slices in batches until they are golden brown and crispy on both sides. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the fried plantains to a plate lined with paper towels to drain any excess oil.
# In the same frying pan, [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] the chopped onion and minced garlic until they become translucent and fragrant.
# Add the cooked beans to the pan and mix well with the onions and garlic.
# Season the beans with ground paprika, ground black pepper, and [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] to taste. Stir to coat the beans evenly with the spices.
# Cook the bean mixture for a few minutes until it is heated through.
# Serve the fried plantains alongside the seasoned beans and enjoy this delightful and flavorful Liberian dish.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Adjust the seasoning according to your taste preferences. You can add other spices like cayenne pepper or thyme for extra flavor.
* If you prefer a sweeter taste, you can sprinkle a little [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]] on the fried plantains before serving.
* This dish can be served as a main course with rice or as a side dish with grilled or fried fish or meat.
* Leftover fried plantains and beans can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat before serving.
* Beans are rich in protein, dietary fiber, and various nutrients such as iron and folate.

'''Liberian collard green stew''' is a hearty and flavorful dish that is a staple in Liberian cuisine. Made with tender collard greens and a rich tomato-based sauce, this stew is both nutritious and delicious. It can be served as a main course with rice or bread, and it's perfect for sharing with family and friends.

== Ingredients ==
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 1 red [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]], diced
* 1 green bell pepper, diced
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Paprika|ground paprika]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|ground cayenne pepper]] (optional, for heat)
* 1 bunch of fresh [[Cookbook:Collard Greens|collard greens]], washed and chopped
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Broth|vegetable broth]] (or water)

== Equipment ==
* Large pot
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]

== Procedure ==
# In a large pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat.
# Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] until the onion becomes translucent and the garlic becomes fragrant.
# Stir in the diced tomato, red bell pepper, and green bell pepper. Cook for a few minutes until the vegetables are softened.
# Add the chopped collard greens to the pot and mix well with the sautéed vegetables.
# Season the stew with ground paprika, ground cayenne pepper (if using), and salt to taste. Stir to coat the collard greens and vegetables with the spices.
# Pour in the vegetable broth (or water) to the pot, ensuring that the collard greens are well covered.
# Cover the pot and let the [[Cookbook:Stew|stew]] simmer on low heat for about 30–40 minutes, or until the collard greens are tender and flavorful.
# Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed, adding more salt or spices according to your preference.
# Serve as a main dish with rice or bread, and enjoy.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* You can add other vegetables like [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]] or [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potatoes]] to the stew for extra flavor and nutrition.
* For a richer taste, you can add some [[Cookbook:Coconut Milk|coconut milk]] to the stew during cooking.
* Leftover stew can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat before serving.

== Nutrition ==
* Collard greens are a good source of vitamins A, C, and K, as well as calcium and iron.
* The variety of vegetables in this stew provides a range of vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber.

{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian butter rice''' is a flavorful and comforting dish that is a popular staple in Liberian cuisine. Made with aromatic ingredients and cooked in butter, this rice dish has a rich and delicious taste that pairs well with a variety of proteins and vegetables. It's a versatile side dish that can be served on its own or as an accompaniment to other Liberian dishes.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] long-grain [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
* 4 cups [[Cookbook:Broth|chicken broth]] (or vegetable broth)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Bay leaf|bay leaf]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
* [[Cookbook:Black pepper|Black pepper]], to taste
* Fresh [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]] or [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]], chopped (for garnish)

== Equipment ==
* Large pot with a lid
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]

== Procedure ==
# Rinse the rice thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear. Drain the rice and set it aside.
# In a large pot, melt the butter over medium heat.
# Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] until the onion becomes translucent and the garlic becomes fragrant.
# Stir in the drained rice and coat it well with the buttery mixture.
# Pour in the broth and add the bay leaf to the pot. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir well.
# Bring the mixture to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], then reduce the heat to low. Cover the pot with the lid and let the rice [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for about 15–20 minutes, or until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is cooked and fluffy.
# Remove the pot from the heat and let the rice rest for a few minutes before fluffing it with a fork.
# [[Cookbook:Garnish|Garnish]] with chopped fresh parsley or cilantro before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* For a richer taste, you can use chicken broth instead of vegetable broth.
* You can add some diced vegetables like [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]] or [[Cookbook:Pea|peas]] to the rice for extra flavor and color.
* Leftover rice can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat before serving.
* Liberian butter rice complements various proteins and vegetables, making it a versatile and tasty addition to your meals.

{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian fried sweet potato puffs''' are delightful and flavorful snacks that make a perfect treat for any occasion. Made with mashed sweet potatoes, these puffs are seasoned with a blend of spices and herbs, giving them a unique taste that will keep you coming back for more. They are fried to golden perfection, creating a crispy exterior with a soft and creamy interior.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 large [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potatoes]], [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiled]] and mashed
* 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]], lightly beaten
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Baking powder|baking powder]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Black pepper|black pepper]]
* ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|ground cinnamon]]
* ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|ground nutmeg]]
* ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]]
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil,]] for frying

== Equipment ==
* Large pot or [[Cookbook:Deep Fryer|deep-fryer]]
* [[Cookbook:Mixing bowl|Mixing bowl]]
* [[Cookbook:Potato Masher|Potato masher]] or fork
* Slotted spoon
* [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|Paper towels]]

== Procedure ==
# In a large mixing bowl, combine the mashed [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potatoes]] with the beaten [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]].
# In a separate bowl, whisk together the [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]], [[Cookbook:Baking powder|baking powder]], [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]], [[Cookbook:Black pepper|black pepper]], [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|ground cinnamon]], [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|ground nutmeg]], and cloves.
# Gradually add the dry ingredients to the sweet potato mixture, stirring until well combined.
# Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or deep-fryer to 350°F (175°C).
# Using a spoon or cookie scoop, carefully drop spoonfuls of the sweet potato mixture into the hot oil.
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] the sweet potato puffs in batches for about 3–4 minutes or until they are golden brown and crispy.
# Remove the fried puffs from the oil using a slotted spoon, and place them on a plate lined with paper towels to drain any excess oil.
# Serve warm as a snack or appetizer.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* You can adjust the seasoning according to your taste preferences. Add more spices or herbs for a bolder flavor.
* These sweet potato puffs can be served with your favorite dipping sauce, such as [[Cookbook:Ketchup|ketchup]] or aioli.

{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian roasted corn''' is a simple and delicious street food that captures the essence of Liberia's culinary delights. This delightful treat is made by roasting fresh corn over an open flame until it develops a smoky and charred flavor. Liberians often enjoy roasted corn as a snack or side dish, especially during gatherings or festivals.

== Ingredients ==
* Fresh [[Cookbook:Corn|corn]] on the cob

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Grilling|Grill]] or open flame (charcoal grill, gas grill, or campfire)

== Procedure ==
# Preheat the grill or set up an open flame (charcoal grill, gas grill, or campfire).
# Remove the husks and silk from the fresh corn on the cob, leaving the base intact for easy handling.
# Place the corn on the grill or directly over the open flame.
# Rotating the corn occasionally to ensure even cooking and prevent burning, roast the corn for about 10–15 minutes or until the kernels are tender and have developed a slightly charred appearance.
# Once the corn is roasted to your desired level, remove it from the grill or flame.
# Serve hot and enjoy as a flavorful snack or side dish.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* For added flavor, you can [[Cookbook:Brush|brush]] the corn with [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or oil before roasting. Some Liberians also sprinkle [[Cookbook:Chili Powder|chili powder]] or other spices on the roasted corn for extra kick.
* Liberian roasted corn is often served with a variety of toppings, such as salt, pepper, or grated [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]].
* This recipe can also be made with corn still in the husks. Simply soak the corn in water for about 30 minutes before roasting to prevent the husks from catching fire.
* Liberian roasted corn is best enjoyed immediately after roasting while it is still warm and full of flavor.

{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian eggplant stew''' is a delectable dish that highlights the unique flavors of eggplant in Liberian cuisine. This hearty stew is made with tender eggplant, savory [[Cookbook:meat|meat]] or [[Cookbook:fish|fish]], and a medley of aromatic spices. It is a popular and comforting meal in Liberia, often served with [[Cookbook:rice|rice]] or [[Cookbook:fufu|fufu]].

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Palm Oil|palm oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 pound [[Cookbook:meat|meat]] ([[Cookbook:Beef|beef]], [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], or [[Cookbook:Goat|goat]]), cut into pieces, or [[Cookbook:fish|fish]] ([[Cookbook:Tilapia|tilapia]] or [[Cookbook:Catfish|catfish]]), cleaned and gutted
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Chicken Broth|chicken broth]] or water
* 1 [[Cookbook:tomato|tomato]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:bell pepper|bell pepper]], diced
* 1 [[Cookbook:Hot Pepper Sauce|hot pepper]], chopped (optional, for heat)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] ground [[Cookbook:pepper|pepper]]
* 2 large [[Cookbook:eggplant|eggplants]], peeled and diced
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste

== Equipment ==
* Large [[Cookbook: Stock Pot|pot]]
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]

== Procedure ==
# In a large pot, heat the palm oil over medium heat.
# Add the chopped onions and minced garlic to the pot. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] until the onions are soft and translucent.
# If using meat, add the meat pieces to the pot and cook until they are browned on all sides.
# Pour in the chicken broth or water and bring the mixture to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]].
# Add the diced tomato, bell pepper, and chopped hot pepper (if using) to the pot. Stir well to combine with the other ingredients.
# Gently add the diced eggplant to the pot and stir to incorporate with the other ingredients.
# Season the stew with ground pepper and salt to taste. Adjust the seasoning according to your preference.
# Let the stew simmer for about 20–25 minutes or until the eggplant is tender and cooked through.
# Stir occasionally during cooking to prevent sticking and to ensure even cooking.
# Remove the pot from the heat and let the stew rest for a few minutes before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* You can add other vegetables like [[Cookbook:carrot|carrots]], [[Cookbook:okra|okra]], or [[Cookbook:spinach|spinach]] to the stew for added nutrition and flavor.
* If using fish, be sure to remove any bones before adding it to the stew.
* This stew can be made with any type of meat or fish according to your preference.
* Liberian eggplant stew can be enjoyed as a standalone dish or served with [[Cookbook:rice|rice]], [[Cookbook:fufu|fufu]], or [[Cookbook:bread|bread]].
* Eggplant is a low-calorie vegetable and is a good source of fiber, vitamins, and minerals.

This is an alternative '''limoncello''' recipe.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Limoncello {{!}} Public Domain Recipes |url=https://publicdomainrecipes.com/limoncello/ |access-date=2024-12-04 |website=publicdomainrecipes.com}}</ref>

==Ingredients==

*5–7 unwaxed [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemons]]
*300 [[Cookbook:milliliter|ml]] 95% ABV grain [[Cookbook:alcohol|alcohol]]
*700 ml [[Cookbook:water|water]]
*500 ml [[Cookbook:sugar|sugar]]

==Equipment==

*1-liter [[Cookbook:Mason Jar|mason jar]]

==Procedure==

# Peel lemons, avoiding or removing the bitter white pith. 
# Combine lemon peel and alcohol in the mason jar.
# Cover the jar and let infuse for 20 days.
# After infusion is complete, create a [[Cookbook:simple syrup|simple syrup]] by boiling the water stirring in the sugar until dissolved.
# Allow syrup to cool completely, then [[Cookbook:Straining|strain]] the infused alcohol into it. Stir well to combine.
# Bottle the limoncello or return to the jar for storage.

==Notes, tips and variations==

* Feel free to scale the recipe up or down, and adjust the sugar to the sweetness you like, but the ABV should remain somewhere around 28–30%.

== Equipment ==

* [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|Mixing bowl]]
* [[Cookbook:Mixer#Stand mixer|Stand mixer]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|Cake pan]] or rimmed [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheet]] at least 1 inch (2.5 cm) deep – quarter sheet size (9x13 inches, 33 x 23 cm)

== Procedure ==
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven Temperatures|350 °F (175°C, gas mark 4—moderate)]].
# Put the butter in a large mixing bowl, and [[Cookbook:Beat|beat]] it with an electric mixer for about 30 seconds. Alternatively, beat it with a wooden spoon until soft.
# Beat in the sugar, cocoa, salt, cloves, and cinnamon, scraping the bowl as needed, until you have a smooth, dark mixture.
# Beat in the eggs.
# Stir in the flour and hazelnut flour. If the butter was cold when you started, this step may be difficult.
# Spread about three-quarters of the cookie dough in the baking pan, reserving the remaining quarter for the topping.
# Spread the fruit preserves evenly over the raw dough in the baking pan.
# Drop the remaining cookie dough by spoonfuls on top of the fruit preserves. If desired, these can be flattened using the back of a spoon, wet fingers, or the waxed paper wrappers from the butter.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in the preheated oven for about 35 minutes, until a wooden toothpick comes out clean.
# Cool in the pan. Cut into 32 bars (4x8 grid).

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* You can use gluten-free flour substitutes. Avoid high-gluten bread flours.
* You can replace up to half the sugar with a sugar substitute.
* You can substitute other kinds of nut flours/nut meal.
* If you halve the recipe, use one whole egg and one egg yolk. Bake in a 7x11-inch pan, an 8x8-inch square pan, or a 9-inch round pan.
* If desired, the bars can be decorated by sifting a small amount of [[Cookbook:Powdered Sugar|powdered sugar]] over the pan just before cutting them.
* Store at room temperature or in the refrigerator for a few days. Freeze for longer periods.

}}'''Lemon-lime soda''' is a carbonated beverage flavored similarly to lemon- and limeade. This recipe originates from Flavorlab.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-10-09 |title=Sprite |url=https://www.flavorlab.xyz/recipes/sprite |access-date=2025-11-17 |website=Flavor Lab |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Ingredients==
* 2 whole [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemons]], washed
* 4 whole [[Cookbook:Lime|limes]], washed
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (120 [[Cookbook:Liter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Sugar|white sugar]]
* 4 tsp (20 ml) lime [[Cookbook:Juice|juice]]
* [[Cookbook:Carbonated Water|Carbonated water]], as needed

==Procedure==
# Remove the zest from the lemons and limes in strips, leaving behind the bitter white pith.
# Combine the sugar and zest in a container, and let this sit in the fridge for 24 hours. The sugar will extract the liquid from the citrus peels and produce a syrupy liquid.
# [[Cookbook:Sieve|Strain]] the solids out of the peel and sugar mixture.
# Mix the peel and sugar mixture with lime juice. This should produce slightly under ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (120 ml) of [[Cookbook:Syrup|syrup]]. 
# To make the finished soda, mix 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of carbonated water.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Use water from a carbonating machine or a brand of pure carbonated water such as Polar Original Sparkling Water, Great Value Seltzer Water, or Signature Select Seltzer Water. Do not use a brand of mineral water such as Perrier, San Pellegrino, or Mineragua because the added minerals will ruin the taste. Avoid flavored sparkling water such as La Croix or Spindrift because the preexisting fruit flavors will ruin the drink.
* You can make a Shirley Temple by mixing five crushed frozen cherries with the zest and sugar or by adding a volume of [[Cookbook:Grenadine|grenadine]] syrup for every volume of lemon-lime syrup when making the finished soda.

* 6⅔ [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (200 mL) water
* 1½ cups (360 mL) [[Cookbook:Sugar|white sugar]]

== Procedure ==

# Combine the spirit or gum arabic water and oils together in a small cup, mixing well. Set aside.
# Transfer this mixture into a larger container. 
# Put the citric acid, water, and white sugar into the container. Stir well. 
# To make the finished soda, combine 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of carbonated water.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Use a clean eye dropper to measure drops. Do not use a pipette, an eye dropper previously used for dispensing medication, or a spoon to measure drops.
* Use water from a carbonating machine or a brand of pure carbonated water such as Polar Original Sparkling Water, Great Value Seltzer Water, or Signature Select Seltzer Water. Do not use a brand of mineral water such as Perrier, San Pellegrino, or Mineragua because the added minerals will ruin the taste. Avoid flavored sparkling water such as La Croix or Spindrift because the preexisting fruit flavors will ruin the drink.
* You can make a Shirley Temple by mixing five crushed frozen cherries with the zest and sugar or by adding a volume of [[Cookbook:Grenadine|grenadine]] syrup for every volume of lemon-lime syrup when making the finished soda.

==Procedure==
# In a large mixing bowl, mix the flour, salt, milk, eggs, baking powder, sugar, cinnamon, and vanilla.

'''Louis dressing''' is a salad dressing commonly used with [[Cookbook:Seafood|seafood]] salads, such as [[Cookbook:Crab Louis|Crab Louis]] and Shrimp Louis. It can also be used as a dip or sandwich spread, or many other uses. The dressing is creamy but has a little spicy kick. This is not the "traditional" recipe, but it is the easiest for untrained cooks to succeed at.

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (235 [[Cookbook:mL|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Mayonnaise|mayonnaise]]
*¼ cup (60 ml) cup mild [[Cookbook:Salsa|salsa]] with green [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile peppers]]
*¼ cup (60 ml) [[Cookbook:Ketchup|ketchup]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] (15 ml) [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]]
*1 ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] (7 ml) [[Cookbook:Worcestershire Sauce|worcestershire sauce]]
*[[Cookbook:Hot Sauce|Hot sauce]] (e.g., Tabasco, Crystal), to taste

==Procedure==
#Combine all ingredients in a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]], and process until smooth. The goal is to have a pink smooth sauce with little green flecks.
#Pour the sauce into a bowl, cover, and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes prior to use.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* For the traditional recipe, replace the salsa and ketchup with ½ cup [[Cookbook:Red Chile Sauce|chile sauce]] (or store-bought chile sauce), and 3 tablespoons each of finely-minced [[Cookbook:Green Onion|green onion]] and green [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|chili peppers]]. Instead of using a blender, [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] the ingredients in a bowl.
* Keep refrigerated.

==Ingredients==

*½ [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]

==Procedure==
#[[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] bacon in a pan until not too crisp; remove and reserve.
#[[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] onion and garlic in bacon fat until just softened (about 2–3 minutes).

#Add 1 cup shrimp stock, bring to a high [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]], and reduce. The liquid should thicken; if necessary, add floured butter at this point ([[Cookbook:Beurre Manié|beurre manié]]).
#Season sauce with salt, pepper, chili flakes, cayenne, and paprika
#Add bacon and shrimp to the sauce, and cook gently until shrimp are just done.
#Add lime juice.
#Serve over grits, and [[Cookbook:Garnish|garnish]] with scallions.

}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] | [[Cookbook:Cake|Cake]]

'''Mandarin orange cake''' is a common low-fat cake recipe with unique variations. The cake is simple to make and does not require you to start from scratch. All the ingredients can be found at grocery stores in the United States.  

== Ingredients ==

=== Cake ===
*  1 box (15 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] / 430 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) yellow [[Cookbook:Cake Mix|cake mix]]
*  1 can (11 oz / 312 g) mandarin oranges
*  3 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]

=== Icing ===
*  1 box (5.1 oz / 144 g) '''instant''' vanilla pudding mix
*  1 can (20 oz / 567 g) crushed [[Cookbook:Pineapple|pineapple]]
*  1 container (12 oz / 340 g) CoolWhip or other [[Cookbook:Imitation Whipped Topping|whipped topping]]

== Procedure ==

# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 350°F (180°C). Grease the sides and bottom of [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|cake pans]] with shortening, and [[Cookbook:Dusting|dust]] with flour.
# Pour yellow cake mix into mixing bowl. Add eggs and the mandarin oranges plus their juice. Blend until moistened, then beat for approximately 2 minutes at medium speed.
# Pour batter evenly into prepared baking pans. [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] approximately 30 minutes in the preheated oven or until a [[Cookbook:Skewer|toothpick]] inserted into the center comes out clean.
# Remove from oven and let the cakes cool completely.
# Scoop CoolWhip into a clean mixing bowl. Add the instant vanilla pudding mix. Drain all the pineapple juice from the can of crushed pineapples, and fold the pineapple into CoolWhip. Chill icing for about 30 minutes.
# After the cakes cool, frost each layer with your icing.

== Nutrition ==

* Each serving is approximately 275 calories with about 4–5 grams of fat.

| Difficulty = 4
| Image = [[File:Makizushi2.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}}

'''''Makizushi''''', also called '''rolled sushi''' or '''maki roll''', is a variety of [[Cookbook:Sushi|sushi]]. It is made by layering [[Cookbook:Nori|nori]], seasoned sushi rice, and fillings, before rolling up and slicing into individual pieces. The outer layer of the maki roll varies, having either nori or rice on the exterior—the latter is sometimes called an inside-out roll.

==Ingredients==

* Prepared [[Cookbook:Sushi/Sushi Rice|sushi rice]]
* Fillings, as desired (this may consist of either raw/smoked [[Cookbook:Salmon|salmon]], [[Cookbook:Tuna|tuna]], etc or perhaps [[Cookbook:Cucumber|cucumber]] or [[Cookbook:Avocado|avocado]])
* [[Cookbook:Nori|Nori]] sheets 
* [[Cookbook:Wasabi|Wasabi]] paste
* Water
* [[Cookbook:Sesame Seed|Sesame seeds]], if making inside-out rolls with rice on outside (optional)

== Equipment ==

* [[Cookbook:Sushi Roller|Sushi roller]] (''makisu'')
* [[Cookbook:Plastic wrap|Plastic wrap]], if making inside-out rolls

==Instructions==

#Place the roller on a cutting board. If making inside-out rolls with rice on the outside, wrap the roller in a double layer of [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|plastic wrap]] to prevent rice from sticking to the roller.
#Place a sheet of nori shiny side-down on top of the roller.
#Dampen your hands before applying the rice. Grab the rice with one hand and put a fistful on the center of the nori. Spread the rice over the nori approximately 6 [[Cookbook:Mm|mm]] thick, leaving a 2 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] gap on the side parallel to the bamboo. As a general rule, if you can't see the nori through the rice, you have too much.
#If making an inside out roll, flip over the nori and rice quickly onto the sushi roller. The rice should now be on on the surface of the plastic wrap, with the nori facing you.
#Place the primary ingredients in a row in the middle. Slowly use the roller to push the nori against itself (rolling it away from you), using your thumbs and heels of hands for stability. Be careful when you reach the row of ingredients, making sure that it goes underneath the roll rather than just being pushed along.
#When you reach the end of the nori sheet, use the roller to compact the roll a little, making sure the rice sticking it together. When evening out a bumpy roll, don't squeeze too hard on the sides and don't flatten the roll from the top.
#To fix the ends of the roll, poke about ½ inch out from one side of mat and while gently holding it in place, press it with the heel of your hand a little.
#Remove the maki from the sushi roller, and put it on the cutting board below.
#Wet a sharp knife before slicing. Slice the rolls from the center outwards, into sections of 5, 6, or 8 (depending on the roll and your preference). Cutting from the center first ensures that all ingredients will shift towards the outside two pieces. For the rolls of 6 or 8, cut from the center, then put one roll behind the other, and cut each half in half.
#If making an inside-out roll, you may garnish the exterior rice with sesame seeds.
#Serve with soy sauce for dipping. You may also want chopsticks, pickled ginger, and wasabi if culture allows. Sashimi, miso soup, other sushi, or just general Japanese food is also often served alongside it. Green tea is considered the drink of choice to have with sushi.
== Notes and tips ==

* Dampening the hands before handling the rice will prevent clumping and the rice sticking to your hands. However, too much moisture may also make the rice less sticky, so don't go overboard.

==Variations==
Common maki rolls include:
* '''California roll:''' [[Cookbook:Avocado|avocado]], [[Cookbook:Crab|crab]] meat or imitation crab, [[Cookbook:Cucumber|cucumber]].

* '''Tuna roll:''' [[Cookbook:Tuna|Tuna]], wrapped in [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] and [[Cookbook:Nori|seaweed]]. This same combination is used to make plain rolls with any other type of fish.

* '''Spicy tuna roll:''' [[Cookbook:Tuna|Tuna]], spicy sauce (mixture of Japanese [[Cookbook:Mayonnaise|mayonnaise]] and [[Cookbook:Sriracha|sriracha]])

* '''Kamikaze roll:''' [[Cookbook:Tuna|Tuna]], [[Cookbook:Yellowtail|yellowtail]], spicy sauce

* '''Philadelphia roll:''' [[Cookbook:Salmon|Salmon]] (either raw or smoked), [[Cookbook:Cream Cheese|cream cheese]]

* '''Cucumber roll:''' Sliced cucumber

* '''Egg roll:''' Sliced [[Cookbook:Egg Yolk|egg yolk]].

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Holiday Recipes|Holiday recipes]]

'''Lussekatter''' or '''luciabullar''' are Scandinavian saffron buns served on [[w:St. Lucia Day|St. Lucia Day]] (13 December).

==Ingredients==

*2 packages (4½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]]) active dry [[Cookbook:yeast|yeast]]
*¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] lukewarm water
*½ tsp crushed (¼ tsp powdered) [[Cookbook:saffron|saffron]] threads
*¾ cup (180 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Half and Half|half and half]], lukewarm
*½ cup (120 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) melted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], beaten
*¾ cup (180 g) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*4–5 cups sifted [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
*[[Cookbook:Raisin|Raisins]] to decorate

==Procedure==
#Combine the yeast and warm water.
#Mix saffron into the warm half and half and let stand.
#Combine the yeast and saffron mixtures. Mix in the melted butter, eggs, sugar, and salt.
#Mix half of flour into the wet mixture and beat until well-blended.
#Mix in additional flour until [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] is smooth but not too firm. [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] on floured surface for ten minutes.
#Place dough in buttered bowl and let rise about 1½ hours or until doubled in volume.
#Divide the dough into multiple pieces. Roll each piece into a 7 inch-long snake, and form into an 'S' shape with the ends curled in. Place a raisin in each curl.
#Place buns on buttered [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|sheet pan]], cover, and let rise 45 minutes. 
#[[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] with beaten egg and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] at 375–400°F (190–200°C) for 10–15 minutes until golden and cooked through.

'''Kombdi vade''' is a Malvani dish, which is quite popular in Maharashtra. The dish consists of the traditional Malvani [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] curry (including chicken pieces with bones), vade (also known as puri, which is a fluffy, fried bread of wheat and nachni flour), onion, lemon and solkadhi (a drink made from coconut milk).

==Ingredients==
*8 [[Cookbook:Green chilly|green chillies]], chopped
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]] paste
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] paste
*800 [[Cookbook:g|g]] (1.8 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] / 8 ea.) medium-sized pieces of [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|oil]]
*1 fresh [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]], flesh [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]]
*4 [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:chilli|chilli powder]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsps]] [[Cookbook:Garam Masala|garam masala]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsps]] Malvani Special Masala
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
*Finely-chopped [[Cookbook:Cilantro|coriander leaves]] for garnishing

==Procedure==
#Grind half of the green chillies to a paste and mix it well with the ginger and garlic pastes. 
#Make cuts on the chicken pieces, rub this mixture on to them well, and [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinate]] for about an hour at least.
#Toast coconut shavings in a pan with a little hot oil until light brown. Cool and grind along with half the onions to a paste.
#Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] the onions on medium level for about 2 minute(s) or until they are light brown in color.
#Add the remaining chopped green chillies and spice powders and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] for a few seconds. Add the marinated chicken pieces and fry on medium level for about 3 minutes or until they are lightly browned.
#Add the paste and salt, then mix well. Add water according to the desired level of consistency and bring to a boil. Cover and cook on low level for about 25 minute(s) or until the chicken pieces are tender and fully cooked.
#[[Cookbook:Garnish|Garnish]] with finely-chopped coriander leaves. 

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* If it is difficult to obtain fresh coconut, it can be replaced by desiccated coconut shavings. For this recipe, there is no need to soak it in warm water. Roast it directly.

Callimachus called these "honey tokens" some time during the 3rd century B.C. Loukoumades were the 1st prizes awarded to winners of the ancient Olympics. Now they are the perfect Greek cafe dessert celebratory piece of decadent, or mid-morning snack. They’re especially good on cold wintry afternoons with a nice cup of coffee. Bon appetit!
==Ingredients==

=== Fritters ===
* 4 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] active dry [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]]
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] warm [[Cookbook:Water|water]]

* [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|Vegetable oil]] for frying

=== Topping ===

* [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|Cinnamon]]
* [[Cookbook:Walnut|Walnuts]], crushed
* [[Cookbook:Sesame Seed|Sesame seeds]]

==Procedure==

=== Fritters ===
# Combine the yeast and ½ cup warm water.
# Mix the flour with the salt and put it in a deep bowl.
# Add the yeast and and 1 cup warm water, and mix well until you make a uniform thin paste.
# Cover and leave in the shade for 1½–2 hours until it rises and forms bubbles under the surface.
# Heat several inches of oil in a deep [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]]. Add the batter by large spoonfuls to make fritters. Turn the balls as they puff-up, [[Cookbook:Frying|frying]] 3–5 minutes until golden brown all over. Do not crowd the pan.
# Remove with a strainer or ladle, and place on paper towels; keep warm.

=== Topping ===
#Drizzle loukoumas with honey.
#Sprinkle with cinnamon, walnuts, and/or sesame seeds to taste.

{{recipesummary|category=Duck recipes|servings=3–4|time=1 hour to 90 minutes|difficulty=2
}}{{recipe}}| [[cookbook:Duck|Duck]] | [[cookbook:Poultry|Poultry]]
__NOTOC__
Long Island roast [[Cookbook:Duck|duckling]] is part of the regional cuisine of eastern Long Island, New York stemming from Long Island's thriving duck-farming industry which began in the late 19th century.<ref name="American duck farming">[http://www.foodreference.com/html/fducks.html Info on American duck farming on the Food Reference website]</ref> 

According to Alton Brown, host of the Food Network's ''Good Eats'', duck farming got its start on Long Island after an American businessman touring China in 1873 bought 25 white pekin ducks and shipped them to Long Island. Only nine survived the trip but those nine reproduced quickly and their descendants eventually found themselves on Long Island's numerous duck farms.<ref name= "What's Up, Duck (part one)">[http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QSO_Ej2WwZU Part one of the ''Good Eats'' episode titled ''What's Up, Duck?'']</ref><ref>[http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Frn-M8HnlP0 Part two of the ''Good Eats'' episode titled ''What's Up, Duck?'']</ref>

White pekins (also called Long Island pekins) now represent 95% of the ducks sold and consumed in the US<ref>[http://www.mapleleaffarms.com/46#q13 Info on white pekin ducks on the Maple Farms website]</ref> and are raised on farms in many parts of that country.<ref>[http://metzerfarms.com The Mertzer Farms home page]</ref><ref>[http://duckhavenfarm.com The Duck Haven Farm home page]</ref><ref>[http://www.roastgoose.com The Schlitz Foods home page]</ref>

According to Brown, many people shy away from cooking whole ducks because of their high fat content.<ref name="What's Up, Duck (part one)"/> Fortunately, there are cooking methods for removing the excess fat.<ref>[http://www.thecitycook.com/cooking/recipes/data/000103 Info on roasting duck on The City Cook website]</ref>

White pekin meat has a mild flavor and, if served skinless, is lower in fat and calories than skinless chicken breast.<ref>[http://www.foodreference.com/html/fducks.html Info on white pekins on the Food Reference website]</ref> Farmers slaughter these birds after six to eight weeks of growth when the meat is at its most tender.<ref name="American duck farming"/>

This recipe utilizes a vertical roasting method to drain the fat away from the duck.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 whole [[Cookbook:Duck|pekin duckling]] (3–6 [[Cookbook:Pound|lbs]], 1.5–3 [[Cookbook:Kg|kg]])
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
* Butter-flavored [[Cookbook:Cooking Spray|nonstick spray]]

== Preparation ==
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|450 °F]].  
# Rinse and wipe duckling, removing giblets.
# Set bird aside in an airy place to allow the skin to dry.
# Rub inside cavity with salt and pepper.
# Insert vertical oven roaster (used for "beer can chicken") into bird, and prop it upright.
# Coat bird on all sides with butter-flavored spray and sprinkle salt and pepper lightly over the skin.
# Place bird and vertical roaster into a large roasting pan (use a wire rack insert if you have one) and add ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] water to the bottom of the pan.  
# Leave bird in oven for 30 minutes, then reduce heat to [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|325 °F]] until done. No need to prick skin or baste bird, as the fat slowly [[Cookbook:Rendering|renders]] off leaving a wonderful crispy skin. Keep the bottom of the roasting pan covered with water to prevent smoking.
# Pour off fat and save, reserving drippings and liquid from the roasting pan.

==Notes, tips, and variations== 
*Serve with brown [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]], [[cookbook:Rice Pilaf|rice pilaf]] or baked [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potatoes]]. Cherry sauce and wild rice are also traditional.
*Use the duck fat to cook sliced [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]] or to make [[cookbook:Duck Confit|duck confit]].
*The fat and liver can be cooked together to make a very tasty paté so don't throw any of it out.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Beverages|Beverages]]

Traditional '''Madras filter coffee''' requires the use of specific fresh-roasted [[Cookbook:Coffee|coffee beans]] and [[Cookbook:Chicory|chicory roots]], which are not always available outside [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|India]]. This recipe uses Indian instant coffee that has chicory in it, which is available in some Indian stores and supermarkets. Nestle Bru instant coffee has 30% chicory added and in general has a near enough taste to authentic Madras filter coffee.

== Ingredients ==

* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* ½–2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] instant [[Cookbook:Coffee|coffee]] with chicory root
* ¾ cup [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* [[Cookbook:Sugar|Sugar]] (optional)

==Procedure==
# Bring the water to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], and stir in the coffee. Ensure there are no lumps.
# Bring the milk to a boil.
# Add the coffee mixture to the milk, and sweeten with sugar to taste.
# While the coffee is still boiling hot, pour it into a mug or, preferably, a stainless steel tumbler. While pouring the coffee, slowly raise the saucepan so the coffee falls into the mug from a height of about 1–1½ ft. This will cause the coffee to froth like espresso.
# If desired, you can dip a teaspoon in the coffee and lightly spread a few drops of it over the froth in the mug.
# Serve piping hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Filter coffee in India is actually made in a closed steel container called a coffee filter.

| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{Recipe}}

== Ingredients ==
[[File:Merry Christmas from Budapest! (42).jpg|thumb|Langos fryer  with its products in street kitchen in Hungary]]
* 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* Instant [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yogurt]] or [[Cookbook:Sour Cream|sour cream]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Lard|Lard]] or [[Cookbook:Canola Oil|canola oil]]

== Procedure ==
# Combine the flour and yeast. Add the eggs, then mix the yoghurt to make a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# Add the salt, and [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] until the dough is pliant and not too sticky, adding more flour or yogurt as necessary. The correct texture is really a matter of trial-and-error. It's not unlike an egg pasta dough, but it's rather less stiff.
# Transfer the dough to an oiled bowl. Cover and let rise overnight in a cool location, like the refrigerator.
# Gently deflate the dough.
# When you're ready to cook, heat about 2 [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]] of lard in a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|pan]]. The oil should be hot enough that when you put a very small piece of the dough into it, it drops to the bottom, and immediately rises up to the surface frying.
# Take a lump of the dough (roughly a bit bigger than a ping-pong ball, but rather smaller than a tennis-ball) and flatten it into a disk shape. Do this by hand rather than using a rolling pin—just keep pressing it between fingers and thumbs, and turning it round and round. Make the centre of the disk fairly thin, and the edge rather thicker. It should end up about 8 inches across if possible. Don't worry over-much about getting it too circular and even; the hand-made look is all part of their attraction.
# Carefully slide the disk of dough into the hot oil and let it [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] for 30 seconds or so. It should start to puff up as it fries; if it doesn't, either the oil isn't hot enough, or the disk is too thick.
# Carefully turn the dough over, and fry for another 30 seconds or so. Turn it over and see if the underside is golden brown or not. If not, fry for a while longer until both sides are golden brown, with a 'puffed-up' surface. Adjust the frying times for subsequent ones accordingly.
# Remove from the hot oil and drain away any excess.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
[[File:Lángos, 13 December 2023.jpg|thumb|Lángos with every traditional topping: salty garlic sauce, sourcream and cheese]]
* Lángos are traditionally served with a pungent fresh garlic [[Cookbook:Dressing|dressing]]. This is made by mincing up several cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] and mixing them into a small amount of oil and water, which is left to infuse for a while. You just spread the garlic dressing over the hot bread and eat.
* You can also top lángos with [[Cookbook:Crème Fraiche|crème fraîche]], [[Cookbook:Sour Cream|sour cream]], or thick yoghurt (as a substitute for something called tejföl that you can't get outside of Hungary), and grated [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]]. Fried lardons or diced [[Cookbook:Pancetta|pancetta]] are a good topping too.
* Three or four of these will leave you feeling pretty full, but if you've really hungry you could also have some good continental [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausage]] (ideally Hungarian kolbász, naturally) to go with them.

| Category = Bread recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Cuisine of India]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Pakistan|Cuisine of Pakistan]]

[[Cookbook:Roti|Roti]], in general, refers to an Indian [[Cookbook:Flatbread|flatbread]] cooked on an iron griddle ([[Cookbook:Tava|tava]]). '''Makki di roti''' (lit. "roti made from corn") refers to a special roti where cornmeal is used instead of the usual [[Cookbook:Flour#Wheat Flour|wheat flour]]. It is a famous delicacy from the north-Indian state of Punjab, and is cooked in the winters and served with ''saron da saag'' (cooked mustard leaves) and [[Cookbook:Lassi|lassi]]. Makki roti is yellow when cooked and has less adhesive strength, which makes it difficult to handle. It is more difficult to cook than ordinary wheat roti.

==Ingredients==

*1 handful [[Cookbook:Cornmeal|cornmeal]]
*1 spoonful unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], softened
*1 cupful lukewarm [[Cookbook:Water|water]]

==Equipment==

*Flat iron [[Cookbook:Griddle|griddle]] ([[Cookbook:Tava|''tahva'']]), preheated
*Flat board (''chakla'')
*Wide, flat mixing tray (''praat'')
*Cooking fire on which the ''tahva'' will be heated

==Procedure==

# Heap the cornmeal in a ''praat'' (a wide flat mixing tray) so it forms a hill. Make a well, and pour in a small quantity of the lukewarm water.
# Start to mix the cornmeal and water into a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]]. The dough should remain moist but not become sticky. Add water in small quantities to retain a moist feel. The final dough should not be sticky (sprinkle some extra cornmeal if needed to help soak up excess moisture).
# Add the soft butter (''makhan'') at the end and give it a final [[Cookbook:Kneading|kneading]].
# Take a small hand-sized portion of the dough from the mixing tray and roll it into a small ball (''ladu'') between the two hands. Gradually start to flatten the ball between the palms of the two hands (wet the hands and fingers to help the dough to stretch). At the same time rotate the flattening dough so that the thinning of the roti is even. It may start to crack at the edges. Repair any cracks by pressing them at the rims. Wetting the fingers and the palm of the hand will help to spread and give the roti a circular shape. Aim for an evenly thinned roti.
# When the roti is about the size of a small plate (or a little larger then a spread-out hand) place it on the preheated tahva. Leave the roti to take in the heat (it takes a while for roti to get cooked). Some areas of the roti will change in colour as the water evaporates. Soon after, the roti will be able to be moved on the tahva. With a dry cloth, press the areas of the roti that look moist.
# It is a matter of judgement when the roti can be turned over and heated on the other side. When the roti have been well cooked they should not have any moist looking areas. Some areas will have burned slightly but this is normal.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* The roti can be heated on open flames of the cooker or on a ''tava''. This process of placing roti on open flames is called ''radhna''. It takes time to get the thick roti to be well cooked.
* The cooked roti is smeared with some [[Cookbook:Clarified Butter|clarified butter]] (''ghee''). This is called ''chopardna''. The roti is then put into a serving dish. Traditionally, the roti is served as it gets prepared and is eaten fresh. On occasions when it has to be stored before serving it is placed in a dry tray called ''chahba''.
