{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Mexico|Cuisine of Mexico]]

'''Machacado con huevo''' is a dish which consists of shredded dry [[cookbook:beef|beef]] that is [[Cookbook:Scrambled Eggs|scrambled]] with [[cookbook:egg|eggs]]. Its name means "shredded with eggs" in Spanish. The shredded dry beef, ''carne seca'', is said to have originated in the town of Ciénega de Flores, about an hour north of Monterrey, [[cookbook:cuisine of Mexico|Mexico]]. The early settlers in the area air-[[cookbook:curing|cured]] beef so that it would be preserved. This particular dish was made famous by Tía Lencha, a local woman who prepared it and eventually sold it in a restaurant. Today there is a commercially available Tia Lencha dried beef in most supermarkets in Mexico.

The basic machacado con huevo is made with eggs and dried beef. Chopped [[cookbook:tomato|tomato]]es, [[cookbook:onion|onion]]s and [[cookbook:jalapeño|jalapeño]]s or serrano [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|chile pepper]]s can be added, or [[cookbook:Salsa|salsa]] can be cooked into it, to create another version.

Machacado con huevo often comes as a "[[cookbook:taco|taco]]" presentation.

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[cookbook:butter|butter]] or [[cookbook:margarine|margarine]]
*6 large [[cookbook:egg|egg]]s, lightly beaten
*2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] shredded [[cookbook:beef|beef]] filling 
*10 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. 8-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] soft taco-size [[Cookbook:Flour Tortilla|flour tortilla]]s, warmed 
*1 can (16 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]]) [[Cookbook:Refried Beans|refried beans]], warmed 
*2 cups (8 ounces) shredded [[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|cheddar]] or [[Cookbook:Monterey Jack Cheese|Monterey Jack Cheese]]
*[[cookbook:Salsa|Salsa]] for accompaniment

==Procedure==
#Heat butter in large [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] over medium-high heat. 
#Add eggs; cook, stirring frequently, for 2–3 minutes or until eggs just begin to set.
#Stir in shredded beef filling. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 2 to 3 minutes or until eggs are cooked and beef is heated through. 
#Serve eggs with tortillas, beans, cheese, and salsa.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* Machacado con huevo can be served in a big bowl, and with some soft tortillas at hand can be prepared in your plate, can be served in the table as tacos, or can be eaten without using tortillas at all.
* Queso fundido con [[cookbook:chorizo|chorizo]] (melted cheese with chorizo) is also something that can be found at the table when eating machacado con huevo. It is usually served at the table in a pan, and added to the taco.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian Cuisine]]

'''Malai mixed vegetable''', is a creamy side dish for Indian bread.

==Ingredients==
* 3 green [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|capsicums]] (bell peppers)
* 1 each orange, yellow, and red capsicum
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Paneer|paneer]] cubes
* [[Cookbook:Cashew|Cashew nuts]]
* 4 large [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Pea|peas]]
* 3–4 [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|green chillies]] (depending on spice requirement), finely chopped
* Dried [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]] and [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Garam Masala|Garam masala]]
* [[Cookbook:Chili Powder|Red chilli powder]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Turmeric|Turmeric]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] [[Cookbook:Cream|whipping cream]]
* 1 Tbsp [[Cookbook:Sour Cream|sour cream]]
* [[Cookbook:Cilantro|Cilantro]] for garnishing

==Procedure==

# Cut the bell peppers into ½-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] pieces.
# [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] paneer until golden brown; set aside.
# Soak a handful of cashew nuts in warm water.
# Grind the tomatoes and the soaked cashew into a fine paste. Keep this paste aside.
# Sauté the chopped vegetables, green chillies, and dried parsley in the butter/oil until they are cooked. You could also microwave the vegetables for ~10 minutes without water, and then sauté them in butter for a minute.
# Add the tomato paste to the vegetables and cook for 5 minutes.
# Add the garam masala, red chilli powder, salt, and turmeric according to taste; [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 2 minutes.
# Add the whipping cream and the sour cream, and let it cook until the cream thickens.
# Add the paneer and mix well.
# [[Cookbook:Garnish|Garnish]] with cilantro and cashew nuts.
# Serve hot with [[Cookbook:Naan|naan]] or [[Cookbook:Roti|roti]].

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* You could choose other vegetables like [[Cookbook:Zucchini|zucchini]] or [[Cookbook:Broccoli|broccoli]] if you like.

{{recipe|Brownies, Magic}}

A '''magic brownie''' is a brownie that has been infused with cannabis. Eating the brownie results in a cannabis high one to a few hours after consumption—as a result, care should be taken not to eat too many of them to avoid adverse effects<ref>https://dhss.alaska.gov/dph/director/pages/marijuana/edibles.aspx</ref><ref>https://patriotcare.org/use-medical-marijuana-edibles/</ref><ref>https://www.phidenverhealth.org/community-health-promotion/substance-misuse/marijuana-edible-facts</ref>.

{{warning|'''Warning:''' The possession and use of cannabis is forbidden in many countries. '''Please read the wikibooks [[Wikibooks:Risk disclaimer|risk disclaimer]] before attempting to follow this recipe.'''}}
== Ingredients ==
* {{convert|4|g|oz|abbr=on}} [[Cookbook:Cannabis|cannabis]], ground
* 60 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (½ stick/2.1 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] 
* 300 g (3½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]]/11 oz) [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate]] chips
* 180 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (¾ cup/160 g/5.6 oz) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] 
* 2 standard [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]] 
* 5 ml (1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]]) [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] extract
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] 
* Grated [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] [[Cookbook:Zest|zest]]
* 250 g (1¾ cups/8.8 oz) self-raising [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] 

== Procedure ==

# Melt the butter in a small [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], and stir in the cannabis. Cook slowly over a low temperature for 2–3 hours. Do not allow to [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] or exceed 200 °F (93°C).
# If desired, [[Cookbook:Straining|strain]] the butter to remove the cannabis solids.
# Melt the chocolate chips in the [[Cookbook:Microwave|microwave]] or over a [[Cookbook:Double Boiler|double boiler]]. Combine the melted chocolate and infused butter, stirring until smooth.
# Stir in the sugar, and allow the mixture to cool if needed.
# Stir in the eggs, vanilla, salt, and lemon zest until smooth.
# [[Cookbook:Folding|Fold]] in the flour just until combined.
# Transfer the batter to a greased and/or [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment]]-lined [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|pan]]. 
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at 360°F/180°C for about 20–25 minutes or until a [[Cookbook:Skewer|toothpick]] inserted in the center comes out without any batter on it.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Try using brown cane sugar instead of white sugar.
* Melt some chocolate and mix with a little sugar, vanilla, lemon, and a little more weed. Drizzle on the freshly cooked brownies for a little added flavour and high. This creates a nicer tasting brownie with more of a kick.
* Try adding a few crushed up biscuits before baking for a more varied taste.

{{recipe}}

'''Madbucha''' or '''matbucha''' is a North African dish of stewed tomatoes and peppers. It can be used as a side dish with meats, as well as put on bread or white rice. There's more than one way to make it, and the following recipe is a family recipe. 

==Ingredients==
*[[Cookbook:Oil and fat|Oil]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]s, [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*2 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], chopped
*15 [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], [[Cookbook:Cube|cubed]]
*10 [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell peppers]], cut into small pieces
*5 [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile peppers]], chopped small
*330 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] canned [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
*[[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
*[[Cookbook:Cumin|Cumin]]
*[[Cookbook:Parsley|Parsley]]
*[[Cookbook:Oregano|Oregano]]

==Procedure==
#Take a pot that is big enough for all of the above ingredients, cover the bottom with oil, and put it on a flame.
#When the oil gets hot, add the onion and garlic. 
#When they start to fry, add the rest of the vegetables and salt.
#Mix it up a bit and cover the pot.
#Leave it to cook, mixing it every so often, until the level of the liquid is higher than the level of the vegetables.
#Drain off most (but not all) the liquid.
#Add the tomato paste and the spices.
#Mix, and let it cool.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* When chopping the peppers, you want them small but not so small that they disappear when cooked.
* The peppers can be any color, but red is traditional.

'''Maitorieska''' (''milk rieska'', pronounced "RE-ehskuh") is a [[Cookbook:Barley|barley]]-based [[Cookbook:Flatbread|flatbread]] that is a local specialty and a very traditional food in the Ylivieska area of [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Finland|Finland]].

==Ingredients==

* 250 [[Cookbook:mL|ml]] (1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]]) cold [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* ⅓ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

==Procedure==

# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 300°C (570°F), or as high as it will go. 
# Combine milk and salt, and add flour. Mix the ingredients well to make a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# [[Cookbook:Knead|Knead]] into a flat, round bread (about 0.5 cm / ¼ [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] thick). 
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] on an [[Cookbook:Oven Tray|oven tray]] for about 10 minutes or until the surface gets some darker spots. Alternatively, [[Cookbook:Pan fry|fry it in a pan]] on the stove or on open fire.
# Eat fresh with [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] and cold milk.

{{Recipe summary
| Category = Recipes for pastries
| Difficulty = 3
}}__NOTOC__
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Middle Eastern cuisines|Middle Eastern cuisine]]

'''Ma'amoul''' are [[Cookbook:Pastry|pastries]] filled with dates or nuts, and they are popular throughout the Arab world. They can be made in special ma'amoul moulds, and there are three shapes of mould. The flattish circular shape is used for date ma’amoul; the round domed shape for walnut ma’amoul; the long oval for pistachio ma’amoul. Some families do not use moulds, but have special crimping tweezers for making patterns on the top of the pastry. Alternatively, a fork may be used.

The Sephardi Jews of the Eastern Mediterranean refer to date ma'amoul as ''menenas''. These are often made in the form of date rolls rather than balls.

==Ingredients==

=== Pistachio filling ===
* ½ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (250 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) finely-[[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Pistachio|pistachios]]
* ¼ lb [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Rosewater|rose water]]

=== Walnut filling ===
* ½ lb (250 g) finely-chopped [[Cookbook:Walnut|walnuts]]
* ¼ lb sugar
* 1 tbsp ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]

=== Date filling ===
* 1 lb (500 g) pitted [[Cookbook:Date|dates]], chopped
* ½ teacup [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* [[Cookbook:Butter|Butter]] (optional)

=== Pastries ===
* 1 lb (500 g) [[Cookbook:Flour|plain white flour]] (up to a quarter of the flour may be replaced with fine [[Cookbook:Semolina|semolina]])
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Sugar|white sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|Baking powder]] (optional)
* ½ lb (250 g) unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] (Normandy butter is best)
* 1–2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Rosewater|rose water]] or [[Cookbook:Orange#Oranges in Cooking|orange flower water]]
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Water|water]] or [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* [[Cookbook:Powdered Sugar|Icing sugar]]

==Special equipment==

* Wooden ma'amoul moulds, oiled and dusted with flour

==Procedure==

=== Fillings ===
# Mix chopped [[Cookbook:Pistachio|pistachios]] with sugar and rose water.
# Mix chopped [[Cookbook:Walnut|walnuts]] with sugar and [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]].
# Combine the chopped dates and water in a pot. Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], squashing the mixture against the side of the pan with a wooden spoon until approximately uniform in consistency. Mix in the butter if using. Blend with an [[Cookbook:Food Processor|electric chopper]] if desired to make a smoother paste. Allow to cool.

=== Pastries ===
# [[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] the flour into a mixing bowl. Mix with the white sugar, and a pinch of salt if desired. Some people add a very small quantity of baking powder.
# Work in the butter until the consistency is as uniform as possible; one way is to heat the butter in the microwave first until it is nearly melted, and then mix it with the flour into a sort of crumble. Cover and leave at room temperature for several hours to overnight.
# Break up the dough with your fingers, and add the rose water or orange flower water and 2 tbsp water or milk until it is malleable. [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] the whole into a smooth ball.
# Take a walnut-sized ball of the dough, stick your thumb into it, and hollow out into a cup shape so that the walls are as thin as possible without breaking.
# Insert filling to about three-quarters full, and pinch the aperture closed. Pat gently into a ball, not letting the walls break.
# Decorate the ball on top with tweezers or the prongs of a fork. Alternatively, pat it into a wooden mould and flatten the exposed bottom surface, then bang the mould face down on the work surface to extract the moulded pastry.
# Repeat the assembly steps until all the dough and the filling is used. If at any stage the remaining dough shows signs of drying out, knead in a little more water or milk.
# Place the pastries on an ungreased [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheet]] and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] in a preheated [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] (180°C / 355°F; 160°C if a fan oven) for 20 minutes: they must not be allowed to become hard or brown. In fact they should look a little moist and underdone when removed from the oven: they will steam off and harden as they cool.
# Leave the pastries to cool, and [[Cookbook:Dusting|dust]] with icing sugar when cold. Keep in a sealed plastic box or biscuit tin.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Some people use ground [[Cookbook:Almond|almonds]], with or without green food colouring, instead of pistachios for the filling.
* A variant served on very special occasions is known as ''karabij''. Make nut ma’amoul, using water rather than milk and no flower water, in the form of balls rather than in a mould, leaving them smooth without making any indentations. Arrange in a pyramid and serve with a special cream called ''naatiffe''. This is made by boiling water, lemon juice, sugar, orange flower water and soapwort root (''Saponaria officinalis'') into a syrup, and folding in stiffly beaten egg whites. Some books mention ''bois de Panama'' instead of soapwort, but apparently this is a fallacy<ref>http://www.anissas.com/natef-a-miraculous-transformation/</ref>.

'''Lumberjacks''' are a [[Cookbook:Cookie|cookie]] from the Old Sturbridge Village Cookbook, and they reflect baking from 1830s New England.

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|caster sugar]]
*1 cup white [[Cookbook:Shortening|vegetable shortening]] or [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*1 cup dark [[Cookbook:Molasses|molasses]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
*4 cups sifted [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] (not self-raising)
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] of [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|bicarbonate of soda]]
*2 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
*1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]

==Procedure==
#[[Cookbook:Creaming|Cream]] together the sugar and shortening.
#Add molasses and eggs, and mix well.
#[[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] together the flour, spices, and bicarbonate of soda. Add this mixture to the egg-butter mixture, and mix well to make a dough.
#Put ¼ cup additional white sugar into a small bowl.
#Dip fingers into the sugar, then pinch off a ball of dough and roll it into the size and shape of a walnut.
#Roll the cookie dough ball into the sugar and place on a greased [[Cookbook:Cookie sheet|cookie sheet]].
#Repeat the shaping and sugar-coating process with the remaining dough, spacing the cookies about 3 [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]] apart on the sheet.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in a preheated 350°F (175°C) [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] for 10–15 minutes.
#Let cool completely—the cookies should be soft when cooled.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Different countries use different strengths of molasses. If you can find the American brand of Grandma's dark molasses then that is perfect.
* If you use some muscovado sugar, then add the white and muscovado sugars at the same time.

'''Macaroni pie''' is a side dish that goes well with stewed [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], callaloo or any stewed peas like pigeon peas or lentils. It can also be enjoyed on its own.

It has versions derived from Caribbean, Early American and Scottish origins.

==Ingredients==
*1 package (225 [[Cookbook:Gram|grams]] / 8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) dried [[Cookbook:Macaroni|macaroni]] pasta
*2 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]s
*2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]] [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]]
*1½ [[Cookbook:cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Condensed milk|evaporated milk]]
*1 small [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], grated
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Pepper|white pepper]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] prepared yellow [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]]
*1 pat of unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], melted
*[[Cookbook:Bread Crumb|Breadcrumbs]]

==Procedure==
#[[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] macaroni in salted water until tender; drain.
#[[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] eggs until fluffy.
#Combine macaroni, eggs, cheese, milk, onion, carrot, salt, white pepper, mustard, and butter.
#Pour into a greased [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|baking dish]] and sprinkle shredded cheese and bread crumbs evenly on top.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at 175°C (350°F) until firm (about 30 minutes). A fork or metal [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewer]] should come out dry when you press it all the way through the pie.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*Macaroni pie can be enhanced further by adding ingredients such as [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]], chopped [[Cookbook:Spices and Herbs|herbs]], minced [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]], or roasted [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]]. Also try using a few varieties of cheese together.
*Usually best when the surface has browned to an even colour.

{{recipe}}
== Ingredients ==
* 1 large (about 2 [[Cookbook:kg|kg]]) whole [[Cookbook:rabbit|rabbit]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Sunflower Oil|sunflower oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:clove|clove]] [[Cookbook:garlic|garlic]]
* 300 [[Cookbook:g|g]] white [[Cookbook:potatoes|potatoes]], peeled
* 1 small [[Cookbook:carrot|carrot]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 800 [[Cookbook:g|g]] canned [[Cookbook:Tomato|crushed tomatoes]] or canned '[[Cookbook:Pelati|Pelati]]'
* 200 [[Cookbook:ML|ml]] [[Cookbook:Red Wine|red wine]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:sugar|sugar]]
* 2–3 [[Cookbook:bay leaf|Mediterranean bay leaves]]
* [[Cookbook:Tabasco Sauce|Tabasco]] sauce
* Freshly-ground [[Cookbook:pepper|black pepper]]
* [[Cookbook:salt|Salt]] to taste
* 100 [[Cookbook:g|g]] canned [[Cookbook:pea|peas]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Mixed Spice|mixed spice]]

== Procedure ==
#Cut up the rabbit at the joints. Cut the rib section into 3–4 pieces, and divide the legs at all the joints. Split the head of the rabbit in half. The whole animal should be cut into about 10–12 pieces so they are large and chunky, but small enough that they can be easily manipulated with large [[Cookbook:Utensil|spoon]]. Remove and keep internal organs apart.
#[[Cookbook:Mince|Mince]] the garlic. Heat the oil in a large [[Cookbook:frying pan|frying pan]]. Heat some of the garlic in the oil. Add some rabbit pieces and cook through.
#Remove cooked meat from the pan and place in a large container. Cook the rest of the meat in the same way in batches, adding some garlic with every batch. The meat should be well cooked but not very brown.
#Fry the internal organs whole in the same oil until well-cooked. Take some of the smaller pieces of meat without bone and add them to the organs. Keep these apart from the main meat.
#Cut the potatoes into large irregular chunks, slightly smaller than the pieces of meat.
#In a [[Cookbook:Stock pot|stock pot]], place the fried rabbit, the potatoes, the chopped carrot, the tomato pulp, wine, sugar and laurel leaves. Add salt, pepper, mixed spice and Tabasco carefully. Cover and [[Cookbook:simmer|simmer]] on a low flame for 4 hours. Stir occasionally during the first hour.
#Once done, add the peas, and cook until tender (about 10 minutes).

== Serving ==
A typical Maltese rabbit stew is served in a few different ways depending on the situation, family tradition and locality. One way is to simply serve a plate of stew with Maltese bread for dipping in the sauce. Sometimes the internal organs and some small bits of boneless meat are served without any garnish on a small plate with salt, pepper, and fresh sour-dough bread as a special treat for children as they wait for this time-consuming dish to be prepared. A full ''fenkata'', a Maltese word meaning 'rabbit-based dinner party' could be as follows:
# Start with Maltese galletti, Gbejniet, Zalzett, bigilla, and the internal organs of the rabbit as [[Cookbook:entrée|entrées]].
# For second plate serve [[Cookbook:Spaghetti|Spaghetti]] (typically slightly overcooked in Maltese cuisine) with a covering of sauce from the stew.
# Serve the rabbit meat and potatoes (with little sauce) as main course, always accompanied by bread, and a strong red wine.
# Serve Maltese style [[Cookbook:Trifle|Trifle]] or Traditional Maltese Ice Cream (also called Gelat tan-Nanna) for [[Cookbook:dessert|dessert]].
# Round off with [[Cookbook:peanut|peanuts]] in the shell and [[Bartending/Alcohol/Anise_liqueur#Anisette|Anisette]].

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* The best stew is slow cooked on the lowest flame for as long as possible. Using a higher flame you can reduce cooking time to 2 hours, but this is not a dish that should be rushed. If you have the time you can even cook it for 6 hours on a camping-type flame for an even richer taste.

'''Madeleines''' small French [[Cookbook:Cake|cakes]] baked in special baking trays that give them a shell-like shape. The Spanish counterparts, Madalenas, are sometimes served in paper cases and then resemble muffins.

==Ingredients==
* 4 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 100 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 100 g [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* grated zest of 1 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]
* 75 g melted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]

==Procedure==
# [[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] the eggs, sugar and salt in a mixing bowl until frothy.
# Combine the flour, baking powder, and lemon zest, and fold into the egg mixture. Fold in the melted butter.
# Divide the dough into greased madeleine molds, keeping in mind that the dough will rise in the oven to fill the molds.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in a preheated [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] at 180°C / 350°F for 12–15 minutes until the cakes are springy but not browned.
# Cool and unmold the madeleines.
# Serve fresh.

{{recipesummary|category=Flatbread recipes|servings=12|time=4–5 minutes|difficulty=3|image=[[File:Malawach.jpg|300px|Malawach]]}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Malawach''' is a layered, flaky [[Cookbook:Flatbread|flatbread]] that is popularly eaten in Israel, and now made popular in other regions. It is typically brushed with oil or fat and cooked flat in a frying pan.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] white [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose wheat flour]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] white granulated [[cookbook:sugar|sugar]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] dried [[cookbook:yeast|yeast]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[cookbook:salt|salt]]
* 2–3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] lukewarm water (or such as is sufficient for kneading dough)
* [[cookbook:vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]] (sufficient for lining skillet)
* 200 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] melted [[cookbook:butter|butter]] or [[cookbook:margarine|margarine]]

== Procedure ==
# Mix together the flour, sugar, yeast, salt, and water, starting with only 2 cups of water. [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] the dough well, adding additional water if necessary to make it soft and pliable.
# Cover and let dough rest until it doubles in size.
# Take up dough and begin to knead it by hand. Divide dough into 12 smaller portions and place upon oiled surface. Let dough rest until each portion rises and doubles in size, occasionally oiling the surface of dough.
# Grease a work surface with oil. Roll out each piece of dough with a [[Cookbook:Rolling Pin|rolling pin]] to get very large, almost paper-thin, rounds of dough.
# [[Cookbook:Brushing|Brush]] each round liberally with melted butter. Fold the dough in half, from the top towards the bottom. Then, roll it up from the top towards the bottom as one would roll-up a sleeping bag, forming a rope. Coil the rope around itself into a spiral.
# Cover and allow the dough to rest until it rises and doubles in size.
# Roll each spiral out again into a thin round. Brush again with butter, then repeat the rolling and coiling process.
# Allow the dough to rest once more while covered until it rises.
# Heat a [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]] with a little vegetable oil.
# Use your hands to flatten out the dough coils on a greased surface.
# Place flattened dough portions in skillet and cover with lid. [[Cookbook:Frying#Pan-frying|Fry]] the dough on a medium to low heat until the bottom turns an amber color. Flip over and fry on reverse side without the lid.
# Serve hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Malawach is often served with a [[Cookbook:Hard Boiled Eggs|hard-boiled egg]], along with tomato [[cookbook:salsa|salsa]] that has been flavored with freshly-[[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[cookbook:coriander|coriander]].

{{Recipe}}

Algerians are very fond of '''m'semen''', a [[Cookbook:Flatbread|flatbread]] made from basic ingredients like flour, semolina, butter, and water. The dough can be sticky to the touch while folding, so oiling the hands is necessary. Some people also fill the pancakes with minced meat and vegetables before frying in oil until they become crisp and golden.

== Ingredients ==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Semolina|semolina]] flour
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* ¼ tsp instant [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]]
* 1 ½ cups warm water
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]]

== Procedure ==

# Combine both flours, sugar, salt, and yeast in a bowl.
# Gradually mix in the warm water until you get a soft [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]]. If it feels too sticky, mix in a little more all-purpose flour. If too dry, mix in some more water.
# On a lightly-floured surface, [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] the dough for 10 minutes or until it is smooth.
# Divide the dough into smaller pieces, and [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|roll]] each out into very thin rounds.
# [[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] each dough round with oil.
# Fold the rounds into square envelope shapes, making 4 folds into the center.
# Cook each flatbread in a hot, lightly-greased [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]] until browned.

{{Recipe}}

This recipe uses a conventional [[Cookbook:Roasting|roasting]] method based on the one featured on The City Cook website.<ref>[http://www.thecitycook.com/cooking/recipes/data/000103 Roast duck recipe on the City Cook website]</ref>

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (4–5 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]], 1.8–3.6 [[Cookbook:Kg|kg]]) whole [[Cookbook:Duck|pekin duckling]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]], cut into quarters
* 1 [[Cookbook:Orange|orange]], cut into quarters or eighths
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]

== Preparation ==
# Defrost the duck in the fridge if it's frozen.
# Remove the giblets and any packages from the body cavity.
# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|375 °F]] and place an oven rack in the center of the oven.
# Rinse the duck and pat it dry both inside and out with [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towels]].
# Pierce the skin every half inch with prongs, pushing the prongs through the skin and into the fat but not into the meat. The fat will escape through these holes as the duck cooks.
# Rub plenty of salt and freshly ground pepper on the skin. Then, place 2 pieces of lemon and 2–4 pieces of orange inside the duck's cavity.
# Tie the duck's legs together with a piece of butcher's twine. This will keep the citrus inside the cavity.
# Place the duck breast side up on a rack that has been placed on a roasting pan. It's important to use a roasting pan that has some depth so the fat drips into the pan and not the oven.
# Push a meat [[Cookbook:Thermometer|thermometer]] into one of the thighs.
# Place the bird on the center rack of the oven. It will cook in 1–1½ hours depending on its size.
# Remove the duck every 20 minutes from the oven and drain the excess fat. Rotate the duck each time you return it to the oven to help it crisp evenly. You'll know it's done when the skin is golden brown and crispy. Also, the meat thermometer should read no lower than 165 °F.
# Remove the bird from the oven. Pour out the liquid from the cavity and discard.
# Allow the duck to rest for ten minutes before carving.

'''Mandazi''' are East African doughnuts that originated from places like Uganda, Kenya, and Tanzania. They are popular as a street food.

== Ingredients ==

* 4 [[Cookbook:Units of measurement#Nigeria|milk cups]] [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]], plus extra for working the dough
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] [[Cookbook:Zest|zest]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* ½ tsp ground [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]] (optional)
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]] or [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], at room temperature
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] essence

* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]] for frying

== Procedure ==

# [[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] together the [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] and baking powder in a bowl.
# Mix in the salt, lemon zest, sugar, and cloves.
# Rub in the [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] until the flour becomes coarse.
# Combine the vanilla and [[Cookbook:Water|water]], then mix this into the flour mixture to get a firm [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] the dough for about 2 minutes until it no longer sticks to your hands. Set aside to rest for 10 minutes.
# Flour a work surface, and [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|roll out]] the dough to about 1-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] thickness.
# Cut the dough into 10 equal squares, then roll each square into a ball.
# Heat a pan of [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]] over medium heat. [[Cookbook:Deep Fat Frying|Deep fry]] the mandazi in batches of 5 for about 10 minutes or until they are puffed, brown all over, and cooked through.
# Remove when it is fully done and enjoy your delicious East African Doughnuts.

{{Recipe summary

| Difficulty = 3
| Image = [[File:Mahshi.jpg|300px]]
}}{{Recipe}}

'''Mahshi''' is a delicious Egyptian dish that involves stuffing various vegetables with a flavorful mixture of rice, herbs, and spices. It is a versatile and satisfying dish that can be customized to individual tastes. Mahshi is typically served as a main course and is enjoyed by families and friends during festive occasions or gatherings.

== Ingredients ==
* Assorted vegetables for stuffing, such as [[Cookbook:zucchini|zucchini]], [[Cookbook:eggplant|eggplant]], [[Cookbook:bell pepper|bell pepper]], and [[Cookbook:tomato|tomato]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] medium-grain [[Cookbook:rice|rice]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:tomato|tomato paste]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:olive oil|olive oil]]
* ¼ cup fresh [[Cookbook:parsley|parsley]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* ¼ cup fresh [[Cookbook:mint|mint leaves]], finely chopped
* 2 cloves [[Cookbook:garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] ground [[Cookbook:cumin|cumin]]
* 1 teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:coriander|coriander]]
* [[Cookbook:salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:black pepper|Black pepper]] to taste
* Water, as needed

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]] for cutting and hollowing out vegetables
* Spoon for scooping out vegetable seeds and flesh
* Mixing bowl
* [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|Baking dish]] or casserole dish
* [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|Aluminum foil]]
* [[Cookbook:Oven|Oven]]

== Procedure ==
# Prepare the vegetables for stuffing by carefully cutting off the tops and scooping out the seeds and flesh, creating hollow shells. Set aside the scooped-out vegetable flesh for later use.
# In a mixing bowl, combine the medium-grain rice, tomato paste, olive oil, finely chopped parsley, finely chopped mint leaves, minced garlic, ground cumin, ground coriander, salt, and black pepper. Mix well until all the ingredients are thoroughly combined.
# Fill each hollowed vegetable with the rice and herb mixture, packing it firmly and leaving some space at the top for the rice to expand while cooking.
# Arrange the stuffed vegetables in a baking dish or casserole dish, placing them closely together to support each other.
# Use the reserved vegetable flesh to fill any empty spaces between the stuffed vegetables. This helps to prevent them from shifting during cooking.
# Pour enough water into the baking dish to partially cover the stuffed vegetables. This will help create a moist cooking environment.
# Cover the baking dish with aluminum foil, ensuring it is tightly sealed to retain moisture.
# Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] the mahshi for about 60–75 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender and the rice filling is cooked through.
# Remove the foil and continue baking for an additional 10–15 minutes to allow the tops of the stuffed vegetables to slightly brown.
# Once cooked, remove the mahshi from the oven and let it cool slightly before serving.

| servings = Serves 4–6
}}

{{Recipe}}

'''Mafrum bil Lahm''' is a traditional Libyan dish that features layers of seasoned meat and potatoes, topped with a flavorful tomato sauce. It is a delicious and satisfying meal that is often enjoyed during festive occasions and gatherings.

== Ingredients ==
* 4 [[Cookbook:potato|potatoes]], peeled and cut into thick slices
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:olive oil|olive oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 3 cloves of [[Cookbook:garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|grams]] (1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) ground [[Cookbook:beef|beef]] or [[Cookbook:lamb|lamb]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] ground [[Cookbook:cumin|cumin]]
* 1 teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:paprika|paprika]]
* ½ teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:cayenne pepper|cayenne pepper]] (adjust according to spice preference)
* [[Cookbook:salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:pepper|Pepper]], to taste
* 400 grams (14 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) canned [[Cookbook:tomato|tomatoes]], crushed
* Fresh [[Cookbook:parsley|parsley]] or [[Cookbook:cilantro|cilantro]], chopped, for garnish

== Equipment ==
* Large pot
* [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|Skillet]]
* Wooden spoon or [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]]
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* Chef's [[Cookbook:Knife|knife]]
* Measuring spoons
* Measuring cups
* Vegetable [[Cookbook:Peeler|peeler]]
* [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|Baking dish]]
* [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|Aluminum foil]]

== Procedure ==
# In a large pot, bring water to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] and add the potato slices. Boil them for about 5 minutes, or until slightly tender. Drain and set aside.
# In a skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and minced garlic, and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] until they become translucent and fragrant.
# Add the ground beef or lamb to the skillet and cook until browned. Break up the meat with a wooden spoon or spatula as it cooks.
# Stir in the ground cumin, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper, and cook for another minute to toast the spices.
# Remove the skillet from the heat and set aside.
# Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
# Take a slice of the boiled potato and flatten it with the palm of your hand. Place a spoonful of the cooked meat mixture in the center of the potato slice, and fold the sides over to enclose the filling. Repeat with the remaining potato slices and meat mixture.
# Arrange the stuffed potato slices in a single layer in a baking dish.
# In a separate bowl, mix the crushed tomatoes with salt, pepper, and any remaining spices. Pour the tomato sauce over the stuffed potatoes, ensuring they are well-coated.
# Cover the baking dish with aluminum foil and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] in the preheated oven for 45 minutes.
# Remove the foil and continue baking for an additional 10–15 minutes, or until the potatoes are fully cooked and golden brown on top.
# [[Cookbook:Garnish|Garnish]] with fresh parsley or cilantro before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations==
* Mafrum bil lahm can be served as a main course accompanied by a salad or crusty bread.
* Leftovers can be refrigerated and reheated for later enjoyment.
* Adjust the spiciness of the dish by adding more or less cayenne pepper according to your preference.
* For added flavor, you can sprinkle grated cheese on top of the mafrum before baking it in the oven.
* Feel free to experiment with different seasonings and spices to personalize the dish to your taste.
* Vegetarian variation: Replace the ground meat with a combination of cooked and seasoned vegetables such as zucchini, eggplant, and bell peppers.
* Gluten-free variation: Ensure that all the ingredients used, including spices and canned tomatoes, are gluten-free certified.

{{Recipe}}

'''Mafe''' is a spicy and delicious African peanut [[Cookbook:Stew|stew]]. It is eaten throughout Africa, especially by the people of Ivory Coast.

== Ingredients ==

* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], neatly [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] cloves, neatly minced
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] grated [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] crushed [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] flavour [[Cookbook:Dehydrated Broth|bouillon cubes]], crumbled
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Peanut Butter|peanut butter]]
* 4 African eggplants, peeled and [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potatoes]], peeled and chopped
* 1 medium size green [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]], washed and chopped
* 4 medium size [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]], washed and [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 3 medium size [[Cookbook:Turnip|turnips]], washed and chopped
* 2 medium size habanero [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile peppers]]
* 15 medium size [[Cookbook:Okra|okra]], washed, trimmed, and chopped
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Black pepper]] to taste
* Chopped [[Cookbook:Peanut|peanuts]] (optional)
==Equipment==
*Large cooking [[Cookbook:Pots and Pans|pot]] or [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]
*[[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
*[[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]
*Wooden [[Cookbook:Cooking Spoon|spoon]] or [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]]
*[[Cookbook:Measuring Cup|Measuring cups]] and [[Cookbook:Measuring Spoons|spoons]]
*[[Cookbook:Sieve|Strainer]]
*[[Cookbook:Garlic Press|Garlic press]]
*[[Cookbook:Ladle|Ladle]]

== Procedure ==

# In a large pot, heat the [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]] over medium heat.
# Add the onions, garlic, grated ginger. Cook, stirring, for about 5 minutes until the onions become translucent.
# Add the tomato paste, bouillon cubes, and 6 cups (about 1.5 litres) hot water. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] over low heat for 10 minutes.
# Stir in the peanut butter until fully incorporated. Add the eggplant, sweet [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], green [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]], [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]], [[Cookbook:Turnip|turnips]], and habanero, then stir carefully to avoid fully crushing the habanero.
# Cover and cook for about an hour over low heat until thickened.
# Stir in the [[Cookbook:Okra|okra]], then season with salt and black [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]] to your desired taste. Cook for about 30 minutes until the vegetables become soft.
# Remove the chilli [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]] and sprinkle it with peanut butter if you will like and if not leave it like that.
# Serve hot.

{{Recipe summary
| Category = Stew recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{Recipe}}

'''Maffé''' is a traditional West African dish that is popular in countries such as Senegal, Mali, and Gambia. This rich and hearty stew is made with a peanut sauce base and typically includes a combination of vegetables, meat (such as beef or chicken), and aromatic spices. Maffé is known for its creamy texture, nutty flavor, and the perfect balance of savory and slightly sweet notes. It is traditionally enjoyed with a side of steamed rice or couscous.

== Ingredients ==

* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]] or [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], cut into cubes
* 1 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] cloves, [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] smooth [[Cookbook:Peanut Butter|peanut butter]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] ground [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile]] powder (adjust to your preferred level of spiciness)
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]] to taste
* 1 can (14 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]]) [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
* 4 cups beef or chicken [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]], diced
* 2 [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], diced
* 1 [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]] (any color of your choice), diced 
* 1 cup sliced [[Cookbook:Okra|okra]]
* 1 cup chopped leafy greens (such as [[Cookbook:Spinach|spinach]] or [[Cookbook:Kale|kale]])
* Fresh [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]] or [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]], chopped (for [[Cookbook:Garnish|garnish]])

== Equipment ==

* Large pot or [[Cookbook:Dutch Oven|Dutch oven]] with a lid
* Wooden spoon or [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]]
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]] 
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]
* Measuring cups and spoons

== Procedure ==

# Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the beef or chicken cubes and cook until browned on all sides. Remove the meat from the pot and set it aside.
# In the same pot, add the chopped onions and minced garlic. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] until the onions become translucent and the garlic is fragrant.
# Reduce the heat to low and add the peanut butter to the pot. Stir constantly until the peanut butter melts and combines with the onions and garlic.
# Add the ground cumin, paprika, chili powder, salt, and pepper to the pot. Stir well to incorporate the spices into the peanut sauce. Then add the diced tomatoes, including their juices, and mix everything together
# Gradually pour the beef or chicken broth into the pot, stirring continuously to create a smooth sauce. Return the seared meat to the pot and stir to coat it with the sauce.
# Cover the pot with a lid and let the stew [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] over low heat for about 30 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld together and the meat to become tender.
# After 30 minutes, add the diced carrots, potatoes, bell pepper, okra, and chopped leafy greens to the pot. Stir well, ensuring that all the vegetables are submerged in the sauce.
# Cover the pot again and let the stew simmer for an additional 15–20 minutes, or until the vegetables are cooked to your desired tenderness.
# Remove the pot from heat and let it sit for a few minutes. This allows the stew to thicken slightly. Serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro or parsley.

{{Recipe}} 

'''M'batata''' is a flavorful and creamy soup popular in the Central African Republic. It combines the natural sweetness of sweet potatoes with the richness of peanuts, resulting in a comforting and nourishing dish. 

== Ingredients ==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] cloves, [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 2 large [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potatoes]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Cube|cubed]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] vegetable or chicken [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]]
* 1 cup unsalted [[Cookbook:Peanut|peanuts]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] ground [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]]
* 1 teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile]] powder (optional, for heat)
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]] to taste
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Coconut Milk|coconut milk]] (optional)
* Chopped fresh [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]] or [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]] for [[Cookbook:Garnish|garnish]] (optional)

== Equipment ==

* Large pot
* [[Cookbook:Blender|Blender]] or [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]]
* Wooden spoon or [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* Soup [[Cookbook:Ladle|ladle]]
* [[Cookbook:Potato Masher|Potato masher]] or fork

== Procedure ==

# Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and minced garlic, and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] until the onion becomes translucent and fragrant.
# Add the cubed sweet potatoes to the pot and stir them together with the onions and garlic for a couple of minutes, allowing the flavors to blend.
# Pour in the vegetable or chicken broth, ensuring that the sweet potatoes are fully submerged. Bring the mixture to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] and then reduce the heat to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]]. Let it cook until the sweet potatoes are tender and easily mashed with a fork, usually around 15–20 minutes.
# While the sweet potatoes are cooking, toast the peanuts in a dry skillet over medium heat until they become fragrant and slightly browned. This step helps to enhance the flavor of the peanuts.
# Transfer the toasted peanuts to a blender or food processor and process them until they form a smooth peanut butter-like consistency. You may need to scrape down the sides of the blender or food processor a few times to ensure everything is well blended.
# Once the sweet potatoes are cooked, remove the pot from the heat and allow it to cool slightly. Use a potato masher or the back of a fork to mash the sweet potatoes until they are smooth and creamy in texture.
# Return the pot to low heat and add the peanut butter to the mashed sweet potatoes, stirring well to combine. The soup will become thick and creamy.
# Add the ground cumin, ground coriander, chili powder (if desired), salt, and pepper to the pot. Stir everything together, allowing the flavors to meld for a few minutes.
# If using coconut milk, pour it into the pot and stir it into the soup, adding an extra layer of creaminess and flavor. Simmer the soup for an additional 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
# Taste the soup and adjust the seasonings as needed, adding more salt, pepper, or spices to suit your preference.
# Ladle the m'batata into bowls and [[Cookbook:Garnish|garnish]] with chopped fresh cilantro or parsley, if desired.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* M'batata is best served hot, and it pairs well with crusty bread or a side salad. This comforting soup is a wonderful representation of Central African cuisine, combining the earthy sweetness of sweet potatoes with the richness of peanuts to create a truly delicious and satisfying dish.

{{Recipe}}

'''Lumanda''' is a flavorful Zambian okra [[Cookbook:Stew|stew]] that celebrates the unique taste and texture of okra. This vegetarian stew is made with fresh okra pods, tomatoes, onions, and a blend of aromatic spices. It is a delightful dish often enjoyed with nshima, a popular Zambian staple food.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pepper|hot pepper]], chopped (remove seeds for less heat)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Paprika|ground paprika]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cumin|ground cumin]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Turmeric|ground turmeric]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Coriander|ground coriander]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] fresh [[Cookbook:Okra|okra]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste

== Equipment ==
* Large pot
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]
* [[Cookbook:Wooden Spoon|Wooden spoon]] or [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]]

== Procedure ==
# In a large pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat.
# Add the chopped onion, minced garlic, and chopped hot pepper to the pot. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] until the onions are soft and translucent.
# Stir in the ground paprika, ground cumin, ground turmeric, and ground coriander. Cook for a minute or two to release the flavors of the spices.
# Add the sliced okra and diced tomato to the pot. Stir well to combine the vegetables with the spice mixture.
# Season the stew with salt to taste. Adjust the seasoning according to your preference.
# Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let simmer for about 15–20 minutes, or until the okra is tender and cooked through.
# Stir occasionally during cooking to prevent sticking and to ensure even cooking of the okra and tomatoes.
# Once the stew is ready, remove the pot from the heat and let rest for a few minutes before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* For a thicker stew, you can add a spoonful of cornmeal or cassava meal to the pot during cooking.
* Lumanda is traditionally served with [[Cookbook:Nsima|nshima]], a stiff maize porridge, but it can also be enjoyed with rice or bread.

{{recipe summary
| category = Ugandan recipes
| cuisine = Ugandan
| difficulty = 3
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Luwombo''', a quintessential Ugandan dish, showcases the rich flavors and vibrant culinary traditions of the country. This unique cooking method involves steaming meat, vegetables, and a delightful blend of local spices in banana leaves, infusing the dish with an unmistakably authentic aroma and taste.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (450 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]] or [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], cut into chunks
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] red [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* 1 tablespoon minced [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
*[[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|Cayenne pepper]]
* 2 tablespoons groundnut paste (or [[Cookbook:Peanut Butter|peanut butter]])
* 1 tablespoon groundnut powder (or [[Cookbook:Peanut|peanut]] powder)
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Palm Oil|palm oil]] or [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|groundnut oil]]
* 1 cup diced [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potatoes]]
* 1 cup diced [[Cookbook:Cassava|cassava]]
* 1 cup diced [[Cookbook:Banana|green bananas]] (matooke)
* 1 cup diced [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplant]] 
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Ground Crayfish|ground crayfish]] (optional, for added flavor)
* 1 cup fresh or canned [[Cookbook:Coconut Milk|coconut milk]]
* 1 cup homemade chicken or vegetable [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
* Banana leaves, for wrapping

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook: Knife|Knife]]
* Large [[Cookbook: Mixing Bowl|bowl]]
* [[Cookbook:Steamer|Steamer]] or large pot with a steaming rack

== Procedure ==
# In a large bowl, [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinate]] the meat chunks with minced garlic, minced ginger, groundnut paste, groundnut powder, ground crayfish (if using), salt, and cayenne pepper. Allow the meat to marinate for at least 30 minutes to absorb the flavorful blend.
# Heat palm oil or groundnut oil in a large pot or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated meat and cook until beautifully browned on all sides, releasing an enticing aroma.
# Stir in the diced onions and cook until they soften and become fragrant.
# Add the diced sweet potatoes, cassava, green bananas, and eggplant to the pot.
# Pour in the fresh coconut milk and homemade chicken or vegetable broth, ensuring all the ingredients are immersed in the rich and creamy goodness. Bring the mixture to a gentle [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]].
# Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot with a lid, and let the ingredients [[Cookbook:Steaming|steam]] for about 1–2 hours until the meat is tender.
# Meanwhile, prepare the banana leaves by briefly holding them over an open flame to soften and make them pliable for wrapping.
# Take a portion of the steamed mixture and place it in the center of a banana leaf, folding the leaf around the mixture to create a packet. Repeat with the remaining mixture and banana leaves.
# Once all the packets are prepared, return them to the steamer or large pot with a steaming rack.
# Steam the luwombo packets for an additional 30 minutes.
# Serve the luwombo packets on individual plates.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Luwombo is often enjoyed with steamed rice or matooke, a dish made from green bananas, to complete the authentic Ugandan dining experience.
* Luwombo offers a well-rounded nutritional profile, boasting proteins from the meat and an array of vitamins and minerals from the diverse vegetables used.

{{Recipe}}

== Ingredients ==
* 5–6 [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] thin
* 2–3 green [[Cookbook:Chiles|chiles]], washed and finely [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]] powder
* ½ tsp [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile]] powder
* 1 tsp ground [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]]
* 1 tsp ground [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander]]
* [[Cookbook:Chickpea Flour|Gram flour]]
* [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|Oil]]

== Procedure ==
# Combine onions and chiles. Mix in salt, and let sit 10–15 minutes.
# Mix in turmeric, chili powder, cumin, and coriander. By this time the onion mix should be moist due to added salt and spices. If a moister mix is required, allow to stand another 5 minutes.
# Start adding gram flour to the onion mix a little at a time. The mixture should not be dry. Add the flour just to absorb the moistness. You should end up with a somewhat sticky mixture.
# Heat sufficient oil in a [[Cookbook:Wok|wok]] or [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]]. Once heated sufficiently, carefully take around 2–3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] of hot oil and add to the onion and gram flour mix. Mix well.
# Drop a few small to medium chunks of dough at a time in the medium hot oil. [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] until it gets a golden brown colour. If you have used 4–5 large onions and a medium wok you are likely to need 3–4 batches of frying to finish the mixture.
# Serve hot with green chutney or tomato ketchup.

__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Indian recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{Recipe}}

== Ingredients ==
* [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|Oil]]
* 1–2 large [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplants]]
* 1 handful plus some more finely chopped [[Cookbook:Green Onion|green onion]], both white and green parts
* 2–3 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] finely-[[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Green garlic|green garlic]] (optional)
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] fresh [[Cookbook:Pea|peas]]
* [[Cookbook:Cumin|Cumin]] seeds
* Rai ([[Cookbook:Mustard seed|mustard seed]])
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* 1–2 green [[Cookbook:Chiles|chiles]] broken into 2–3 pieces each
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]] (optional)
* ½ teaspoon red [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile]] powder (optional)

== Procedure ==

=== Raw method ===
# Wash, then wipe dry eggplant. Apply some oil on the surface of each one of them.
# Blacken eggplants over direct heat. Alternatively, char-roast in an [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] or over a fire to infuse smoke.
# Once the skin is blackened and comes away on touch, let them cool a bit and then peel the burnt skin. Reserve the drippings.
# Mash the eggplant flesh by hand until smooth. Transfer flesh to a large bowl.
# Mix in the green onion, green garlic (if using), peas, and salt to taste.
# Heat some oil in a pan. Once heated sufficiently add rai, then cumin seeds, then green chilies. Let the chilies [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] for 10–12 seconds.
# Pour this spice mix onto the eggplant mixture in the bowl. Mix well and serve with bhakri and thecha/kharda below.

=== Frying method ===

# Follow steps 1 through 5 as directed above.
# In the step 6 above add turmeric after chilies. Add the eggplant mixture to the pan of tadka. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] for about 1–2 minutes. If required add some of the reserved eggplant drippings to moisten the bharta.
# Serve hot.

=== Kharda/thecha (accompaniment) ===

# Wash and dry about 10–15 green chilies and half handful of fresh coriander. Peel 5–7 cloves of garlic; break the chilies in to 2–3 pieces each.
# Heat about 1–1½ tbsp of oil on the griddle (tava).
# Once heated sufficiently add chilies and garlic (make sure you have exhaust turned on and working).
# Fry them for 30–40 seconds over low heat. Turn the heat off. Now add salt to taste. Put this mix in a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]] along with chopped coriander and blend it roughly.
# Thecha is ready to serve. While serving put some raw groundnut oil on each serving. This is very very hot dish depending the chilies used. Eat and handle carefully!

A version of lumpia that Filipinos love to share at a party.

==Ingredients==
*½ [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] ground [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]]
*1 medium-sized clove of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], shredded
*1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]], beaten
*Water
*1 pack lumpia or spring roll wrappers
*[[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] banana ketchup

==Procedure==
#Combine the pork, garlic, and carrot in a mixing bowl.
#Add the egg, and mix well to combine.
#Lay one wrapper flat on your work surface. Place a small amount of the filling mixture on it, shaped like a log.
#Fold two opposite sides of the wrapper over the filling to enclose the two ends of the filling. Then, use the rest of the of wrapper to roll everything up length-wise.
#Moisten the edge of the wrapper and press it against the roll to seal and prevent it from unwrapping.
#Repeat the filling and rolling steps with the remaining filling and wrappers.
#[[Cookbook:Deep Fat Frying|Deep fry]] the rolls in the oil until golden brown all over and cooked through.
#Serve with the banana ketchup.

'''Maja blanca''' is a gelatin-like comfort food.

==Ingredients==
*2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|cornstarch]]
*4 cups [[Cookbook:Coconut Milk|coconut milk]]
*1 can (14 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Condensed Milk|sweetened condensed milk]]
*1 can (13.5 oz) [[Cookbook:Coconut Cream|coconut cream]]
*¾ cup white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 cup [[Cookbook:Corn|corn]] kernels (optional)
*¼ cup toasted [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]] flakes (optional)

==Procedure==
#In a bowl, dissolve cornstarch in 1 cup of coconut milk. Set aside.
#In a pot, combine the remaining coconut milk, condensed milk, coconut cream, and sugar. Bring to a gentle [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] over medium heat.
#Gradually pour the cornstarch mixture into the pot while continuously stirring. Lower the heat and continue stirring until the mixture thickens, about 10–15 minutes.
#If desired, add corn kernels into the mixture and stir for an additional 2–3 minutes.
#Pour the mixture into a greased [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|baking dish]] or other mold. Let it cool and set for at least an hour in the refrigerator.
#Once set, slice the pudding into squares and sprinkle toasted coconut flakes on top before serving.

{{recipe}}  | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Beverages|Beverages]] 

'''Masala chai''' is a spiced version of the typical [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian]] [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] [[Cookbook:Tea|tea]]. As with much of Indian cuisine, the exact mix of dry [[Cookbook:Spices|spices]] varies greatly and is often handed down in families from one generation to the next. 

== Ingredients ==

=== Masala mixture ===
* 100 [[Cookbook:g|grams]] powdered [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
* 25 grams [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]]
* 100 grams whole black [[Cookbook:Pepper|peppercorns]]
* 60 grams whole [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]], broken small, or 40 grams ground cinnamon
* ½ seed of [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]], crushed
* 35 grams green [[Cookbook:Cardamom|cardamom]] pods

=== Chai ===
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 1 ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* ¾ teaspoon dried [[Cookbook:Tea|tea]] leaves—to be traditional, a strong Indian tea such as an Assam is best.
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of masala mixture
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]

== Procedure ==

=== Masala ===
# Combine all of the spices, and blend well in an electric grinder. 
# Store the powder in a clean container at room temperature; you only need a small quantity for each cup of chai, and a full recipe will keep you stocked full of chai for months.

=== Chai ===
# [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] water and milk together in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]].
# Add sugar, tea leaves, and masala. Boil until the mixture becomes dark (about 5–10 minutes); the longer you boil, the stronger the chai.
# Strain into teacups to serve.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Let the remaining solids cool and sprinkle them on your plants for an excellent fertiliser.
* Tea masala or garam masala from a store can be used to get around the masala mixture process; however, pre-ground spices lose their flavor over time.
* When making the chai, boil the water and milk separately, and in step two add the tea leaves and masala to the boiling water, boiling until the tea is as strong as you like. Only then add the milk to the mix. This can speed up the process without affecting the flavor. This method is often used by restaurants to serve chai in large quantities quickly as orders are taken.
* Optionally turn off the heat in the end, cover, and let sit for about 5 minutes for a richer flavor.
* Try adjusting the ratio of milk to water. For a richer milky tea, try two parts milk to one part water.
* Leave out the sugar for a more adult flavor. Sugar can be added while drinking if so desired.
* Try other combinations of South Asian spices. Each region in which chai is commonly available has its own popular or traditional spice mix. One optional addition to masala chai is fennel seeds.
* Add a piece of a [[Cookbook:Lemongrass|lemongrass]] leaf (called lili cha in Gujarati), while the water is still boiling (before adding milk). This gives a nice flavor to the tea. Mint, fresh ginger, and/or holy basil (tulsi) can also be added.
* To make ground ginger: Select good quality ginger and wash to remove soils and other foreign objects. Cut into thin slices. Spread evenly in trays. Dry under the sun or in oven under moderate heat or (70ºC). Pulverize using [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]] or grinder. Pack and seal tightly.

'''Atchar''' is a spicy condiment, often eaten with a curry. It comes from the Indian cuisine in South Africa. In India, it is spelled Achar, and the word means pickle in Hindi. Usually the atchar made in South Africa is made with unripe green mangoes and chillies. The whole mango is used for making atchar.

This traditional mango atchar is easily made at home. Adjust the amount of chillies to your liking and serve with a vegetable curry, or on a slice of white bread.

== Ingredients ==

* 1.5 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] unripe [[Cookbook:Mango|mangoes]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] garlic and herb salt
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Chili Powder|chilli powder]]
* 2 Tbsp [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]] powder
* 1 Tbsp ground [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander]]
* 3 Tbsp [[Cookbook:Curry Powder|curry powder]]
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (360 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) raw [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]] or [[Cookbook:Fructose|fructose]]
* 2 cups (480 ml) [[Cookbook:Balsamic vinegar|balsamic vinegar]]
* ½ cup (120 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|corn]] or [[Cookbook:Potato Starch|potato starch]]
* 2 Tbsp [[Cookbook:Mustard seed|mustard seeds]]
* 1 handful [[Cookbook:Curry Leaf|curry leaves]]
* 1½ cups (360 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) virgin [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]] or cold-pressed [[Cookbook:Sunflower Oil|sunflower oil]]

==Procedure==

# [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] all the ingredients except the mangoes and the oil until thickened.
# Pour mixture over the mangoes, add the oil, and mix well.
# Cool and refrigerate for at least 12 hours.

'''Marshmallows''' are a light, spongy confection made primarily with sugar and gelatin, although some recipes contain egg whites.
 
==Ingredients==
*About 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (125 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 4.4 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Powdered Sugar|confectioners' sugar]]
*3 ½ envelopes (2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] plus 2 ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]]) unflavored powdered [[Cookbook:Gelatine|gelatin]]
*½ cup (125 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] / 4.2 oz) cold water
*2 cups (450 g / 16 oz) white [[Cookbook:Granulated Sugar|granulated sugar]]
*½ cup (160 g / 5.6 oz) light [[Cookbook:Corn Syrup|corn syrup]]
*½ cup (125 ml / 4.2 oz) hot water (about 115°F / 46.1°C)
*¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*2 large [[Cookbook:Egg White|egg whites]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Vanilla Extract|vanilla extract]]
*½ cup (125 ml / 4.2 [[Cookbook:Fluid Ounce|fl oz]]) [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]

==Procedure==
#Oil the bottom and sides of a {{convert/3|13|x|9|x|2|in|cm|adj=on}} rectangular metal [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|baking pan]], and [[Cookbook:Dusting|dust]] the bottom and sides with some confectioners' sugar.
#In bowl of standing electric mixer or in a large bowl, sprinkle gelatin over cold water and let stand to soften.
#In a 3 [[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] (2.8 L) heavy [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], cook granulated sugar, corn syrup, hot water, and salt over low heat, stirring with a wooden spoon, until sugar is dissolved. 
#Increase heat to moderate and [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] mixture, without stirring, until a candy or digital [[Cookbook:Thermometer|thermometer]] registers {{convert|240|F|C}}, about 12 minutes. Remove pan from heat and pour sugar mixture over gelatin mixture, stirring until gelatin is dissolved.
#Using a standing or a hand-held electric [[Cookbook:Mixer|mixer]], [[Cookbook:Whipping|whip]] mixture on high speed until white, thick and nearly tripled in volume (about 6–10 minutes). 
#In a large bowl with cleaned beaters, whip whites (or reconstituted powdered whites) until they just hold stiff peaks. Beat whites and vanilla into sugar mixture until just combined. 
#Pour mixture into baking pan and [[Cookbook:Sifting|sift]] ¼ cup confectioners' sugar evenly over top. Cool marshmallow, uncovered, until firm (at least 3 hours and up to 1 day).
#Run a thin knife around edges of pan and invert pan onto large cutting board. Lifting up 1 corner of inverted pan, with fingers loosen marshmallow and let drop onto cutting board. 
#With a large knife trim edges of marshmallow and cut marshmallows into roughly 1-inch cubes. Sift remaining confectioners' sugar into a large bowl and add marshmallows in batches, tossing to evenly coat.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* Try coating with toasted [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]] or [[Cookbook:Cocoa Powder|cocoa powder]] instead of powdered sugar.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian Cuisine]]

'''Marsala chicken scallopini''' is a meal in the style of Italian cuisine, with mouthwatering flavors gotten from the fortified Marsala wine.

==Ingredients==
*2 boneless skinless [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] breasts
* 4 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 3 tsp [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] dry [[Cookbook:Marsala Wine|marsala wine]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]]/chicken [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] of fresh [[Cookbook:Asparagus|asparagus]]
* [[Cookbook:Parsley|Parsley]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
* [[Cookbook:Flour|Flour]]
* [[Cookbook:Oregano|Oregano]]
* Fresh [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]]

==Procedure==
# Put each chicken breast in a plastic bag and flatten with a meat tenderizer. 
# Coarsely [[Cookbook:Chop|chop]] the basil, and then throw it in a deep [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|baking pan]] along with some flour, oregano. [[Cookbook:Mixing#Tossing|Toss]] the chicken with it.
# Melt 2 tsp of butter in a medium [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] on low-medium heat. When the butter stops bubbling, add the chicken and brown each section for approximately 3 minutes on each side. Once this is done, cover and set aside on a separate plate.
# Drain off most of the liquid from the pan, and raise the heat. Pour a dollop of olive oil in, and [[Cookbook:Searing|sear]] the asparagus quickly. Remove this and set aside.
# Keep at high heat, add the marsala and ¼ of the stock. [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] off for a few minutes. Lower the heat, and return the asparagus to the pan. Add the remaining stock and boil off to reduce. Add a tsp of butter, and cover chicken with sauce.
# Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* At various points during the cooking, you may want to grind some fresh pepper and sprinkle salt over top of the sauce or chicken; do so according to your tastes.

== Ingredients ==

* 6 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]]
* 8 [[Cookbook:Oz|oz]] (200 [[Cookbook:G|g]]) [[Cookbook:Paneer|paneer]], cut in 1” [[Cookbook:Cube|cubes]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Ginger Garlic Paste|ginger-garlic paste]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]]
* 1 cup puréed [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
* 3 green [[Cookbook:Chile|chilies]], seeded and finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]] seeds
* ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Tumeric|turmeric]] powder
* ½ teaspoon red [[Cookbook:Chili Powder|chilli powder]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander]] powder
* Garam masala
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Pea|peas]]
* ¾ cup (200 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 1 tablespoon chopped [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander]]

== Procedure<ref>https://www.yumcurry.com/matar-paneer.htm/</ref> ==

=== '''Frying paneer''' ===
#Heat some oil in a deep pan.
#Add paneer cubes in it. [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] on all the sides over medium-low heat until golden brown.
#Remove paneer from the pan, and drain on [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towels]].

=== '''Gravy''' ===
#Remove excess oil from the same pan, and add ginger-garlic paste.
#Add chopped onion to it. Cook, stirring, until onion becomes translucent.
#Add chopped tomatoes and mix. Cook well over medium heat.
#Turn off the heat when tomatoes have left all the water. Let cool.
#Transfer mixture to a blender, and add the chiles.
#Blend until smooth.

=== '''Matar paneer''' ===
#Heat oil in a pan.
#Add cumin seeds, and fry until they start to crackle.
#Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, and garam masala. Mix well over low heat.
#Add the blended purée, and mix well over medium heat.
#Season with salt, then mix in the peas.
#Add some water, cover, and [[Cookbook:Steaming|steam]] until the peas are fully cooked.
#Uncover and add the fried paneer. Mix well, adding more water if required.

=== '''Tadka''' ===
#Heat a small pan/tadka pan.
#Add 1 tsp oil and ½ tsp red chilli powder. Mix well.
#Turn off the gas and add to the matar paneer while serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* [[Cookbook:Paneer|Paneer]] is a pressed uncured cheese usually made fresh. It can be bought in Indian or specialty grocery stores or substituted by [[Cookbook:tofu|tofu]] if unavailable.

{{recipesummary|category=Bean recipes|time=7 hours|difficulty=2}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:North American cuisines|North American Cuisines]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Ontario|Cuisine of Ontario]]

'''Maple beans''' is a modification of the standard [[Cookbook:Baked Beans | Baked Beans]] made throughout much of Europe and North America. This variant is common through south and central Quebec as well as most of Ontario and can be purchased in cans across Canada.

==Ingredients==

* 625 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (2 ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]]) small dried white beans
* 2 L (8 cups) water
* 1 large sweet [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely diced
* 250 ml (1 cup) [[Cookbook:Maple Syrup|maple syrup]]
* 30 ml (2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]]) dark [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
* 30 ml (2 Tbsp) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 2 ml (½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]]) dry [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]]
* 5 ml (½ tsp) ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
* 5 ml (1 tsp) [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 6 slices side [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]] OR 60 ml (¼ cup) bacon runoff
==Procedure==

# Wash beans and place in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] with the water. Cover and bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], checking regularly.
# When water has reached the boiling point, time for 5 minutes and remove from heat. Let sit for 1 hour, covered.
# After the hour, return beans and water to heat and bring to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]], still covered. Simmer for 45 minutes.
# Strain beans and water through a [[Cookbook:Colander|colander]], collecting the liquids in a bowl for later use.
# Combine the onion, salt, mustard, and maple syrup. Add 625 ml (2 ½ cups) of the aforementioned bean-water to the mix and blend well.
# Finely slice the bacon, place in roast pan/casserole dish, and cover with the beans, pouring the liquid mixture over top.
# Cover and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] for 3 hours at 165°C (325°F), adding 125 ml (½ cup) of bean-water at the 2 ½ hour mark.
# Melt butter and combine with brown sugar. Pour over the baked beans and bake, uncovered, until liquid is no longer visible.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* You can substitute [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]] or molasses for the maple syrup; maple is used for it's flavouring as much as its sweetness.
* Margarine or vegetable oil will do as well as butter for this; butter was used traditionally and is thus listed.
* This is often served with [[Cookbook:Ham |ham]] and [[Cookbook:Sweet Cornbread |sweet cornbread]].
