This '''prickly pear soda''' is popular in Mexico and the Southwestern United States. 

==Ingredients==
* 3 [[Cookbook:Prickly Pear|prickly pears]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) water
* ½ cup (120 ml) [[Cookbook:Agave Syrup|agave nectar]]
* [[Cookbook:Carbonated Water|Carbonated water]] as needed (see note)

==Procedure==
# Remove the peel from the prickly pears, cut them into small pieces about 0.5 x 0.5 in (1.25 x 1.25 cm), and remove the seeds.
# Combine the fruit flesh, water, and agave nectar in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]].
# [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] the mixture until it becomes very thick, then [[Cookbook:Sieve|strain]] it to get approximately 5 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (120 ml) of syrup.
# Make the finished soda by combining 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of carbonated water.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Use water from a carbonating machine or a brand of pure carbonated water such as Polar Original sparkling water, Great Value Seltzer Water, or Signature Select Seltzer Water. Do not use a brand of mineral water such as Perrier, San Pellegrino, or Mineragua because the added minerals will ruin the taste. Avoid flavored sparkling water such as La Croix or Spindrift, because the preexisting fruit flavors will ruin the drink.

Similar to a sandwich, the amount of ingredients for a '''quesadilla''' depends on how many you are serving and how big you want to make a particular quesadilla. Here are ingredients for one serving using the typical size of tortillas most commonly available in stores in the southwestern U.S. (and in many other areas and countries). Other locally available thin flat breads may work instead of work of tortillas, but please know, the tortillas are intended to be similar to a 'wrap' to allow the eating of the filling.

==Ingredients==

=== Base ===
*2 flour [[Cookbook:Tortilla|tortillas]], 6 [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]] (15 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]) in diameter
*⅓ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]] meltable [[Cookbook:cheese|cheese]] (preferably a [[Cookbook:Monterey Jack Cheese|Monterey Jack]] and [[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|cheddar]] blend or a Tex Mex blend) 
*¼ cup filling (see options below)
*[[Cookbook:Cooking Spray|Cooking spray]]

=== Fillings ===
*[[Cookbook:Salsa|Salsa]]
* [[Cookbook:Sarza Criolla|Sarza criolla]]
* [[Cookbook:Chiles|Chile peppers]]
* [[Cookbook:Chopping|Chopped]] [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]] and [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]]
* Cooked [[Cookbook:Meat and Poultry|meat or seafood]]
* Fresh [[Cookbook:Spinach|spinach]], washed and torn into small pieces
* Canned [[Cookbook:Black Bean|black beans]], rinsed and well drained

== Procedure ==
#Warm both tortillas in the [[Cookbook:Microwave|microwave]] to the point of flexibility, keeping one warm.
#Preheat a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] or [[Cookbook:Griddle|griddle]] over medium-low heat. Grease with oil or cooking spray, and place one of the tortillas in the pan.
#Sprinkle the shredded cheese over the tortilla.
#Top the cheese with any combination of the fillings, ideally warmed and very well drained. Make sure they are evenly distributed across the tortilla.
# Allow the cheese to melt. The tortilla may brown in spots but it should not be cooked to the point of changing color substantially.
#Press the other tortilla over the top of the tortilla in the pan, making sure it sticks a bit.
#Flip the quesadilla and allow to warm until it joins as a unit.
#Remove from pan and cut in eight wedges.
#Eat immediately, or remove to a fairly low-temperature 'keep warm' area, below the melting temperature of the cheese.
==Notes, tips, and variations==

* Quesadillas are not usually not very good re-heated.
* In some regions of Mexico a quesadilla is a simple corn tortilla with cheese, non-fried.
* One traditional quesadilla filling consists of grilled chicken, beef, or pork, finely minced, sprinkled with a teaspoon of finely minced onion and half of teaspoon of cilantro, with a small amount of some lime squeezed on top.
* Corn tortillas can be used in a pinch at home, but they may not hold together or work as well as flour tortillas.
* See [[Cookbook:Crab Quesadillas with Mango Salsa|Crab Quesadillas with Mango Salsa]] for a variation.

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] dry split [[Cookbook:Pea|peas]]
*Water
*[[Cookbook:Chicken Broth|Chicken broth]]
*[[Cookbook:Carrot|Carrot]], [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]]
*[[Cookbook:Onion|Onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*1 white [[Cookbook:Turnip|turnip]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
*3 stalks [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]], chopped
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
*[[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
*Ground [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]]
*[[Cookbook:Tumeric|Turmeric]]
*[[Cookbook:Nutmeg|Nutmeg]]
*[[Cookbook:Cumin|Cumin]]
*[[Cookbook:Curry Powder|Curry powder]]
*[[Cookbook:Cornstarch|Cornstarch]]
*[[Cookbook:Sour Cream|Sour cream]], as a garnish

==Procedure==

# Add the split peas to a pot. Add the chicken broth and enough water to cover the peas.
# Bring the peas to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], then remove from the heat and let soak.
# Prepare equal quantities of grated carrot and chopped onion.
# Add the carrot, onion, turnip, and celery to the split peas. Mix in salt, pepper, cloves, turmeric, nutmeg, cumin, and curry powder.
# [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] everything slowly for about an hour, or until the vegetables are well softened. Adjust seasoning to taste.
# Make a mixture of cornstarch and water with the consistency of thin cream.
# Bring the split peas to a simmer. Mix in the cornstarch slurry, and cook for a minute or two until thickened.
# Adjust the consistency with stock (or milk) as desired.
# Serve hot. If desired, garnish with a floating dab of sour cream and a light sprinkling of nutmeg.

These muffins make a good [[Cookbook:Breakfast|breakfast]] for a family. They go well with [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]].

==Ingredients==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Whole Wheat|whole wheat]] [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 1 cup (240 g) [[Cookbook:Rolled Oats|rolled oats]] (traditional slow type)
* ⅓ cup (80 g) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] (10 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]
* ¾ cup (180 ml) [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* ¼ cup (60 ml) [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]]
* ½–1 cup (120–240g) [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]]
* [[Cookbook:Butter|Butter]] for the pan

==Procedure==

#Pre-heat an [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven_temperatures|375°F]] (190°C).
#Butter a [[Cookbook:Muffin Pan|muffin pan]] or [[Cookbook:Cupcake Pan|cupcake pan]].
#Place the dry ingredients in one bowl, and the wet ingredients in a different bowl.
#Mix the ingredients in each bowl, then combine the mixtures to make a [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]].
#Spoon batter into the pan.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 20 minutes, or until brown with crispy edges.
#Immediately flip the muffins upside-down using a butter knife. Leave them in the hot pan to prevent condensation from ruining the surface.
#Muffins are best served hot!

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Follow the above recipe with the following ingredient adjustments:
** {{convert|140|g|oz}} whole wheat [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
** {{convert|120|g|oz}} rolled oats
** {{convert|75|g|oz}} sugar
** {{convert|40|-|80|g|oz}} raisins

| Difficulty = 4
| Image = [[File:Pupusas.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisines|Cuisines]]

A '''pupusa''' is a stuffed [[Cookbook:Tortilla|corn-tortilla]], usually served with a spicy [[Cookbook:Coleslaw|coleslaw]] called [[Cookbook:Curtido|curtido]]. Pupusas originated in El Salvador, but immigrants have taken the dish to other Central American countries and beyond. Pupusas are hand-made and thick. Like all corn tortillas, they are made using [[Cookbook:Corn Masa|corn masa]]. They are stuffed with one or more of the following: 
*[[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]] ''(queso)'' (usually a soft Salvadoran cheese called Quesillo)
*[[Cookbook:Frying|fried]] pork rind ''(chicharrones)''
*[[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] ''(pollo)''
*[[Cookbook:Refried Beans|refried beans]] ''(frijoles refritos)''
*''queso y Loroco'' (loroco is a shrub flower bud from Central America)
There are also the ''pupusa revueltas'' (with mixed ingredients of cheese, pork, and [[Cookbook:Bean|beans]]). Pupusas are usually served with curtido and [[Cookbook:Tomato Sauce|tomato sauce]]. They are eaten with the fingers.

== Ingredients ==

=== Dough ===

* [[Cookbook:Corn Masa|Corn masa]]
* Water

===Cheese filling===
*3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] of shredded [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]] (use a combination of hard and soft cheese; you can mix frying cheese, [[Cookbook:Mozzarella Cheese|mozzarella]], and [[Cookbook:Ricotta|ricotta]])
*3–4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] of [[Cookbook:Heavy Cream|heavy cream]]
*½–1 cup of ''[[Cookbook:Loroco|loroco]]'' (this can be hard to source, so you can use very finely chopped [[Cookbook:Green Pepper|green peppers]] or [[Cookbook:Scallion|scallions]] instead)
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste

===Chicharron (pork rind filling)===
*1 cup [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]]
*[[Cookbook:Garlic|Garlic]] (optional), [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
*4–5 [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Green Pepper|green pepper]]
*Salt to taste

===Revueltas filling===

* Ground and [[Cookbook:Frying|fried]] beans (can be canned or prepared from your favorite recipe)

==Procedure==

=== Dough ===

# Follow the instructions on the bag of masa for making tortilla [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]], and make as much dough as needed. One pupusa uses about as much dough as two tortillas.
# Set the dough aside while you prepare the filling.

=== Cheese filling ===

# Make a paste with all of the ingredients. To avoid the paste leaking out of the pupusas, it should not be too soft.

=== Chicharron filling ===

# Cook the bacon with some garlic. Set [[Cookbook:Fat|fat]] aside but do not discard.
# Once cooked, grind bacon with the tomatoes, green pepper, and salt to taste.
# Mix in some of the bacon fat until it has a soft consistency.

=== Revueltas filling ===

# Prepare the ground and [[Cookbook:Frying|fried]] beans as desired.

=== Assembly ===

# Shape and fill 2 tbsp of the dough per pupusa using one of the two methods below. When filling the pupusas add some of the bean, chicharrón, and/or cheese fillings.
#* Beginner method: Shape the dough into a ball, and clap it between your hands until you make a round, thin tortilla about ⅛ in thick. Continue making more tortillas this way. Put some filling on one tortilla, cover with another, and press the sides to seal them.
#* Experienced method: Shape the dough into a ball, then insert your thumb in the ball to make a hole in the center. Fill the hole with some filling, and seal the hole by pushing and pinching the dough on the sides up. Carefully clap the pupusa between your hands to flatten it without pressing out the filling.
# Cook the pupusas on a lightly greased [[Cookbook:Griddle|griddle]], [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|pan]], or electric pancake griddler over low-medium heat ([[Cookbook:Oven Temperatures|325–350°F]]) on one side, then the other until they are cooked. Each side will be ready when it no longer sticks to the pan (depending on the thickness of the tortillas, this might take 4 minutes or more per side).
# Top the pupusas with [[Cookbook:Curtido|curtido]] and tomato sauce.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* There are different brands of corn masa to make the dough. MASECA, which can be found in most large American supermarkets in the international section, is one of them but there are others.
* If you can find it, try replacing the cheese filling with prepared ''queso con loroco''. You won't get the authentic flavor from a pupusa if you use American ingredients.

==Ingredients==

*¼–½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] extra-virgin [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
*6 [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] cloves, [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
*1 can (28 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] / 830 g) crushed [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
*½ cup [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] pitted Kalamata [[Cookbook:Olive|olives]]

*1 teaspoon dried [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]]
*⅛ teaspoon [[Cookbook:pepper|pepper]]
*2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]

==Procedure==

# Heat oil in a large [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]]. 
# Add garlic and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] over medium heat until garlic starts to brown lightly. 
# Add oregano, pepper, olives, capers, and tomatoes. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] for about 15 minutes. 
# Add parsley and cook for another 2 minutes. 
# Add salt to taste. 
# Pour over 1 pound (450 g) of cooked [[Cookbook:Pasta|pasta]], and serve.

'''Queen's Soup''', or ''Zuppa Regina di Riso'', is a rice soup. One recipe is as follows.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] ground [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Pint|pint]] (285 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (30 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* Fowl (poultry) [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]]

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Saucepan|Saucepan]]
* [[Cookbook:Bain-marie|Bain-marie]]
* [[Cookbook:Sieve|Sieve]]

== Procedure ==
# Put the ground rice into a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]. Gradually add the milk.
# Cook gently for 12 minutes in a [[Cookbook:Bain-marie|bain-marie]], stirring the whole time, until very smooth.
# Add the butter, and pass through a [[Cookbook:Sieve|sieve]].
# Mix the fowl stock, and serve immediately.

{{recipe}}

'''Rainbow Jell-O''' is a multilayered, multiflavored Jell-O extravaganza based on a recipe from [http://www.kraftfoods.com/main.aspx?s=recipe&m=recipe/knet_recipe_display&u1=keyword&u2=rainbow&u3=**6*6&wf=9&recipe_id=50315 Kraft]. This recipe takes about five hours to prepare, although the time is spent largely in waiting; it is therefore best to plan to intersperse it with other activity and, if they don't mind the constant smell of Jell-O, best done with other people. It yields ten layers (or as many as you want), alternating opaque and clear, of five colors. The sour cream or yogurt, used for opacity, cannot be tasted in the final product.

== Ingredients ==

*6 ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (about 1.5 [[Cookbook:Liter|L]]) [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]] water
*5 (or more) packages Jell-O flavored gelatin (4-serving-size each; different flavors and colors)
*1 cup (240 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Sour Cream|sour cream]] or plain or vanilla [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yogurt]]

== Procedure ==

# Select one or more molds. The total volume will be approximately 8 cups; a ring mold, 2–3 glass containers (as pictured), or any other assortment should work; for best results, the container should be at least 3 [[Cookbook:Inch|in]] (10 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]) deep, allowing for about ten 1cm-thick layers.
# Stir 1¼ cups boiling water and one package gelatin in a small bowl for at least 2 minutes, until completely dissolved. In practice, it may not quite completely dissolve.
# Pour ¾ cups dissolved gelatin into the mold(s).
# Refrigerate for about 15 minutes, until the gelatin sets but is not yet firm: the gelatin should stick to your finger when you touch it. The aim is for the layers to stick, but not mix.
# Refrigerate the remaining gelatin for about 5 minutes, until it is slightly thickened (to the consistency of unbeaten egg white).
# Gradually stir 3 tablespoons sour cream or yogurt into the remaining, thickened gelatin.
# Spoon the gelatin on top of the previous layer (gently, so as to maintain a smooth surface).
# Refrigerate again for about 15 minutes.
# Repeat the above layering process for each of the remaining flavors. Be sure to cool adequately between layers to prevent melting and mixing.
# Refrigerate for about 2 hours, until firm.
# Remove the gelatin from the mold and place it (probably upside down) on a plate or smooth cutting board. Store refrigerated under [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|saran wrap]] or [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|aluminum foil]]. For best effect, serve sliced perpendicular to the layers, so each slice (approximately 1 cm thick) displays the full rainbow.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Cuisine of India]] | [[Cookbook:Bread|Bread]]

'''Puri''', also spelled '''poori''' is a fried [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian]] [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]].

==Ingredients==

* 2 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (60 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Whole Wheat|whole-wheat flour]]
* 2 oz (60 g) [[Cookbook:Flour#Wheat Flour|plain white flour]]
* 2 oz fine [[Cookbook:Semolina|semolina]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]] for the dough
* About 500 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (1 [[Cookbook:Pint|pint]]) vegetable oil for [[Cookbook:Deep Fat Frying|deep frying]]
* [[Cookbook:Water|Water]] to mix the dough

==Procedure==

===Dough===
# Put all the dry ingredients into a bowl. 
# Add salt and drizzle the 1 tbsp oil over top. Mix well.
# Gradually mix in enough water to get a stiff [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] the dough well for a few minutes.
# Cover the dough and leave to rest for about half an hour.

===Frying===
# Pour the oil for deep frying in a wok or other deep pan. Heat the oil.
# Meanwhile, divide the dough into 8 small balls and roll each into a small circle (about 3 [[Cookbook:Inch|in]] / 7.5 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] in diameter). You can use a bit of hot oil to roll the dough so it will not stick to the surface. 
# Check if the oil is hot enough—when you put a tiny piece of dough in the oil it should immediately rise to the surface. When the oil is ready, lay the flattened dough over the oil, press the top slightly with the slotted spoon until it inflates itself, and turn to other side. Adjust the flame as necessary.
# Remove the puri from the oil after it turns golden brown and place on a wire rack or kitchen paper towel for excess oil to drain.

==Notes, tips and variations==
* For chapatti dough, don't use semolina and plain flour. Only use whole wheat flour, salt, and oil.
* If the dough sinks quickly to the bottom of the wok, the oil is not hot enough and the puri will absorb too much oil. It should balloon within a few seconds.

{{recipe}}
__NOTOC__
==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:rabbit|rabbit]]
*[[Cookbook:Onion|Onions]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*[[Cookbook:Carrot|Carrots]], chopped
*1–2 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. St. Sixtus 8 degree abbey [[Cookbook:Beer|beer]]
*Prepared [[Cookbook:mustard|mustard]]
*2 slices of old [[Cookbook:bread|bread]]

==Procedure==
#Divide the rabbit into practical pieces.
#Cook the onions and carrots in a large pot until colored.
#Add the portions of rabbit to the pot, and [[Cookbook:Searing|sear]] the meat.
#Add the 1–2 beers depending on the size of your pot and how big the rabbit was. The rabbit does not need to be completely submerged.
#Spread mustard onto the sliced bread, and lay those on top of the mixture. Seal the pot with [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|aluminum foil]] and a lid.
#Stew for several (2–3) hours over low heat.
#Cool the stew and serve it the following day.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*Do take care to check the stew from time to time, and stir to avoid burning things.
*Do not serve the same day—leave it to cool overnight, and serve the next day.
*You can also freeze it. Like most stews, it will taste even better when you defrost it.
*It can be served with mashed potatoes and the onions and carrots from the stew.
*One might consider using a [[Cookbook:Pressure Cooker|pressure cooker]], but those are usually quite tall for this recipe. It might work better with a big diameter pot, that's not too tall, hence the foil and lid recommendation. Besides, a pressure cooker will cook too fast, which is not ideal for a stew.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Radish_Pie|Radish Pie]]

'''Radish pie''' is a savory [[Cookbook:Pie|pie]] suitable for a vegetarian diet.  Radishes, fresh goat cheese, and walnuts give the pie a unique taste, which is most flavorful when served cold.

==Ingredients==
*1–2 bunches red [[Cookbook:Radish|radish]]es
*1–2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
*¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (60 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], divided
*8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (227 g) [[Cookbook:Phyllo Dough|phyllo]] dough
*1 red [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] dry [[Cookbook:Sherry|sherry]] wine
*2 large [[Cookbook:egg|egg]]s
*1 [[Cookbook:Egg Yolk|yolk]]
*¾ cup (177 ml) heavy [[Cookbook:cream|cream]]
*4 oz (113 g) fresh goat [[Cookbook:cheese|cheese]] 
*¾ cup (177 ml) broken [[Cookbook:walnuts|walnut]] pieces
*⅓ cup (80 ml) fresh Italian [[Cookbook:parsley|parsley]]

==Procedure==
[[File:RadishPieSlice250px.jpg|thumb|250x250px|Slice of radish pie]]
#Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 350°F (175°C).
#Wash the radishes well, remove and discard tops. Put radishes into a small [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|baking dish]] and drizzle with olive oil. [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for about an hour. Let them cool and then cut into small cubes.
#Use half the butter to grease a [[Cookbook:Pie and Tart Pans|pie pan]], and then line it with pieces of [[wikipedia:Phyllo|phyllo dough]], covering the pan evenly. Tuck any stray bits under to make a nice edge.
#Heat the remaining butter in a large pan and sauté the onion in it for about 5 minutes. Add the wine and diced radishes, then cook for another minute. Remove from heat and pour into the pastry shell.
#In a bowl, mix together the eggs and cream, and then pour over the vegetables in the pie crust. Crumble the goat cheese over the cream.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] the pie in a preheated oven at aforementioned temperature for 20 minutes.
#Add the walnuts and bake for another 15–20 minutes.
#Remove the pie from the oven and top it with the chopped parsley.
#Let cool completely before serving.
==Notes, tips, and variations==
*Use fewer radishes for milder taste, or add more according to your own taste.
*The radishes can be baked the day before and then refrigerated until you make the pie.
*For a professional look, garnish each serving with a sprig of parsley.

{{recipe}}

'''Radish tart''' is a tasty and colorful [[Cookbook:Pie|pie]], best served hot from the oven. Fresh red radishes and yellow cheese give this pretty pie an interesting look and taste.

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
*½ cup cold [[Cookbook:butter|butter]]
*1 cup (4 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) shredded Edam, Gouda, or Gruyere [[Cookbook:cheese|cheese]], divided ([[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|Cheddar]] is also acceptable)
*1 cup heavy [[Cookbook:cream|cream]], divided
*4 [[Cookbook:egg|egg]] yolks
*¼ tsp [[Cookbook:salt|salt]]
*½–1 small bunch of red [[Cookbook:radish|radishes]]

==Procedure==
#Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 425°F (220°C).
#[[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] and measure flour into a bowl. Cut in the butter until the particles are coarse. Stir in half of the cheese. Pour in ¼ cup of the cream; [[Cookbook:Mixing#Tossing|toss]] the mixture with a fork until all parts are moistened.
#Turn the dough into a 9-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] round [[Cookbook:Pie and Tart Pans|pie pan]]. With floured fingers, press the mixture into the bottom and sides of the pan, then prick the shell with a floured fork.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] the pie shell for 10–12 minutes. The sides will slip down a little during baking. Cool on a [[Cookbook:Cooling Rack|wire rack]].
#Lower the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C).
#Sprinkle the remaining cheese evenly over the bottom of the cooled pie shell. [[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] together the egg yolks, the ¾ cup cream, and the salt. Pour the egg mixture over the cheese. Place the radish slices evenly over the top of the pie.
#Bake for 20–25 minutes, or until set.
#Remove the pie from the oven, cut it into wedges, and serve it hot. 

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*If you really like the taste of radishes, use ½ cup or more. For a milder pie, use ¼ cup.
*The cheese crust has a pleasant crisp texture when eaten fresh out of the oven. Leftovers can be refrigerated and reheated later, but the texture will not be as good.
*A really sharp knife will aid in cutting the wedges without displacing the radishes.

''I first came up to the idea of the pitta as I found that chopped-up Quorn pieces available from supermarkets taste (after microwaving without additives) quite bad. After adding ketchup, it tasted way better, so I started thinking and experimenting and finally came up with blending tomato paste, vinegar, garlic and some red peppers (similar to a regular taco-mix). This sauce I made is however not made with sugar and not greasy (unlike ketchup). I added the whole in a pitta, as this is widely available (you may use other oven-baked breads too). As certain nutritionist organisations have their own version of pitta too to include in their diets, and as the ingredients used here are even better in quality.''

'''Queen of puddings''' is a favourite English bread pudding served with an apricot glaze and a soft [[Cookbook:Meringue|meringue]] topping.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] / 85 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) white [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* Zest of 1 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]
* 2 oz (4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]] / 55 g) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 6 oz (about 4 cups / 170 g) freshly-grated [[Cookbook:Bread Crumb|bread crumbs]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], [[Cookbook:Separating Eggs|separated]]
* 4 Tbsp raspberry [[Cookbook:Jam|jam]], or jam of choice
* 2 Tbsp [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] sugar

== Procedure ==
# Heat the milk, sugar, lemon zest and butter until just below the [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
# Pour onto the bread crumbs and allow the whole to cool slightly, about 10 minutes.
# [[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] the egg yolks and stir into the bread crumb and milk mixture.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at 350°F (180°C) for 35 minutes.
# Remove from the oven and let cool for 10 minutes.
# Spread the top with the warmed jam, being careful not to break the surface of the pudding.
# [[Cookbook:Whipping|Whip]] the egg whites with the vanilla sugar and a few drops of lemon juice until the mixture reaches soft peaks.
# Spread the meringue over the top of the pudding. Return to the oven and bake for 15 minutes until the meringue has browned.
# Serve as is or with [[Cookbook:Crème anglaise|''crème anglaise'']].

'''Racuszki''' are [[Cookbook:Pancake|pancakes]] made from [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]] fried on a hot griddle or a pan. They are a traditional Polish dish, but they exist in several variations in many different local [[Cookbook:Cuisine|cuisine]]s, such as Danish [http://xphiles.typepad.com/table/2006/04/easter_ebleskiv.html|Ebleskivers]. Usually the form varies from small pancakes or something akin to donuts, and the filling can change as well (e.g. apple and cinnamon, raisins, etc.).

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Liter|L]] sour milk or cultured [[Cookbook:Buttermilk|buttermilk]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] white [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
*1½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Eggs|eggs]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Kg|kg]] [[Cookbook:Apple|apples]] (optional), [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] (optional)
*½ cup [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]] (optional)

==Procedure==
#In large bowl, [[Cookbook:Mix|mix]] the baking soda, salt, and flour together well.
#Add sour milk and eggs, and [[Cookbook:Mix|mix]] until smooth.
#Pour small ladlefuls of the mixture into a [[Cookbook:Non-stick|non-stick]] pan, one at a time OR dip slices of peeled apples in batter and put them in the pan.
#Cook until the edges are dry. Turn; cook until golden.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Serve with sugar, butter, maple syrup, melted chocolate, or jam. Sugar is traditional, and some people eat them without toppings.
* Racuszki do not store well.
* Use [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yogurt]] or cultured [[Cookbook:Buttermilk|buttermilk]] if you do not have sour milk, but do not replace it with normal milk.
* Cooking apples are preferred, if using.

{{recipe}}

== Ingredients ==

=== Meat filling ===
*[[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|Oil]]
*[[Cookbook:Butter|Butter]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. small [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] lean [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]]
*2 rashers rindless smoked back [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]], finely chopped
*2 heaped [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] grated salt-cured [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]] (e.g. sheep or goat's milk, or [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|Parmigiano-Reggiano]])
*1 slice of day old [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]], soaked in [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] and wrung out
*1 tbsp chopped flat-leaf [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]] leaves
*2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], beaten
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] 
*[[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]] 

=== Ricotta filling ===
*450 g well-drained fresh sheep's milk [[Cookbook:Ricotta|ricotta]]
*100 g grated [[Cookbook:Pecorino Romano Cheese|Pecorino cheese]] (Romano type or with peppercorns)
*2 tbsp chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley or [[Cookbook:Marjoram|marjoram]]
*2 eggs, beaten
*Salt
*Pepper

=== Meat and rice filling ===
*2 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], minced
*1 cup uncooked round or long-grain [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
*1 cup Bolognese-type meat sauce
*½ cup water
*½ tsp [[Cookbook:Mixed Spice|mixed spice]]
*1 large egg, beaten
*Salt
*Pepper

=== Assembly ===

* 1 kg [[Cookbook:Zucchini|zucchini]] or other firm, large [[Cookbook:Squash|squash]]
* 1 cup fresh tomato sauce
* Dry [[Cookbook:Bread Crumb|breadcrumbs]] or medium-coarse [[Cookbook:Semolina|semolina]]
* Grated cheese

=== Optional ingredients ===

* [[Cookbook:Potato|Potatoes]], sliced medium-thick
* [[Cookbook:Onion|Onions]], sliced
* Salt
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
* [[Cookbook:Caraway|Caraway seed]]
* Stock or water

== Procedure ==

=== Meat filling ===

# [[Cookbook:Sweating|Sweat]] the chopped onion in a mixture of oil and butter.
# Combine the onion with the minced pork, bacon, cheese, soaked bread, parsley, eggs, salt, and pepper.
# Reserve.

=== Ricotta filling ===

# Combine the ricotta, grated cheese, parsley, eggs, salt, and pepper.
# Reserve.

=== Meat and rice filling ===

# Combine all ingredients together.
# Reserve.

=== Assembly ===

# Depending on the size of the squash, either cut off a lid and use whole or else cut in half.
# Carefully scoop out the squash flesh, leaving a 1 cm thick shell or boat to fill. The removed flesh can be diced and added to the filling ingredients if desired.
# Fill each hollowed squash with some of one of the fillings. Do not fill to the top, as the eggs (and rice if using) will expand.
# Combine the breadcrumbs and grated cheese. Dip the top of each filled squash in the topping ingredients (or sprinkle evenly on top) to help seal the filling in.

=== Cooking ===

# Cook the filled squash in one of the following three ways:
#* '''Baking (suitable for all 3 fillings):''' Place a layer of sliced potatoes and onions in a baking dish. Season with salt, pepper, and caraway seed, and moisten with stock. Place the stuffed squash on top. Cover with foil, and bake 30 minutes at 180˚C. Remove the foil and continue baking for about 10-15 minutes to crisp the top.
#* '''Pot roasting (suitable for all 3 fillings):''' Closely pack the stuffed squash in a pot. Fill with water to just over halfway up the squash. Cover with a lid, and cook on medium heat until the squashes are tender and the rice or meat filling cooked through (about 35 minutes).
#* '''Simmering (not suitable for ricotta filling):''' Place carefully-sealed squash in a simmering meat [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]] (made with root vegetables and meat bones) and simmer on low heat for about 40 minutes. You can serve the strained broth as a first course and the vegetables and stuffed squash as a second course.
# Serve hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* For the pot roasting method, you may set the squash on a bed of chopped onion and drizzle with a little olive oil and tomato paste.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Cuisine of India]]

'''Puttu''' is a [[Cookbook:breakfast|breakfast]] dish in Kerala, India. The main ingredients are rice [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] and coconut. It is usually eaten with [[Cookbook:Steaming|steamed]] bananas or [[Cookbook:Cholley|Kadala Curry]] ([[Cookbook:Chickpea|chickpea]] curry), [[Cookbook:Chicken Curry|Chicken Curry]], or [[Cookbook:Boil|boiled]] green gram ([[Cookbook:Mung Bean|moong]]) and pappad.
== Ingredients==
* 1 medium-sized [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]]
* 4 cups puttu powder ([[Cookbook:Rice Flour|rice flour]])
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook: Water|Water]] (enough to moisten the flour)

== Procedure == 

#[[Cookbook:Grating|Grate]] the coconut flesh finely.
#Mix the puttu powder and salt in a wide bowl. Add half of the grated coconut.
#Rub the mixture with your fingertips, sprinkling in water until it is moist and develops a coarse texture.
#Leave the mixture for an hour if the flour is ready made, as it absorbs more water.
#Check the consistency of the flour. One should be able to make a ball out of the flour that can be easily crumbled. Adjust the water content accordingly.
#Spread a little coconut over the bottom of the puttu vessel (''puttu kutti''), and fill it with the moist flour. Layer it with coconut.
#Steam it on the puttu vessel or on the pressure cooker nozzle. In a few minutes, steam will start escaping through the top of the puttu vessel. It will be done in 4 minutes.
#Serve hot with kadala curry, boiled green gram and pappad (payarum pappadavum), or with steamed bananas.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* [[Cookbook:Rice|Rice]], [[Cookbook:wheat|wheat]], [[Cookbook:corn|corn]], ragi, or [[Cookbook:tapioca|tapioca]] flours can all be used to make puttu.

{{Recipe}}

'''Radish stew''' dates back to at least the 4th century when a recipe appeared in the Roman cookery book Cnecht. It is a simple and inexpensive dish, and is said to calm an upset stomach.

==Ingredients==
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] [[Cookbook:Radish|red radish]], cut in 1-inch strips, or about 5–6 [[Cookbook:Slicing|slices]]
* 1 large [[Cookbook:onion|onion]], cut in 1-inch chunks
* 4–6 [[Cookbook:green onion|green onion]]s, [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:flour|flour]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaves]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] dried leaf [[Cookbook:thyme|thyme]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] dry [[Cookbook:Wine|white wine]]
* 3 pounds non-red [[Cookbook:Radish|radish]], cut in 1-inch chunks (red, yellow, or variety)
* 3 cups [[Cookbook:Chicken Broth|chicken broth]]
* ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:pepper#black pepper|pepper]]
* Sweet ground [[Cookbook:paprika|paprika]] (optional)

==Procedure==
#In a large [[Cookbook:saucepan|saucepan]] or [[Cookbook:Dutch oven|Dutch oven]], cook the radish until crisp. 
#Add onions and cook until they soften somewhat, about 4–5 minutes.
#Sprinkle flour over the onions, add bay leaves and thyme, and increase the heat to high.
#Pour in wine and stir to loosen brown bits from the bottom of the pan. Cook for about 2 minutes, or until wine has evaporated.
#Add non-red radishes, broth, and pepper. Cover and bring to a [[Cookbook:boil|boil]]. 
#Reduce heat to medium low and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] until radishes are tender, about 45–60 minutes. 
#Sprinkle with paprika, if desired. Taste and adjust seasonings. 
#Remove bay leaves before serving.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] | [[Cookbook:Holiday Recipes|Holiday]]

'''Pumpkin roll''' is a traditional holiday [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]] that's lovely to serve. The filling keeps the cake moist. This dessert can be prepared and kept frozen before the holidays.

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (220 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 7.8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*3 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], beaten
*⅔ cup (80 g / 2.8 oz) canned [[Cookbook:Pumpkin|pumpkin]]
*¾ cup (110 g / 3.9 oz) [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]]
*¾ cup (75 g / 2.6 oz) [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Pecan|pecans]]
*1 package (8 oz / 230 g) [[Cookbook:Cream Cheese|cream cheese]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*1 cup (125 g / 4.4 oz) [[Cookbook:Powdered Sugar|powdered sugar]]

==Procedure==

=== Cake ===
#Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to {{convert|375|F|C}}.
#Mix sugar, eggs, and canned pumpkin in a large bowl until well blended.
#Using a second bowl, mix flour, salt, cinnamon, and baking soda.
#[[Cookbook:Folding|Fold]] dry mixture into larger bowl with pumpkin mixture.
#Line rectangular [[Cookbook:Cookie Sheet|cookie sheet]] with greased parchment paper or waxed paper. Make sure to extend over the sides of the cookie sheet.
#Pour batter evenly onto the lined cookie sheet.
#Sprinkle batter with the chopped pecans.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at {{convert|375|F|C}} for 15 minutes.

=== Filling ===
#Set aside ⅛ cup (15 g / 0.53 oz) of the powdered sugar; it will be used later.
#[[Cookbook:Whipping|Whip]] cream cheese, vanilla, butter, and remaining powdered sugar until smooth.
#Set aside.

=== Assembly ===
#Lay a clean dish towel on a flat kitchen surface.
#Evenly sprinkle towel with the powdered sugar that was set aside earlier.
#Once the cake has been completely baked and before cooled, flip onto the towel with the powdered sugar.
#Loosely roll cake, then cool completely to allow cake to set.
#Once cooled, unroll cake.
#Spread filling over cake.
#Roll cake and filling up in a spiral.
#Wrap in [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|foil]] or [[Cookbook:Plastic wrap|plastic wrap]] and freeze.
#Once frozen, remove foil and cut into slices while still frozen.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Any chopped nuts may be substituted for the pecans.

{{Recipe}}

'''Jangjorim''' is Korean dish consisting mainly of boiled or braised beef and soy sauce. This version uses quail eggs.

== Ingredients ==

* [[Cookbook:Quail|Quail]] [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] water
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* ¼ cup refined rice [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]
* 6 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* 3 slices of fresh [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
* 3 dried red [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile peppers]]

== Procedure ==

# Bring a pot of water to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. Add the quail eggs, and boil for about 10 minutes.
# Carefully drain the eggs, and cool in cold water.
# Peel the cooled eggs.
# Combine the water, soy sauce, sugar, wine, garlic, and ginger in a saucepan. Bring to a boil.
# Add the eggs to the pot, and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] until the liquid is reduced by half.
# Add the peppers, and cook just for 1–2 minutes.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Adding 1 tablespoon each of salt and vinegar to the boiling water makes the eggs easier to peel.
* Don't overcook after adding the chili pepper—it will get too soft.

{{recipesummary|category=Recipes for dessert|servings=48|time=2 hours|difficulty=4}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Desserts]]
==Ingredients==

=== Cake ===
*675 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (1.49 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] / 5½ sticks) unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], plus extra for greasing
*675 g (1.49 lb / 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]]) superfine [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tbsp|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla extract]]
*12 medium or 10 large (about 500 g) [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
*675 g (1.49 lb / 5 cups) [[Cookbook:Self-rising Flour|self-raising flour]]
*1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] each of red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple [[Cookbook:Food Coloring|food colourings]]
===Icing===
*500 g (1.1 lb / 4 sticks) unsalted butter
*1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] (2.2 lb / 8 cups) [[Cookbook:Powdered Sugar|powdered sugar]]
*3 tbsp [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
*1 tbsp vanilla extract
*[[Cookbook:Sprinkles|Sprinkles]] (eg. hundreds and thousands) (optional)
==Procedure==

====== Make cake ======
#Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to {{Convert|190|C|F}}. Grease and [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|line]] six {{Convert|20|cm|in|abbr=on|adj=on}} round [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|cake tins]].
#[[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] the butter, sugar and vanilla in a large mixing bowl, until soft and fluffy.
#Beat in the eggs, two at a time.
#Combine the flour and baking powder. [[Cookbook:Folding|Fold]] this dry mixture into the batter.
#Divide the mixture into 6 separate bowls.
#Add the red food colouring, one drop at a time, to the mixture in one bowl and stir in until the mixture reached the desired colour.
#Repeat step 6, using orange, yellow, green, blue and purple food colourings.
#Spread the red mixture in one of cake tin. Repeat with other colours.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 25 minutes, in batches of two cakes, until a [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewer]] inserted comes out clean.
#Transfer the cakes to a [[Cookbook:Cooling Rack|wire rack]] and leave to cool. Unmold cakes.

====== Make icing ======
#For the icing, beat the butter in a mixing bowl until soft.
#Add half of the icing sugar, 1 cup at a time, and beat in.
#Beat in the milk and vanilla extract.
#Add the rest of icing sugar, 1 cup at a time, and beat in.

====== Assemble cake ======
#Spread one-eighth of the icing onto the purple cake. Top with blue cake layer, and press gently.
#Repeat the frosting and cake layering in rainbow order, finishing with the red layer.
#Spread the rest of icing all over the cake.
#If you like, sprinkle the cake with sprinkles.
#Enjoy!

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Gel food coloring is better than dilute liquid coloring. Using more concentrated coloring will result in more vibrant colors.
* Mixing the food coloring into the cake batter after the flour is added can make the cake tough due to the additional stirring needed. Be careful to only mix as much as necessary.

{{Recipe}}

When really pressed for time, the following recipe will produce a reasonable semblance of '''''risotto''''' within ten minutes.

== Ingredients ==

* [[Cookbook:Stock|Stock]]
* [[Cookbook:Butter|Butter]]
* Arborio or other risotto [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
* Seasonings, as desired

== Procedure ==
# Place a pot over strong heat and pour in the stock to [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. You will need twice as much stock as the rice to be cooked (e.g. 2 cups of stock for 1 cup of dry rice).
# Place a second pot over strong heat and drop in some butter.
# Once the butter in the first pot has melted, pour in the rice and start [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sautéing]] it, stirring continuously with a wooden spoon. The butter will soon start to froth. Extra seasonings can also be added at this point.
# By this time, the stock will have started boiling. Pour it into the pot with the rice (caution: this produces hot steam suddenly), stir well to make sure that no rice has stuck on the inside of the pot, cover the pot, and switch off the heat.
# Leave alone for 5–7 minutes, then serve.

'''Flaky pastry''' is also known as "Quick Puff Pastry".

== Ingredients ==
* 460 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], divided into four equal portions
* 460 g [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* '''Cold''' water (enough to form a dough)

== Procedure ==
# [[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] the flour into a bowl.
# Cut one portion of butter into the flour until it becomes crumbly.
# Add cold water, as needed, to make a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# Lightly dust kneading board and [[Cookbook:Rolling Pin|rolling pin]] with flour. [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll]] dough until it is approximately 0.5 cm thick.
# Cut (smear) another portion of butter into the pastry. Fold pastry into quarters. Roll pastry back to 0.5 cm thickness. Repeat this step until there is no butter left.
# Draw a sheet of [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|plastic food wrap]] large enough to cover one side of the flattened pastry. Invert the kneading board.
# Cover the other side with another sheet of plastic food wrap. Gently roll the pastry into a cylindrical shape.
# Store in refrigerator until needed for use. Keeps well for a week or 6 months in freezer.

{{Recipe summary
| Category = Beverage recipes
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{Recipe}}

This recipe is quicker than [[Cookbook:Traditional Finnish Lemon Mead (Sima)|traditional sima]], optimized for simplicity and short preparation time, makes it easier to try making sima: the only equipment needed are a 3 litre open container (a saucepan or small bucket perhaps), a 2 litre soda bottle and a funnel. The result is still undoubtably sima.

Making 2 litres at a time is very fast and a good way to practice without fear of losing a large batch to an error. On the first day it takes only about as long as it takes for the water to boil, and on the second day the bottling can be done in five minutes. Making a new small batch every 2–3 days lets you drink fresh sima daily without worrying about it spoiling, and takes hardly any time at all.

== Ingredients ==
* 250 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]], juiced
* Small amount of dry [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]]
* [[Cookbook:Raisin|Raisins]] (optional)

== Procedure ==

=== First day ===
# [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] 1–2 litres water.
# While the water is boiling, wash a 3-liter container and squeeze the juice from the lemon into a glass.
# Set aside 1 litre of hot water for the sima. Rinse the container with the rest to sterilize it.
# Put sugar and lemon juice into the container.
# Pour 1 litre hot water onto the sugar and lemon juice and mix until sugar dissolves.
# Add 1 litre cold water.
# Add a very small amount of yeast (up to ¼ teaspoon).
# Let it stand overnight.

=== Second day ===
# Wash a 2 litre soda bottle and rinse it with boiling water.
# Add 1 teaspoon sugar into the bottle and a few raisins if you want to.
# Pour the sima into the bottle with a [[Cookbook:Funnel|funnel]].
# Leave in a dark place in room temperature for 2 days.
# Move the bottle into the refrigerator; the sima is ready.

[[Category:Recipes using brown sugar]]

{{recipesummary|category=Beef recipes|servings=6|time=45 minutes|difficulty=2}}{{Recipe}}

This meal takes roughly 45 minutes to make and yields great left-overs.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 packages (around 1.5–2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] / 750–1000 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) bite-size [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]]
* 1 can (8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] / 250 g) [[Cookbook:Mushroom Soup|cream of mushroom soup]]
* ½ can (4 oz / 125 ml) [[Cookbook:Broth|beef broth]]
* 1 tub (8 oz / 250 g) [[Cookbook:Sour cream|sour cream]]
* 1 bag (16 oz / 500 g) [[Cookbook:Egg noodles|egg noodles]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]] to taste

== Procedure ==
# Cook egg noodles in a large pot according to directions.
# While egg noodles cook, season the beef with salt and pepper and [[Cookbook:Brown|brown]] the meat in a [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]] unless it is already cooked. Low and slow makes a tender product. If meat is already cooked, heat the meat in the [[Cookbook:Microwave Oven|microwave]] or in a skillet.
# Drain egg noodles.
# Mix cream of mushroom soup, beef broth, and sour cream in the pot used for the egg noodles. Season the sauce with salt and pepper keeping in mind that many of the ingredients contain plenty of salt.
# Add noodle mixture with beef and serve.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Pre-cut stew meat is preferred for the beef. Left-over steaks cut into pieces work well. Ground beef browned in a skillet can also work if you have it around.

This recipe for '''pumpkin soufflé casserole''' is adapted from [https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/239216/pumpkin-casserolesouffle/ one posted on Allrecipes].

== Ingredients ==

* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] white [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* ½ cup unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], softened
* 3 large [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 1½ cups [[Cookbook:Pumpkin|pumpkin]] purée
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Cake Flour|cake flour]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]], or more to taste

== Special equipment ==

* [[Cookbook: Oven|Oven]]
* [[Cookbook:Mixer|Electric mixer]]
* 9-inch square [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|baking dish]]

== Procedure ==

# Preheat the oven to 450 °F (230 °C), and grease the baking dish.
# Use the electric mixer to [[Cookbook:Beat|beat]] together sugar, butter, and eggs until smooth and creamy. 
# Mix in pumpkin purée until well combined. 
# Add milk, cake flour, and baking powder, and mix until smooth.
# Pour mixture into the prepared baking dish, and sprinkle cinnamon over top.
# Bake in the heated oven until it is set in the middle, 45 minutes or more.

{{Recipe summary
| Yield = 9x2-inch quiche; 8 big slices
| Difficulty = 4
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of France|Cuisine of France]]

This is a tall fluffy custard quiche as served at Thomas Keller's restaurant, Bouchon. This version is brief and slightly modified with less filling and more custard; you can find the full version in Keller's ''Bouchon'' cookbook.

==Ingredients==
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] belly, skinned and cut into lardons 1½ x ⅜ inches
* 1½ [[Cookbook:cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Onion_Confit|onion confit]]
* ¾ [[Cookbook:tsp|tsp]] kosher [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:tsp|tsp]] fresh ground black [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:tsp|tsp]] chopped [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]]
* 1 [[Cookbook: Tall Quiche Shell|tall quiche shell]], baked as directed in a 9x2-inch [[Cookbook:Quiche Ring|quiche ring]] on parchment
* ½ [[Cookbook:cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Grater|grated]] [[Cookbook:Comté Cheese|Comté]] or [[Cookbook:Emmental Cheese|Emmentaler]] [[Cookbook:cheese|cheese]]
* 1 recipe's worth of [[Cookbook: Quiche Batter|quiche batter]]

== Equipment ==

* [[Cookbook:Oven|Oven]]
* 1 ea. [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheet]] at least 9 inches across
* [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|Paper towels]]
* Measuring [[Cookbook:Measuring Cup|cups]] and [[Cookbook:Measuring Spoons|spoons]]
* [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|Frying pan]], 9 inches or larger

==Procedure==
# Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] pork belly lardons on baking sheet for 20–25 minutes. The fat should be [[Cookbook:Rendering|rendered]], but the pork should not be crisp. Drain on paper towels.
# Lower oven heat to 325°F (163°C).
# Add onion confit, pork, salt, pepper, and thyme to the frying pan over medium heat. Allow to warm up for 4 minutes. Drain on paper towels.
# Arrange ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] cheese and half the pork mixture in the bottom of the quiche shell.
# Pour half the quiche batter into the shell, and check for leaks. If the shell is leaking a tiny bit or not at all, you can continue; if it's leaking a lot, it's best to bake the mixture in a [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|casserole dish]] and serve the crust on the side.
# Sprinkle the rest of cheese evenly over the filling, then top with the remaining pork mixture.
# Add enough quiche batter to fill the rest of the crust without spilling. You may not need all of it.
# Bake the quiche for about 90 minutes, checking every so often. The quiche is done when it's browned on top and it jiggles slightly like a properly set custard when you shake the pan. If it still looks quite liquid, it probably needs more time. If it's hard, puffed up a lot, and doesn't really jiggle, it might be overbaked. Adjust the time and temperature accordingly for your oven.
# Cool completely at room temperature, then chill in the fridge at least overnight and up to 3 days.
# Cut the excess crust off the top of the quiche ring, then run a paring knife carefully between the ring and the crust to separate them. Remove the ring, then slice the quiche. Serve at room temperature or warm up for 15 minutes at 350–375°F.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* You may have extra quiche batter, and you have a few options here. The first is to check the quiche after about 10–15 minutes of baking to see if you can fit any more of the quiche batter on top. If not, you  can always bake the extra in a little ramekin and have it with leftover crust pieces.

This quiche batter is used in tall fluffy custardy quiches like [[Cookbook:Quiche_Lorraine|Quiche Lorraine]].

==Ingredients==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* 2 cups [[Cookbook:Heavy_Cream|heavy cream]]
* 6 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tbsp|tbsp]] kosher [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Tsp|tsp]] fresh ground white [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
* 10 gratings of [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]], or to taste

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Blender|Blender]]
* [[Cookbook: Measuring Cup|Measuring cups]] and [[Cookbook: Cooking Spoon|spoons]]
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] (or bigger) [[Cookbook: Saucepan|saucepan]] 

==Procedure==
# Combine the milk and cream in the saucepan over medium heat. Cook until scalded and a skin forms, then remove from the heat and let cool slightly.
# Combine the eggs, salt, nutmeg, and pepper in the blender. 
# With the blender running, drizzle in the milk mixture, and keep blending on high speed for 1 minute.
# Use immediately as directed in your quiche recipe, or set aside for later.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* If the total batter volume is too large to fit in the blender, you may need to work in batches, dividing the quantities evenly to scale. Alternatively, you can blend in as much of the milk as will fit, then whisk in the remaining milk in a larger receptacle.
* If setting the batter aside to use later, make sure to blend it for about 30 seconds before using in order to aerate it.

{{Recipe summary
| Category = Fermented recipes
| Difficulty = 1
}}

{{recipe}}

This is a quick way to start a sourdough starter and is particularly useful for [[Cookbook:Amish Friendship Bread|Amish friendship bread]]. Instead of relying on the wild yeast and bacteria that are naturally present in the air, it swaps in a commercial yeast. Because the commercial strains are very vigorous, it is unlikely that wild yeast will supplant them.

This makes enough for two starters, so you can use it all yourself, or you can share it with a friend.

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* 1 small package (0.25 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] / 7 [[Cookbook:Gram|grams]]) instant dry [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]] 

==Equipment==

* A bowl or other container, at least 1 quart (1 liter) in size. It should be made of a non-reactive material, such as plastic, glass, or stainless steel (but not copper, cast iron, etc.)
* Spoon or [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] for stirring
* Lid or plate to cover the bowl

==Procedure==
# Mix all ingredients in a bowl until smooth.
# Cover the bowl and place in a warm place (~70–80 °F / 20–27 °C). It should begin making some small bubbles within an hour or two (the timing depends mainly on how cold the milk is).
# Proceed as directed for "Day 1" of your sourdough recipe.

== Maintenance ==
Sourdough starters are flexible and difficult to kill. As long as they get oxygen, flour, and liquid on a regular basis, they are likely to thrive. Below is a low-hassle schedule for maintaining a starter with rich ingredients (i.e., using milk and sugar instead of water). Other schedules feed the starter each day, or even twice a day, but they add smaller amounts each time. Especially for bread baking, some schedules feed the starter at night and then mix the bread dough early in the morning (first reserving the amount needed to continue the cycle, usually one cup/250 mL), so that the dough will benefit from a fully risen starter at peak activity. For a slower schedule, put the starter in the refrigerator; stir it most days, but feed it half as much. To take a break for multiple weeks or months, put it in the freezer. When you thaw it out (perhaps overnight in the refrigerator), it's day 1 again.

This schedule is a one-week plan, but some bakeries have shorter cycles, and other people prefer a long cycle. This is accomplished mainly by changing the amount of food and liquid added each time. As long as you feed it before baking, it is possible to use this starter on any day of the week. If you need to bake a cake on a different day, you can declare today an honorary baking day, and proceed as if it were Day 7. The day after you bake is always Day 1 in your new cycle.

If you are not planning to bake [[Cookbook:Amish Friendship Bread|Amish friendship bread]] (which is a sweet cake), you may reduce or completely omit the sugar from this schedule.

* Day 1: Mix the starter as above (or, if you already have starter, or someone gave you a starter, stir the starter well) and put it in a warm place.
* Day 2: Stir the starter well.
* Day 3: Stir the starter well.
* Day 4: Feed the starter by adding 1 cup each of flour, sugar, and milk. Stir until smooth.
* Day 5: Stir the starter well.
* Day 6: Stir the starter well.
* Day 7: Baking day! First feed the starter by adding 1 cup each of flour, sugar and milk. Stir until smooth. Then set aside the amount of starter you want to keep for next week's cycle (usually 1 cup). Use the rest to make Amish Friendship Bread or other baked goods.
If the starter is in a plastic zip-type bag, open the bag every time you stir it to let out any excess gas and get fresh air in. You don't want gas to build up in the bag, because it might pop open and make a mess. Flexible bags can be "stirred" by just mashing the bag, but make sure they get fresh air each time.

If a brown liquid (called "hooch") pools on the surface, the starter is still alive and edible. It's a sign of active yeast fermentation with too little oxygen and too little food. However, that liquid will separate out every time you let the starter sit, and if a large amount forms, it may affect the flavor of your cake. Just pour that thin liquid away, and consider stirring the starter more often, reducing the amount of sugar you feed it, or feeding smaller amounts more frequently (e.g., ½ cup flour, ½ cup milk, and ¼ cup sugar once a day for a few days).

This schedule can be adjusted to suit your needs. You can slow down the starter's cycle by storing it in the refrigerator instead of in a warm place. In the refrigerator, stir occasionally and feed the starter at least once a week (more often if liquid "hooch" forms on the surface). You can also freeze the starter for many months.  When you are ready to use it again, thaw in the refrigerator overnight, and then feed it the next day to restart your cycle on Day 1.

== Safety ==

* Always keep sourdough starters and raw yeast dough away from pets.  Eating living, growing yeast can cause vomiting, diarrhea, and other digestive problems in dogs and cats.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of France#Provence|Provençale recipes]] | [[Cookbook:Vegan cuisine|Vegan Cuisine]]

'''Ratatouille''' is a traditional [[Cookbook:Cuisine_of_France#Provence|Provençale]] stewed vegetable dish that can be served as a meal on its own, accompanied by [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]], [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]] or French [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]], or as a side dish. It can be served hot or cold.

==Ingredients==
* [[Cookbook:Olive oil|Olive oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
* 1 clove [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], or to taste
* 1 [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplant (aubergine)]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]] (green, red, yellow or a combination)
* 2 [[Cookbook:Zucchini|zucchini (courgettes)]]
* 6 medium [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]]es, ripe (juicy), peeled and seeded
* [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] and [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Herbes de Provence|Herbes de Provence]] to taste or 1 small bunch [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]] (optional), [[Cookbook:Chiffonade|chiffoned]]

==Procedure==

#Put a large [[Cookbook:Pots_and_Pans#Enameled_Cast_Iron|casserole]] on the stove on medium heat.
#When the casserole is hot, add enough olive oil to just cover the bottom.
#Cut the zucchini and eggplant into ½ inch slices. Then, cut these into rectangles of about 3x1 inches. Add to the casserole.
#[[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] the slices until light brown; remove from pan and set aside temporarily.
#[[Cookbook:Chop|Chop]] the onions and garlic. Cut the green pepper into strips or dice, as preferred.
#Add some additional oil if needed, and cook the onions and peppers  slowly for about 10 minutes until tender but not brown. Stir in the garlic.
#Peel and seed the tomatoes. [[Cookbook:Dice|Dice]] them or cut them into quarters, add to the casserole. Add some salt to bring out their juices. Cover and lower the heat.
#Five minutes later, check to see if the tomatoes have made enough juice to almost cover the vegetables—if so, perfect; if not, add water as needed (not too much).
#Add salt, pepper and Herbes de Provence to taste. In general, 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] of salt, ½ tsp of pepper, and 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] of the herbs will suffice. 
#Add the zucchini and eggplant back and blend gently with the tomato-onion-pepper mixture. Cover the casserole and let [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] on low heat until the vegetables are tender but still intact, 10–20 minutes, or to taste.
#Remove the lid, raise the heat a little and cook uncovered for another 15 minutes, [[Cookbook:Basting|basting]] frequently until the liquids have mostly evaporated, leaving a small amount of juice and olive oil.
==Notes, tips, and variations==

* Increase quantities to serve more, and add different vegetables as desired for variation.
* When ratatouille is used as a filling for savoury [[Cookbook:Crêpe|crêpes]] or to fill an omelette, the vegetables are sometimes cut into smaller pieces.
* While most recipes do not brown the onions, if you like them browned, brown them. Food traditions have always been subject to individual interpretation.
* N.B. It is important that each of the vegetables retain its own shape and character. Most authorities agree that ratatouille should not be a mush. Avoid overcooking. Sautéing the eggplant and courgettes initially helps retain their shape and improves their flavour, but is optional. Of course, if you personally prefer a more homogeneous dish, it may be cooked for 45 minutes to 1 hour, but this is unusual.

'''Rice an' peas''' is a traditional [[Cookbook:Caribbean cuisines|Caribbean]] dish, done easy in a [[Cookbook:Rice Cooker|rice cooker]], great for your ital-eating Rastafarian or vegan friends. There's lots of ways to cook rice an' peas, but this one is easy and hassle free.   

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Bean|bean]]s ([[Cookbook:Kidney Bean|kidney beans]], [[Cookbook:Black Bean|black beans]], [[Cookbook:Pinto Bean|pinto beans]]) (also known as "peas"), dried or canned
*1 cup [[Cookbook:Rice|brown rice]]
*1 cup [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut milk]]
*1 cup water

==Procedure==
#If using dried beans, cover them in water and [[Cookbook:Soaking Beans|soak]] for at least 8 hours.
#Drain and rinse the beans (even canned beans) prior to use.
#If using dried red kidney beans, [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] briskly for 20 minutes, then drain again.
#Add rice, beans, water, and coconut milk to a [[Cookbook:Rice Cooker|rice cooker]]. If using a programmable cooker, set to cook for brown rice. For an on/off cooker, turn it on.
#In about 30 minutes your rice cooker will finish cooking the rice. Open, stir, and serve.

== Warnings ==

* It is important to soak and pre-cook dried kidney beans. Dried kidney beans will cause nausea, vomiting and diarrhea unless they have been boiled briskly for at least twenty minutes to destroy the very indigestible phytohaemagglutinin that they contain—a slow cooker is not enough and can even make things worse. They will then need another 60–90 minutes at a slow simmer to become tender. Tinned kidney beans are quite safe and do not need pre-cooking as their preparation involves sufficient heat to destroy the toxin.

}}Extremely simple to cook, '''mejadra''' is a fundamental component of Middle Eastern cuisine. It provides carbohydrates, proteins, and a full stomach. It also tastes great. The most common recipe uses rice. Bulgur can be substituted for rice, using the exact same procedure. When cooked with rice, this recipe is [[Cookbook:Gluten-Free|gluten-free]]. It isn't gluten free when cooked with bulgur (wheat).

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (100 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 3.5 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) dry [[Cookbook:Lentil|lentils]]
* [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Baharat|Baharat]]
* [[Cookbook:Cumin|Cumin]]
* [[Cookbook:Cardamom|Ground cardamom]]
* 4 cups (1 [[Cookbook:Liter|L]] / 1.1 [[Cookbook:Quart|qt]]) water, divided
* 1 cup (80 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 2.8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) uncooked [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] or [[Cookbook:Bulgur|bulgur]]
* Ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
* 1 medium sized [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]

== Procedure==
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] the lentils in oil for 3–4 minutes, stirring continuously, until the first beans show signs of scorching.
# Add salt, baharat, cumin, and ground cardamom to taste.
# Add 2 cups water and cover. Bring to a boil, lower to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]]. Cook for 20 minutes or until all the water is absorbed by the lentils.
# Fry the rice in oil for 3–4 minutes, stirring continuously, until the grains change colour.
# Add salt, black or white pepper, and ground cardamom.
# Add 2 cups water and cover. Bring to a boil, lower to a simmer. After 5 minutes turn the heat off, and leave standing for another 10 minutes.
# Cut the onion into thin strips (about 0.5x4 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] / 0.2x1.6 [[Cookbook:Inch|in]]).
# Fry the onion in olive oil until crisp and deeply golden brown (this may take a while but will result in much fuller flavor).
# Mix the lentils and rice, and top with the fried onion. Use 2 parts lentils to 1 part rice for a moist consistency.

== Procedure ==
#[[File:Lentil soup done.jpg|thumb|Finished lentil soup, with potatoes, parsley, and dill added|308x308px]]Pick over the lentils to remove any debris if needed. Rinse well.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Tex-Mex cuisine|Tex-Mex cuisine]]

Dried red chiles can be soaked and [[Cookbook:Puree|pureed]] to make '''red chile sauce'''. It can be used in many ways, including as an [[Cookbook:Enchilada|enchilada]] sauce, [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] [[Cookbook:Marinade|marinade]], or in [[Cookbook:Huevos Rancheros|huevos rancheros]].

== Ingredients ==
* 3 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (90 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) dried [[Cookbook:Chile Pepper|chile peppers]], such as New Mexico chile
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (500 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) hot water (boiled water that has cooled a little)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] (15 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 3 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] (5 ml) ground [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]]
* 1 tablespoon (15 ml) Mexican [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]]

== Procedure ==

# Wipe chile peppers with a damp cloth to clean. See [[Cookbook:Red Chile Sauce#Warning|warning]] for handling instructions.
# Break off stems, and remove seeds.
# Soak chili peppers in hot water until softened, about an hour.
# Taste the soaking water. If it is bitter, replace it with fresh water.
# [[Cookbook:Puréeing|Purée]] chili pepper and water mixture in a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]]
# Heat the oil in a pan, add onion, garlic, and seasonings.
# Once the onions are cooked, add the chili purée to the pan. [[Cookbook:Simmer|Simmer]] for 15 minutes.
# Return mixture to the blender, and purée. See [[Cookbook:Red Chile Sauce#Warning|warning]].
# Pour sauce through a [[Cookbook:Sieve|sieve]]. Use a spoon to stir and press the mixture against the sieve to extract all the sauce.
# Add salt to taste. If the sauce is a little bitter, some sugar can be added to compensate.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* This sauce freezes well.
* The sauce may stain certain materials, including some plastics. Store in glass to avoid staining.

== Warnings ==

* Use caution when handling [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|chili peppers]]. Wearing rubber gloves is recommended, and be sure to wash the gloves, and your hands, thoroughly after handling the chili peppers. If rubber gloves are not available, rub some oil onto your hands before handling the chilies. The capsaicin in the chili peppers, the chemical that makes them hot, will burn the eyes, nose, or mouth on contact, and exposed skin if left for long.
* Use caution when pureeing hot liquids in a blender. The hot liquid can spill out the top of the blender. Either allow the sauce to cool first, or hold the lid in place during blending, using a towel or oven glove to protect your hand. Only fill the blender half full, do multiple batches if required.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|Cuisine of the United States]] | [[Cookbook:Sandwiches|Sandwiches]]

'''Red Devils''' are hot, open faced sandwiches. They are a great dinner or lunch. They include all the major food groups and taste great. Their ease of preparation makes them suitable for people on the move and the recipe can easily be scaled up or down for family or guests.

==Ingredients==
*[[Cookbook:Bread|Bread]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
*[[Cookbook:Processed Cheese|American cheese]], sliced
*[[Cookbook:Tomato|Tomato]], sliced
*[[Cookbook:Onion|Onion]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
*[[Cookbook:Bacon|Bacon]]

==Procedure==
#Place bacon in a [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|sheet pan]].
#Set the [[Cookbook:Broiler|broiler]] to 'low'.
#Pre-cook the bacon under the broiler until it is about halfway done.
#While bacon cooks, place white bread on a sheet, one slice per diner.
#Place a slice of American cheese on each slice of bread.
#Place the tomato slices on each sandwich
#Sprinkle a small amount of onion onto each sandwich.
#Place a strip of half-cooked bacon on each sandwich.
#Place the cookie sheet under broiler, set to maximum temperature, and broil for approximately 3–4 minutes. You must check on them often to prevent burning.
#Remove once the bread is toasted, the cheese is golden at the edges, and the bacon is fully cooked.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* Often it may be easier to eat with utensils instead of by hand.
* The bacon is usually too long to fit on the sandwich so cut it in half. One strip of bacon is usually used per sandwich so it will have 2 halves on it when finished.
* Precooking the bacon may be accomplished while preparing the rest of the food. It is best to cook until between rare and crisp.
* Red devils usually require one tomato per sheet of sandwiches but may vary depending upon the size of your sheets or the size of your tomato slices.
* A whole onion is not needed for a tray of Red Devils. A small sprinkling of diced onions is sufficient. Sweet onions or red onions are a good substitution for normal white "storage" onions.
* As always, you can experiment or change things according to your tastes.

==Warnings==

* It is very important to check on the Red Devils once they are in the oven. They can quickly change from being undercooked to overcooked within a few seconds. The goal is to quickly cook the bacon and toast the bread and cheese without making the sandwich too hot to eat soon after being finished.

'''Raita''' is an [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian]] [[Cookbook:Garnish|garnish]] often served with spiced dishes. It acts as a cooling flavour as the fat in the yogurt dissolves and mollifies [[Cookbook:Chilli|chili]] in the curry, while the taste of [[Cookbook:Cucumber|cucumber]] and fresh [[Cookbook:Mint|mint]] or other herbs refreshes the palate. 

The essential ingredient is [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yogurt]].

==Ingredients==

* ⅛ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]] cucumber (about 1 inch of cucumber)
* ½ cup plain [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yogurt]]
* 2–3 [[Cookbook:Mint|mint]] leaves, [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]] leaves, chopped
* 1–2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] finely chopped or [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] (coarse salt preferred)
* [[Cookbook:Chile|Chile]] powder
* Ground [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]]

==Procedure==

# Squeeze the grated cucumber to remove and discard excess liquid.
# Stir the cucumber into the yogurt.
# Add chopped mint, [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]], and onion.
#Add salt to taste.
# Sprinkle a little ground [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]] on top.
# Sprinkle with chili powder if desired.
# Refrigerate and serve cold.

'''Red cross fudge''' is a delicious, easy fudge that works every time and never crystallizes.

== Ingredients ==
* 4½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] / 2.2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* {{convert|0.5|lb|g}} [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 1½ cups (375 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] / 12.7 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Condensed Milk|evaporated milk]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] extract
* 2 cups (120 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 4.2 oz) miniature [[Cookbook:Marshmallow|marshmallows]]
* 12 oz (340 g) real [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate chips]]
* 2 cups (120 g / 4.2 oz) [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Walnut|walnuts]]

== Procedure ==

# Combine sugar, butter, evaporated milk, and vanilla in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] and bring to a rolling [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
# Cook on medium heat for 11 minutes, stirring constantly.
# Add marshmallows, chocolate chips, walnuts to fudge and mix well.
# Pour into a buttered pan and let cool. 
# Cut into squares when it cuts without melting back together but before it becomes crumbly. 
# Store in an air-tight container.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Substituting margarine for butter makes the fudge oily. Imitation vanilla affects the aroma.
* Other varieties of chips (vanilla, butterscotch, etc.) work as well.

Oddly enough, '''refried beans''' ''(frijoles refritos)'' are only [[Cookbook:Frying|fried]] once. The prefix "re" is a [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Spain|Spanish]] prefix meaning "very" or "well", inappropriately tacked onto a non-Spanish word.

==Ingredients==
* [[Cookbook:Pinto Bean|Pinto beans]] or [[Cookbook:Black Bean|black beans]]
* [[Cookbook:Butter|Butter]] (optional) or home-[[Cookbook:Rendering|rendered]] [[Cookbook:Lard|lard]] (optional)

==Procedure==
#If using dried beans, wash them then cover with water in a medium pot and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] according to the package directions. You may add [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]] halves or a [[Cookbook:Ham|ham]] bone, which you can remove at the end.[[Image:BeansHamPot.jpg|thumb|339x339px|Cooked [[Cookbook:Bean|Beans]] and [[Cookbook:Ham|ham]] bone]]
#If using canned beans, rinse them briefly before use.
#Smash the beans, perhaps with a potato [[Cookbook:Potato Masher|masher]].
#Add home-rendered lard or butter, totaling up to 20% of the total (25% of the amount prior to adding). You may also use a substantially smaller amount of some other oil or omit it entirely.
#Fry the beans, stirring and turning them until they thicken to the degree you desire, which can be anywhere from soupy to parched.

==Use==
*[[Cookbook:Burrito|Burrito]]
*[[Cookbook:Pupusa|Pupusa]]

==Ingredients==
*1 large (~2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lbs]] / 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]]) whole [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]], cleaned 
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
*2 cups uncooked [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] 
*1 ½ cups [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]] 
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
*[[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|Lemon juice]] 
*Water

== Procedure ==
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] fish in olive oil until well cooked. Remove the fish and allow to cool.
# Fry the chopped onions in the same oil until well browned. Meanwhile, debone the fried fish, reserving the cooked fillets to be served over the rice.
# Add the head, bones and skin of the fish to the fried onions and cook with 4 cups of water in a [[Cookbook:Pressure Cooking|pressure cooker]] for 15 minutes, or for a longer time in an open pan. 
# [[Cookbook:Straining|Strain]] the broth and [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] the rice in it using 1–4 cups of broth for each cup of rice (this will depend on the absorbency of the rice you use).
# [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] the rice on low heat so that most of the broth is absorbed. 

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Some of the broth may be flavored with a few drops of lemon and served on the side as a sauce for this dish.

'''Rice bubble cake''' is quick and easy to make. Made with crisped rice cereal, the only other ingredients are butter, sugar and honey.

==Ingredients==
*100 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (4 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*6 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*4 heaped [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]] 
*5 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] rice [[Cookbook:Breakfast Cereal|cereal]]

==Procedure==
#Add the first three ingredients to a large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] (large enough to later add the rice cereal) and melt over a medium heat
#Bring the mixture to the [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] and allow it to turn over for about 4 minutes or until the mixture starts to turn brown. Stir occasionally
#Remove from the heat and add the rice cereal. Stir well to evenly mix everything together
#Press the mixture into a lined [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|tin]] (buttered)
#Before it sets too hard, cut into even squares.
